intro.title: Introduction: Songs of Grace
paras: The Fourth Thirumurai gathers twelve garlands of songs (mālai) by Ramalinga Adigal, Vallalar. Eight are sung to the Lord who dances in the golden hall of Chidambaram, with Sivakama Valli at his side. Four honour the saints whose Tamil songs went before him: Sambandar, Appar, Sundarar and Manikkavasagar.

Their heart is the Garland of the Light of Grace, the Arutprakasa Malai, a hundred verses long. In it Vallalar says one thing again and again, plainly: the Lord walked through the night to the place where he stayed, had the door opened, called him, and placed a gift in his hand. He does not claim he deserved it. Grace came to him unearned, and he never stops wondering at it.

The other garlands follow that wonder through love, bliss, devotion, beauty and astonishment, and through a long plea for forgiveness. Vallalar tells how he was taught from within, without books, and kept from the religious paths he calls full of faults, to walk the one universal path of grace. He says the Lord is beyond the reach of those who murder any living being. Jeevakarunyam, compassion for every life, is the door; and ArutPerunJothi, the Light of Grace, is real and open to all.
Each verse is given in four layers: the original Tamil, an ISO 15919 transliteration, a translation and a short commentary. A glossary explains the Tamil terms.

works.title: Songs of Grace
works.translit: BOOK IV - Thiru Arutpa - Naangaam Thirumurai

translit: aṟputappoṉ ampalattē ākiṉṟa aracē āramutē aṭiyēṉṟaṉ aṉpē-eṉ aṟivē kaṟputavu peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭalē-eṉ kaṇṇē kaṇṇutalē āṉantak kaḷippēmeyk katiyē veṟputavu pacuṅkoṭiyai maruvuperun taruvē vēta-ā kamamuṭiyiṉ viḷaṅkumoḷi viḷakkē poṟpuṟavē ivvulakil poruntucittaṉ āṉēṉ poruttamum niṉtiruvaruḷiṉ poruttamatu tāṉē.
translation: O King who manifests in the wondrous golden hall! Rare nectar, my love, my knowledge, great ocean of compassion, my eye, Lord with the eye on the forehead, joyous ecstasy, true refuge, great tree embracing the tender green vine born of the mountain, radiant lamp shining at the crown of the Vedas and Agamas. I have become an accomplished Siddha beautifully in this world. This alignment is indeed the alignment granted by your divine grace.
commentary: True spiritual attainment comes solely through divine grace, not personal effort. Vallalar declares that he has become a Siddha (an accomplished spiritual master) in this world only because the divine light aligned with him. He addresses the divine as a radiant lamp above all scriptures, showing that the ultimate truth surpasses even traditional texts like the Vedas and Agamas (ancient sacred scriptures).

translit: niṟai-aṇinta civakāmi nēyaniṟai oḷiyē nittapari pūraṇamām cuttaciva veḷiyē kaṟai-aṇinta kaḷattaracē kaṇṇuṭaiya karumpē kaṟkaṇṭē kaṉiyē-eṉ kaṇṇēkaṇ maṇiyē piṟai-aṇinta muṭimalaiyē peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭalē periyavarel lāmvaṇaṅkum periyaparam poruḷē kuṟai-aṇintu tirikiṉṟēṉ kuṟaikaḷelān tavirttē kuṟṟamelāṅ kuṇamākak koḷvatuniṉ kuṇamē.
translation: O perfectly full light of love for Sivakami adorned with perfection, pure space of Siva that is eternal absolute fullness, King with the dark-stained throat, jointed sugarcane, rock sugar, sweet fruit, my eye, pupil of my eye, mountain peak crowned with the crescent moon, great ocean of compassion, supreme reality worshipped by all the great ones. I wander bearing flaws. Relieving me of all flaws, accepting all my faults as virtues is your true nature.
commentary: The defining quality of the divine is absolute forgiveness. Addressing God as a sweet fruit and an ocean of compassion, Vallalar acknowledges his own wandering mind and human faults. He states simply that the supreme reality does not punish these flaws, choosing instead to accept and transform them into virtues.

translit: āṇpaṉaipeṇ paṉaiyākki aṅkamataṅ kaṉaiyāy ākki-aruṇ maṇattiloḷi aṉaivaraiyum ākkum māṇpaṉaimik kuvantaḷitta mākaruṇai malaiyē varuttamelān tavirtteṉakku vāḻvaḷitta vāḻvē nāṇpaṉaiyun tantaiyumeṉ naṟkuruvum āki nāyaṭiyēṉ uḷḷakattu naṇṇiyanā yakaṉē vīṇpaṉaipōṉ mikanīṇṭu viḻaṟkiṟaippēṉ eṉiṉum viruppamelām niṉaruḷiṉ viruppamaṉṟi ilaiyē.
translation: O mountain of great compassion who joyously granted the greatness of turning male palmyra trees into female, transforming bones into a beautiful maiden, and turning everyone into light at the wedding of grace! O life that dispelled all my sorrows and granted me true life! O Lord who became my friend, my father, and my good guru, approaching within the heart of this dog-like devotee! Even if I grow excessively tall like a useless palmyra tree and draw water for barren land, all my desires are nothing but the desire of your grace.
commentary: The only true desire a devotee can hold is the desire for divine grace. Vallalar recalls great miracles from Tamil devotional history, such as turning dry bones into a living girl and male trees into bearing fruit, to illustrate God's boundless power to transform reality. He confesses that even if his own life seems as useless as a barren tree, his inner heart wants nothing but what the divine wills for him.

translit: cittamaṉē kampurintu tirintuḻaluñ ciṟiyēṉ ceyvakai-oṉ ṟaṟiyātu tikaikkiṉṟēṉ antō uttamaṉē uṉṉaiyalāl orutuṇaimaṟ ṟaṟiyēṉ uṉṉāṇai uṉṉāṇai uṇmai-itu kaṇṭāy ittamaṉē yaccalaṉam iṉippoṟukka māṭṭēṉ iraṅki-aruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum itutaruṇam entāy cuttamaṉē yattavarkkum eṉaippōlu mavarkkum tuyartavippāṉ maṇimaṉṟil tulaṅkunaṭat taracē.
translation: With a mind distracted by many things, I am a lowly one wandering about. Alas, I stand bewildered, not knowing what to do. O supreme one, I know no other companion but you. Upon your oath, upon your oath, know that this is the truth. I can no longer endure this wavering of the mind. You must show mercy and grant me your grace. This is the moment, my father, O dancing King shining in the ruby hall to dispel the sorrow of pure-hearted ascetics and those like me.
commentary: The divine is the only reliable companion when the human mind is scattered and confused. Swearing a solemn oath of complete reliance, Vallalar cries out that he can no longer bear his own mental instability. He asks for immediate grace, trusting that the Lord who dances in the hall of light exists precisely to dispel the sorrows of perfected ascetics and flawed beginners alike.

translit: tuppāṭu tirumēṉic cōtimaṇic cuṭarē turiyaveḷik kuḷḷirunta cuttaciva veḷiyē appāṭu caṭaimuṭi-em āṉanta malaiyē aruṭkaṭalē kuruvē-eṉ āṇṭavaṉē aracē ippāṭu paṭa-eṉakku muṭiyātu turaiyē iraṅki-aruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum itutaruṇaṅ kaṇṭāy tappāṭu vēṉeṉiṉum eṉṉaiviṭat tuṇiyēl taṉimaṉṟuḷ naṭampuriyun tāṇmalaren tāyē.
translation: O shining ruby flame with a divine form of coral hue, pure space of Siva residing within the transcendent space, our mountain of bliss crowned with matted hair, ocean of grace, Guru, my ruler, my King. I can no longer bear to suffer like this, O Lord. You must show mercy and grant me your grace. See that this is the moment. Even if I commit faults, do not resolve to abandon me, O my mother whose lotus feet perform the dance in the peerless hall.
commentary: The divine loves and forgives with the protective tenderness of a mother. Describing God as a radiant flame in the highest pure space, Vallalar makes an urgent plea for relief from worldly suffering. He begs the Lord not to cast him aside for his mistakes, trusting entirely in the motherly compassion of the divine.

translit: kaṇṇōṅku nutaṟkarumpē karumpiṉiṟai amutē kaṟkaṇṭē carkkaraiyē katalinaṟuṅ kaṉiyē viṇṇōṅku viyaṉcuṭarē viyaṉcuṭarkkuṭ cuṭarē viṭaiyavaṉē caṭaiyavaṉē vētamuṭip poruḷē peṇṇōṅkum orupākam piṟaṅkuperun takaiyē perumāṉai orukaraṅkoḷ periyaperu māṉē eṇṇōṅku ciṟiyavaṉēṉ eṉṉiṉumniṉ ṉaṭiyēṉ eṉṉaiviṭat tuṇiyēlniṉ iṉṉaruḷtan taruḷē.
translation: O sugarcane with the prominent eye on your forehead, O nectar brimming within the sugarcane. O rock candy, O sugar, O fragrant plantain fruit. O vast light towering in the sky, O light within that vast light. O rider of the bull, O one with matted locks, O supreme meaning at the crown of the Vedas. O great noble one shining with a woman on one side, O great Lord holding a deer in one hand. Even though I am a lowly person filled with endless thoughts, I am your devotee. Do not resolve to abandon me. Bestow your sweet grace upon me.
commentary: The divine is both intensely sweet like nectar and overwhelmingly vast like a towering light. Vallalar uses traditional images of the god Siva, picturing him with matted locks and riding a bull, to call upon the supreme reality. He asks for grace, confessing that his own mind is restless and small, yet trusting that God will not let him go.

translit: tiruneṟicēr meyaṭiyar tiṟaṉoṉṟum aṟiyēṉ ceṟivaṟiyēṉ aṟivaṟiyēṉ ceyvakaiyai aṟiyēṉ karuneṟicērn tuḻalkiṉṟa kaṭaiyariṉuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ kaṟkiṉṟēṉ cākāta kalvinilai kāṇēṉ peruneṟicēr meyññāṉa cittinilai peṟuvāṉ pitaṟṟukiṉṟēṉ ataṟkuriya peṟṟiyilēṉ antō varuneṟiyil eṉṉaivalin tāṭkoṇṭa maṇiyē maṉṟuṭaiya peruvāḻvē vaḻaṅkukaniṉ aruḷē.
translation: I know nothing of the ways of true devotees on the holy path. I know no focus, I know no wisdom, and I do not know what actions to take. I am the lowest of the low wandering in the cycles of birth. I study, yet I do not perceive the state of deathless learning. I babble about attaining the state of true spiritual perfection on the great path, but alas, I lack the merit for it. O gem who forcefully claimed me along my way, O great life of the Hall, grant me your grace.
commentary: True spiritual knowledge is a deathless state, completely beyond ordinary learning. The speaker feels lost in the cycles of birth, lacking the focus, wisdom, and merit needed to reach this perfection. By confessing his total helplessness, he shows that human effort alone is not enough. Only the sheer force of divine grace can lift the soul.

translit: kuṉṟāta kuṇakkuṉṟē kōvāta maṇiyē kuruvē-eṉ kuṭimuḻutāṭ koṇṭacivak koḻuntē eṉṟātai yāki-eṉak kaṉṉaiyumāy niṉṟē eḻumaiyumeṉ ṟaṉai āṇṭa eṉuyiriṉ tuṇaiyē poṉṟāta poruḷēmeyp puṇṇiyattiṉ payaṉē poyyaṭiyēṉ piḻaikaḷelām poṟuttaperun takaiyē aṉṟāla niḻalamarnta aruḷiṟaiyē eḷiyēṉ ācaiyelām niṉṉaṭimēl aṉṟi-oṉṟum ilaiyē.
translation: O undiminishing mountain of virtues, O unstrung gem. O Guru, O tender shoot of Siva who claimed my entire lineage. You stand as my father and my mother. O companion of my soul who has ruled me through all seven births. O imperishable reality, O fruit of true merit. O great noble one who forgave all the faults of this false devotee. O graceful Lord who sat beneath the banyan shade on that day. All the desires of this lowly one rest entirely upon your feet, and there is nothing else.
commentary: God is the eternal companion of the soul, acting as both father and mother across every lifetime. The Lord sitting beneath the banyan shade refers to a classic image of the divine as the silent, ultimate teacher of wisdom. The devotee surrenders completely to this teacher, laying down all worldly desires and resting entirely on the certainty of God's forgiveness.

translit: pūṇāta pūṇkaḷelām pūṇṭaparam poruḷē poyyaṭiyēṉ piḻaimuḻutum poṟuttaruḷi eṉṟum kāṇāta kāṭciyelāṅ kāṭṭi-eṉak kuḷḷē karuṇainaṭam purikiṉṟa karuṇaiyai-eṉ pukalvēṉ māṇāta kuṇakkoṭiyēṉ itainiṉaikkun tōṟum maṉamuruki irukaṇṇīr vaṭikkiṉṟēṉ kaṇṭāy ēṇātaṉ eṉṉiṉumyāṉ ammaiyiṉniṉ aṭiyēṉ eṉa-aṟintēṉ aṟintapiṉṉar itayamalarn tēṉē.
translation: O supreme reality adorned with unimaginable ornaments. You graciously forgave all the faults of this false devotee, revealed all unseen sights, and perform the dance of grace within me. How can I describe such compassion? I am a cruel person lacking noble qualities. Whenever I think of this, my heart melts and tears stream from both my eyes. Even though I am worthless, I realized that I have been your devotee since ancient times. After realizing this, my heart blossomed.
commentary: The divine presence is not something far away, but a dance of grace happening right inside the person. When a devotee realizes how deeply God forgives their flaws, the natural response is to melt in tears of gratitude. Recognizing this ancient, unbreakable bond between the self and the divine causes the heart to blossom.

translit: antō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aṟivaṟiyāc ciṟiyēṉai aṟivaṟiyac ceytē intōṅku caṭaimaṇiniṉ aṭimuṭiyuṅ kāṭṭi itukāṭṭi atukāṭṭi eṉnilaiyuṅ kāṭṭic cantōṭa cittarkaḷtan taṉiccūtuṅ kāṭṭi cākāta nilaikāṭṭic cakacanilai kāṭṭi vantōṭunikarmaṉampōyk karainta iṭaṅ kāṭṭi makiḻvittāy niṉaruḷiṉ vaṇmai-evark kuḷatē.
translation: Ah, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What can I say? You made me, a lowly person devoid of wisdom, realize true knowledge. O gem with the crescent moon on your matted locks, you revealed your feet and crown. You showed me this, you showed me that, and you showed me my own true state. You revealed the unique secrets of the joyful Siddhas. You showed the deathless state and the natural state. You showed the place where the wandering mind, running like a stream, finally went and dissolved. You filled me with joy. Who else possesses the boundless generosity of your grace?
commentary: This passage captures the sheer wonder of spiritual awakening. Grace gives the soul an all-encompassing vision, revealing the secrets of the Siddhas (perfected spiritual masters) and the true nature of reality. Most importantly, it grants the deathless state, a natural perfection where the restless, wandering mind finally dissolves into deep peace and joy.

translit: aṉparuḷak kōyililē amarntaruḷum patiyē ampalattil āṭukiṉṟa āṉanta nitiyē vaṉparuḷat tēmaṟaintu vaḻaṅkumoḷi maṇiyē maṟaimuṭi-ā kamamuṭiyiṉ vayaṅkuniṟai matiyē eṉparuvaṅ kuṟiyāmal eṉṉaivalin tāṭkoṇ ṭiṉpanilai taṉai-aḷitta eṉṉaṟivuk kaṟivē muṉparuvam piṉparuvaṅ kaṇṭaruḷic ceyyum muṟaimainiṉa taruḷneṟikku moḻitalaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: O Lord who graciously sits in the temple of your devotees' hearts. O treasure of bliss dancing in the Hall. O luminous gem who hides within the hearts of the cruel while still granting light. O shining full moon at the crown of the Vedas and Agamas. Without considering my maturity, you took me by force and granted me the state of bliss. O intelligence within my intelligence. I do not know if your path of grace involves examining a person's earlier and later maturity to bestow your blessings.
commentary: God grants his grace unconditionally, without waiting for a person to become spiritually mature. Vallalar says the divine took hold of him before he was ready, bypassing any test of his worthiness. This divine light is so generous that it shines even inside the hearts of cruel people, though they remain blind to it. It is the ultimate truth standing above the Vedas and Agamas (ancient Hindu scriptures).

translit: pālkāṭṭum oḷivaṇṇap paṭikamaṇi malaiyē pattikku nilaitaṉilē tittikkum paḻamē cēlkāṭṭum viḻikkaṭaiyāl tiruvaruḷaik kāṭṭum civakāma vallimakiḻ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē mālkāṭṭi maṟaiyāteṉ matikkumati yāki vaḻikāṭṭi vaḻaṅkukiṉṟa vakaiyataṉaik kāṭṭik kālkāṭṭik kālālē kāṇpatuvum eṉakkē kāṭṭiyaniṉ karuṇaikkuk kaimmāṟoṉ ṟilaṉē.
translation: O crystal mountain of radiant light shining like milk. O fruit that tastes sweet in the state of devotion. O Lord of the sacred dance who brings joy to Sivakama Valli, she who reveals divine grace with the corner of her carp-like eyes. Without casting illusions and hiding yourself, you became the wisdom of my wisdom. You showed me the path and the way you grant your grace. You showed me your feet and made me see through those very feet. I have no recompense for this compassion you have shown me.
commentary: God acts as the inner intelligence that clears away all illusion. Vallalar explains that the divine showed him the way by revealing its own sacred feet, allowing him to see the truth using that very same divine vision. He mentions Sivakama Valli (the goddess who represents divine grace) to show how this love is freely given. This sheer compassion leaves the devotee with no possible way to repay the gift.

translit: eṉṉai-oṉṟum aṟiyāta iḷampavaruvan taṉilē eṉuḷattē amarntaruḷi yāṉmayaṅkun tōṟum aṉṉai-eṉap parintaruḷi appōtaik kappō tappaṉeṉat teḷivittē aṟivuṟutti niṉṟāy niṉṉai-eṉak keṉeṉpēṉ eṉuyir eṉpēṉō nīṭiya-eṉ uyirttuṇaiyām nēyamateṉ pēṉō iṉṉalaṟut taruḷkiṉṟa eṉkuruveṉ pēṉō eṉeṉpēṉ eṉṉuṭaiya iṉpamateṉ pēṉē.
translation: In my tender youth when I knew absolutely nothing, you took your seat in my heart. Whenever I grew confused, you showered me with love like a mother. Time and again, you brought me clarity and instructed me like a father. What shall I call you? Shall I call you my life? Shall I call you the love that remains my life's enduring companion? Shall I call you my Guru who severs all suffering and bestows grace? What shall I call you? I shall call you my very own bliss.
commentary: God is the ultimate intimate companion, stepping in as mother, father, and teacher whenever the soul needs guidance. Vallalar describes how this divine presence settled in his heart when he was just a child who knew nothing. He struggles to find a single word for a love that protects like a mother, instructs like a father, and guides like a Guru (spiritual teacher). He concludes that this presence is simply his own perfect bliss.

translit: pāṭumvakai aṇuttuṇaiyum parintaṟiyāc ciṟiya paruvattē aṇintaṇintatu pāṭumvakai purintu nāṭumvakai uṭaiyōrkaḷ naṉkumatit tiṭavē nallaṟivu ciṟitaḷittup pullaṟivu pōkki nīṭumvakai caṉmārkka cuttaciva neṟiyil niṟuttiṉai-ic ciṟiyēṉai niṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ kūṭumvakai uṭaiyarelāṅ kuṟippetirpārk kiṉṟār kuṟṟamelāṅ kuṇamākak koṇṭakuṇak kuṉṟē.
translation: In my tender youth when I did not know the slightest thing about singing, you made me compose and sing verse upon verse. You made seekers of truth hold me in high esteem. You granted me a measure of good wisdom and drove away my base ignorance. You established this lowly one in the enduring pure Siva path of Sanmarkkam. What can I say of your grace? All those capable of union await your sign. O mountain of virtue who accepts all flaws as merits.
commentary: Every word of wisdom and poetry Vallalar produced was placed in him by God. He confesses that he knew nothing about singing or spiritual truth as a child. It was the divine that drove away his ignorance, made respected seekers listen to him, and placed him firmly on the path of Sanmarkkam (the path of pure truth and compassion). God is so generous that he accepts all human flaws as if they were virtues.

translit: caṟṟumaṟi villāta eṉaiyumvalin tāṇṭu tamiyēṉcey kuṟṟamelāñ cammatamāk koṇṭu kaṟṟumaṟin tuṅkēṭṭun teḷintaperi yavaruṅ kaṇṭumaki ḻappurintu paṇṭaiviṉai akaṟṟi maṟṟumaṟi vaṉavellām aṟivitteṉ uḷattē maṉṉukiṉṟa meyiṉpa vāḻkkaimutaṟ poruḷē peṟṟumaṟi villāta pētai-eṉmēl uṉakkup peruṅkaruṇai vantavakai entavakai pēcē.
translation: You took me by force and ruled me even when I lacked the slightest wisdom. You gladly accepted all the faults committed by this lonely one. You made great people who have learned, listened, and gained clarity look upon me with joy. You removed my past karma and taught me everything else to be known. O Primal Reality of true blissful life dwelling permanently in my heart. Tell me, how did you develop such immense compassion for an ignorant fool like me?
commentary: The vastness of God's compassion is a mystery that completely transforms an ordinary, flawed person. The divine erases all past karma (the accumulated consequences of past actions) and teaches the soul everything it needs to know. Vallalar expresses wonder that the ultimate reality of the universe would choose to live permanently in his heart and show such immense love to someone who started out with no wisdom at all.

translit: cuṟṟatumaṟ ṟavvaḻiyā cūtatu-eṉ ṟeṇṇāt toṇṭarelāṅ kaṟkiṉṟār paṇṭumiṉṟuṅ kāṇār eṟṟatumpu maṇimaṉṟil iṉpanaṭam puriyum eṉṉuṭaiya turaiyēnāṉ niṉṉuṭaiya aruḷāl kaṟṟatuniṉ ṉiṭattēpiṉ kēṭṭatuniṉ ṉiṭattē kaṇṭatuniṉ ṉiṭattē-uṭ koṇṭatuniṉ ṉiṭattē peṟṟatuniṉ ṉiṭattē-iṉ puṟṟatuniṉ ṉiṭattē periyatavam purintēṉeṉ peṟṟi-ati cayamē.
translation: Devotees study all those texts without realizing that the path is an illusion. They did not see the truth in the past and they do not see it today. My Lord, you perform the dance of bliss in the gem-set hall surrounded by dashing waves. By your grace, what I learned was from you. What I later heard was from you. What I saw was from you. What I absorbed within was from you. What I received was from you. The bliss I experienced was from you. I performed great penance. My attained state is a wonder.
commentary: Vallalar says plainly that devotees who study by that path, not seeing that it deceives them, have never seen the truth, then or now. Instead of relying on texts, every single thing he learned, saw, and absorbed came directly from divine grace.

translit: ēṟiyanāṉ orunilaiyil ēṟa-aṟi yātē iḷaikkiṉṟa kālatteṉ iḷaippellām oḻiya vīṟiya-ōr paruvacatti kaikoṭuttut tūkki mēlēṟṟac ceytavaḷai mēvuṟavuñ ceytu tēṟiyanīr pōleṉatu cittamikat tēṟit teḷintiṭavuñ ceytaṉai-ic ceykai-evar ceyvār ūṟiyamey aṉpuṭaiyār uḷḷameṉum potuvil uvantunaṭam purikiṉṟa oruperiya poruḷē.
translation: When I climbed but did not know how to ascend to a certain state, I grew weary. To remove all my fatigue, a powerful manifesting energy extended her hand and lifted me. You made me climb higher and united me with her. You made my mind perfectly clear and lucid like pure water. Who else could perform this deed? You are the one supreme Reality who joyfully dances in the open hall of the hearts of those filled with welling true love.
commentary: Spiritual progress cannot be forced by personal effort alone. When weariness sets in, a powerful divine energy reaches out to lift the seeker higher. The supreme reality is not confined to a physical temple, but dances joyfully in the open hall of a heart filled with true love for all beings.

translit: tarunitiyak kuruviyaṟṟac cañcalikku maṉattāl taḷarntaciṟi yēṉtaṉatu taḷarvellān tavirttu irunitiyat tirumakaḷir iruvareṉai vaṇaṅki icaintiṭuvan taṉamappā eṉṟumakiḻn ticaittup perunitivāyt tiṭa-eṉatu muṉpāṭi āṭum peṟṟi-aṟit taṉai-intap pētamaiyēṉ taṉakkē orunitiniṉ aruḷnitiyum uvantaḷittal vēṇṭum uyarpotuvil iṉapanaṭam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē.
translation: I was a lowly person, weary and distressed in mind because I lacked the wealth-yielding treasure. You dispelled all my weariness. You made the two goddesses of great wealth bow to me, joyfully sing "Accept our salutations, father," and dance before me so that immense riches would come to me. You bestowed this state upon my ignorant self. You must joyfully grant me the supreme treasure, the treasure of your grace. You are the supreme Reality who performs the dance of bliss in the high universal hall.
commentary: Material wealth and worldly success are completely insignificant next to the truth. Even if the goddesses of fortune were to bow before him and offer immense earthly riches, Vallalar asks only for the single supreme treasure: divine grace.

translit: añcātē eṉmakaṉē aṉukkirakam purintām āṭukanī vēṇṭiyavā ṟāṭuka-iv vulakil ceñcoli vayalōṅku tillaimaṉṟil āṭun tirunaṭaṅkaṇ ṭaṉpuruvāyc cittacutta ṉāki eñcāta neṭuṅkālam iṉpaveḷḷan tiḷaittē iṉitumika vāḻiyaveṉ ṟeṉakkaruḷic ceytāy tuñcāti yantamilāc cuttanaṭat taracē turiyanaṭu vē-irunta cuyañcōti maṇiyē.
translation: "Do not fear, my son. I have bestowed my grace upon you. Dance as you wish, dance in this world. Witness the holy dance in the hall of Thillai surrounded by fertile fields of red paddy. Become the embodiment of love. Attain purity of mind. Revel in the flood of bliss for an endless time and live most sweetly." Thus you blessed me. You are the King of the pure dance, free from slumber, beginning, and end. You are the self-effulgent Jothi gem shining in the center of the transcendent state.
commentary: The divine command is simple: do not fear, become the embodiment of love, and attain a pure mind. The ultimate reality blessing him is the self-effulgent Jothi (light), shining clearly at the very center of the transcendent state.

translit: nāṉkēṭkiṉ ṟavaiyellām aḷikkiṉṟāy eṉakku nallavaṉē ellāmum vallaciva cittā tāṉkēṭkiṉ ṟavaiyiṉṟi muḻutoruṅkē uṇarntāy tattuvaṉē mati-aṇinta caṭaimuṭi-em iṟaivā tēṉkēṭkum moḻimaṅkai orupaṅkil uṭaiyāy civaṉē-em perumāṉē tēvarperu māṉē vāṉkēṭkum pukaḻttillai maṉṟilnaṭam purivāy maṇimiṭaṟṟup peruṅkaruṇai vaḷḷaleṉkaṇ maṇiyē.
translation: You grant me everything I ask for. Oh good Lord, you are the all-powerful Siva Siddha. Without having to ask for anything, you comprehended everything entirely and at once. Oh embodiment of truth, our Lord wearing the moon on your matted hair. You hold on one side the goddess whose words are sweeter than honey. Oh Siva, our Lord, the Lord of the gods. You perform the dance in the hall of Thillai whose fame reaches the heavens. Oh greatly compassionate benefactor with a sapphire throat, you are the apple of my eye.
commentary: The divine is completely compassionate and understands human needs before a single word is spoken. While drawing on traditional images of the deity Siva, such as the moon in his hair and his blue throat, the focus remains entirely on this boundless, giving grace.

translit: āṉanta veḷiyiṉiṭai āṉanta vaṭivāy āṉanta naṭampuriyum āṉanta amutē vāṉanta mutalellā antamuṅkaṇ ṭaṟintōr matikkiṉṟa poruḷēveṇ matimuṭicceṅ kaṉiyē ūṉantaṅ kiyamāyai uṭaliṉiṭat tiruntum ūṉamilā tirukkiṉṟa uḷavaruḷic ceytāy nāṉanta uḷavukaṇṭu naṭattukiṉṟa vakaiyum nallavaṉē nīmakiḻntu collavaru vāyē.
translation: O nectar of bliss who dances the dance of bliss in the space of bliss, taking the form of bliss. O Reality revered by those who have seen and known all ends, beginning with the end of sound. O red fruit wearing the white moon on your crown. You graciously revealed the secret of remaining flawless even while living in this fleshy, illusory body. O good one, please come joyfully and tell me how I can realize this secret and practice it.
commentary: The physical body is often seen as a trap of illusion and decay. Yet, the divine reveals a deep secret: it is possible to live inside this flesh without being corrupted by it. The speaker asks for the grace to not just understand this secret, but to actively live it out in the world.

translit: āraṇamum ākamamum etutuṇinta tatuvē ampalattil āṭukiṉṟa āṭṭameṉa eṉakkuk kāraṇamuṅ kāriyamum pulappaṭavē terittāy kaṇṇutalē iṅkitaṟkuk kaimmāṟoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ pūraṇaniṉ aṭittoṇṭu purikiṉṟa ciṟiyēṉ pōṟṟiciva pōṟṟi-eṉap pōṟṟimakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ nāraṇanāṉ mukaṉmutalōr kāṇparuman naṭattai nāyaṭiyēṉ itayattil naviṟṟiyaruḷ vāyē.
translation: You clearly revealed to me the cause and the effect, showing that the dance you perform in the hall is the very truth established by the Vedas and Agamas. O Lord with the eye on your forehead, I know no way to repay you for this. As a lowly one performing complete service at your feet, I rejoice in praising you, crying "Praise, O Siva, praise." Please graciously instruct my dog-like heart in that conduct which is hard to behold even for Vishnu, Brahma, and the other gods.
commentary: Traditional scriptures like the Vedas and Agamas point toward a supreme truth, which is brought to life perfectly in the divine dance. Understanding the deep laws of cause and effect is a gift so great that no human service can ever repay it. The speaker prays to be taught a way of living that even the highest gods struggle to comprehend.

translit: iṟaivaniṉa taruḷālē eṉaikkaṇṭu koṇṭēṉ eṉakkuḷuṉaik kaṇṭēṉpiṉ iruvarumoṉ ṟāka uṟaivatukaṇ ṭaticayittēṉ aticayattai oḻikkum uḷavaṟiyēṉ avvuḷavoṉ ṟuraittaruḷal vēṇṭum maṟaivatilā maṇimaṉṟuḷ naṭampuriyum vāḻvē vāḻmutalē paramacuka vāri-eṉkaṇ maṇiyē kuṟaivatilāk kuḷirmatiyē civakāmavallik koḻuntupaṭarn tōṅkukiṉṟa kuṇanimalak kuṉṟē.
translation: O Lord, by your grace I found myself. I saw you within me, and then I was amazed to see us residing together as one. I do not know the secret to transcend this amazement. You must graciously tell me that secret. O life who dances in the imperishable hall of gems. O source of life, ocean of supreme bliss, apple of my eye. O flawless cool moon. O flawless hill of virtues upon which the tender vine of Sivakama Valli spreads and flourishes.
commentary: True self-discovery happens only through divine grace. When the soul finally sees God living within itself, the two merge into one inseparable presence. This union brings an overwhelming sense of wonder, and the speaker asks for the supreme clarity needed to move beyond even that amazement into lasting peace. (Sivakama Valli names the divine mother's grace, which flourishes here like a living vine).

translit: cattiyamey aṟiviṉpa vaṭivākip potuvil taṉinaṭañcey taruḷukiṉṟa caṟkuruvē eṉakkup puttiyoṭu cittiyumnal laṟivumaḷit taḻiyāp puṉitanilai taṉilirukkap purintaparam poruḷē patti-aṟi yācciṟiyēṉ mayakkamiṉṉun tavirttup paramacuka mayamākkip paṭiṟṟuḷattaip pōkkit tattuvanī nāṉeṉṉum pōtamatu nīkkit taṉittacukā tītamumnī tantaruḷka makiḻntē.
translation: O True Guru who graciously performs the peerless dance in the public hall, embodying existence, pure consciousness, and bliss. O Supreme Reality who granted me clear intellect, spiritual attainment, and good wisdom, making me abide in the imperishable pure state. Eradicate the remaining delusion of this lowly one who knows no devotion. Make me an embodiment of supreme bliss, banish my deceitful mind, remove the dualistic awareness of "you" and "I", and joyfully grant me the supreme state beyond bliss.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual goal is to tear down the dividing wall between "you" and "I". The divine acts as the true teacher, offering a pure state of existence, awareness, and joy. The speaker begs to have all lingering deceit and worldly confusion stripped away, leaving only a perfect, unified reality that goes far beyond ordinary happiness.

translit: ētumaṟi yātiruḷil iruntaciṟa yēṉai eṭuttuviṭut taṟivuciṟi tēyntiṭavum purintu ōtumaṟai mutaṟkalaikaḷ ōtāmal uṇara uṇarvilirun tuṇartti-aruḷ uṇmainilai kāṭṭit tītuceṟi camayaneṟi cellutalait tavirttut tiru-aruṇmeyp potuneṟiyil celuttiyum nāṉmaruḷum pōtumayaṅ kēlmakaṉē eṉṟumayak kellām pōkki-eṉak kuḷḷirunta puṉitaparam poruḷē.
translation: I was a lowly one sitting in darkness, knowing nothing. You lifted me out and caused a little knowledge to dawn in me. You taught me from within my own awareness so that I could understand the Vedas and fundamental arts without reading them, and you revealed the true state of grace. You prevented me from walking the flawed paths of various religions and guided me into the true, universal path of holy grace. Whenever I grew confused, you told me, "Do not be bewildered, my son." O pure Supreme Reality residing within me, you dispelled all my delusion.
commentary: Grace kept Vallalar from the religious paths, which he calls full of faults, and set him on the true, universal path of holy grace. His knowledge did not come from reading books or keeping sectarian rules: God awakened it from within his own awareness. Whenever he grew confused, the Lord spoke to him like a loving parent: “Do not be bewildered, my son.”

translit: muṉṉaṟiyēṉ piṉṉaṟiyēṉ muṭipatoṉṟu maṟiyēṉ muṉṉiyumuṉ ṉātumiṅkē moḻintamoḻi muḻutum paṉṉilaiyil ceṟikiṉṟōr palarummaṉam uvappap paḻutupaṭā vaṇṇamaruḷ parintaḷitta patiyē taṉṉilaiyil kuṟaivupaṭāt tattuvappēr oḷiyē taṉimaṉṟuḷ naṭampuriyañ cattiyataṟ paramē innilaiyil iṉṉumeṉṟaṉ mayakkamelān tavirttē eṉai-aṭimai koḷalvēṇṭum itucamayaṅ kāṇē.
translation: I do not know the beginning, I do not know the end, I do not know any conclusion. O Lord, you lovingly bestowed grace so that many who gather in various states rejoice in their hearts without finding fault with any word spoken here, whether thought out or spontaneous. O great light of truth that never diminishes in its state. O supreme reality of truth who dances in the peerless hall. In this state, you must remove all my remaining delusions and take me as your servant. See, this is the right moment.
commentary: True spiritual wisdom does not rely on formal logic or knowing how things begin and end. The divine light of truth directly guides the speaker's words, making his spontaneous songs flawless and joyful to people of many different backgrounds. He asks this supreme reality to clear away whatever confusion remains in his mind and accept his complete surrender.

translit: aiyaṟiviṟ ciṟitumaṟin taṉupavikkat teriyā taḻutukaḷit tāṭukiṉṟa apparuvat teḷiyēṉ meyyaṟiviṟ ciṟantavaruṅ kaḷikka-uṉaip pāṭi virumpi-aruḷ neṟinaṭakaka viṭuttaṉainī yaṉṟō poyyaṟiviṟ pulaimaṉattuk koṭiyēṉmuṉ piṟappil purintavam yātataṉaip pukaṉṟaruḷa vēṇṭum tuyyaṟivuk kaṟivāki maṇimaṉṟil naṭañcey cuttapari pūraṇamāñ cukarūpap poruḷē.
translation: I was a simpleton in that childhood stage, knowing nothing of how to experience even a little through the five senses, only crying, rejoicing, and playing. Did you not make me sing of you so that even those excelling in true knowledge rejoice, and set me to desire and walk the path of grace? You must graciously tell me what penance I, a cruel one with a base mind of false knowledge, performed in my past birth. O form of bliss, the pure, completely perfect reality who dances in the ruby hall, acting as the knowledge for pure knowledge.
commentary: Even as an ignorant child who only knew how to cry and play, the speaker was drawn to sing songs of grace that astonished the wise. He marvels at this unearned gift, wondering what past acts of devotion could possibly justify it. He credits all his spiritual knowledge entirely to the dancing light of divine perfection.

translit: aruḷniṟainta peruntakaiyē āṉanta amutē aṟputappoṉ ampalattē āṭukiṉṟa aracē teruḷniṟainta cintaiyilē tittikkun tēṉē ceṅkaṉiyē mati-aṇinta ceñcaṭai-em perumāṉ maruḷniṟainta maṉakkoṭiyēṉ vañcamelāṅ kaṇṭu makiḻntiṉiya vāḻvaḷitta mākaruṇaik kaṭalē iruḷniṟainta mayakkamiṉṉun tīrttaruḷal vēṇṭum eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakaṉē itutaruṇaṅ kāṇē.
translation: O great noble one filled with grace. O nectar of bliss. O King who dances in the wondrous golden hall. O honey that tastes sweet in the clear mind. O ripe red fruit. Our Lord with red matted locks adorned with the moon. O great ocean of compassion who saw all the deceit of my cruel, delusion-filled mind and still joyfully granted me a sweet life. You must graciously clear away my remaining dark delusions. My Lord, see, this is the moment.
commentary: The divine appears here with traditional imagery of Siva, wearing the crescent moon in his matted red hair. A compassion so immense ignores human flaws and deceit, offering a sweet life instead of harsh judgment. Awestruck by this unearned grace, the speaker asks this great ocean of compassion to wash away the last of his inner darkness.

translit: maṉṉiyapoṉ ṉampalattē āṉanta naṭañcey māmaṇiyē eṉṉirukaṇ vayaṅkumoḷi maṇiyē taṉṉiyalpiṉ niṟaintaruḷuñ cattuvapū raṇamē taṟparamē ciṟparamē tattuvappē roḷiyē aṉṉiyamil lātacutta attuvita nilaiyē ātiyanta mētumiṉṟi amarntaparam poruḷē eṉṉiyalpiṉ eṉakkaruḷi mayakkamiṉṉun tavirttē eṉai-āṇṭu koḷalvēṇṭum itutaruṇaṅ kāṇē.
translation: O great gem who performs the dance of bliss in the enduring golden hall. O shining jewel of light in my two eyes. O complete perfection of goodness who graciously abides in your own nature. O supreme reality. O supreme consciousness. O great light of truth. O pure non-dual state without any other. O supreme reality seated without beginning or end. Granting me grace fitting my nature, you must remove my remaining delusions and rule over me. See, this is the moment.
commentary: God is experienced both as an intimate, shining light in the eyes and as a boundless reality without beginning or end. It is a pure, non-dual state of oneness where nothing else exists. Recognizing this vast perfection, the speaker asks to be freed entirely from all worldly confusion so the divine can rule over him.

translit: pūtanilai mutaṟparamē nātanilai aḷavum pōntavaṟṟiṉ iyaṟkaimutaṟ puṇarppellām viḷaṅka vētanilai ākamattiṉ nilaikaḷelām viḷaṅka viṉaiyēṉṟaṉ uḷattiruntu viḷakkiyamey viḷakkē pōtanilai yāyatuvuṅ kaṭanta-iṉpa nilaiyāyp potuviṉiṉmey aṟiviṉpa naṭampuriyum poruḷē ētanilai yāvakai-eṉ mayakkamiṉṉun tavirttē eṉaikkāttal vēṇṭukiṉṟēṉ itutaruṇaṅ kāṇē.
translation: O true lamp who sat in my karmic heart and illuminated it to reveal the nature and combinations of everything from the physical elements up to the supreme state of sound, and to make clear all the states of the Vedas and Agamas. O reality who exists as the state of knowledge and the state of bliss beyond it, performing the dance of true knowledge and bliss in the common hall. I ask you to protect me by removing my remaining delusions so no harmful state befalls me. See, this is the moment.
commentary: The divine acts as a lamp lit directly within the human heart. This inner light reveals the deepest workings of the physical world, the true meanings of ancient scriptures like the Vedas and Agamas, and the highest spiritual states of sound and bliss. The speaker asks this supreme light of true knowledge to guide him safely past all harm.

translit: cevvaṇṇat tirumēṉi koṇṭorupāṟ pacantu tikaḻpaṭika vaṇṇamoṭu tittikkuṅ kaṉiyē ivvaṇṇam eṉamaṟaikkum eṭṭāmeyp poruḷē eṉṉuyirē eṉṉuyirkkuḷ iruntaruḷum patiyē avvaṇṇap peruntakaiyē ampalattē naṭañcey āramutē aṭiyēṉiṅ kakamakiḻntu purital evvaṇṇam atuvaṇṇam icaittaruḷal vēṇṭum eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakaṉē itutaruṇaṅ kāṇē.
translation: You have a red sacred body, green on one side, and you shine with the color of crystal. O sweet fruit! O true Reality beyond the reach of the Vedas, which cannot define you by saying you are like this. O my life! O Lord who graciously resides within my life! O Great One of such magnificence! O rare nectar dancing in the Hall! You must instruct me how I, your servant, should act here with a joyful heart. O my Master, see that this is the right moment.
commentary: The poet asks the divine for immediate guidance on how to live and act with a joyful heart. He visualizes God shining like crystal and bearing a form that is red on one half and green on the other, symbolizing the perfect balance of masculine and feminine energies. Though the Vedas, the ancient sacred scriptures, fail to fully describe this ultimate reality, the poet knows this presence intimately because it resides within his own soul. He turns to this inner Master, who performs a cosmic dance in the open space of consciousness, to reveal the right path forward.

sections.title: The Garland of the Light of Grace

note: Editor's note: verse 78, kammaṭiyā (கம்மடியா): Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar read kammaṭiyar (கம்மடியர்); the author's handwriting allows both readings.
translit: ulakamelām utikkiṉṟa oḷinilaimey yiṉpam uṟukiṉṟa veḷinilaiyeṉ ṟupayanilai yāki ilakiyaniṉ cēvaṭikaḷ varuntiyiṭa naṭantē iravileḷi yēṉirukkum iṭantēṭi aṭaintu kalakamilāt terukkatavaṅ kāppaviḻkkap purintu kaḷitteṉai-aṅ kaḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttāy alakilaruṭ kaṭalāmuṉ perumaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ āṉanta vallimakiḻ aruḷnaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: O Lord of the dance of grace who delights Ananda Valli! Your beautiful red feet shine as the dual states: the state of light from which all worlds arise and the state of space where true bliss is experienced. Walking until those feet ached, you searched for and reached the place where this poor one was in the night. You opened the lock of the peaceful street door, joyfully called me there, and gave something into my hand. What can I say of your greatness, you who are an infinite ocean of grace?
commentary: The divine is the source of all light and the vast space of ultimate bliss, yet it acts with stunning intimacy. God searches in the dark, walking until His own feet ache, just to find a single poor soul. The immense creator of the universe stands at an ordinary street door to place a gift directly into a human hand.

translit: oḷivaṇṇam veḷivaṇṇam eṉṟaṉanta vēta ucciyelām meccukiṉṟa uccamala raṭikaḷ aḷivaṇṇam varuntiyiṭa naṭantaruḷi aṭiyēṉ aṭaintaviṭat taṭaintukata vantiṟakkap purintu kaḷivaṇṇam eṉai-aḻaitteṉ kaiyilvaṇṇam aḷitta karuṇaivaṇṇan taṉaiviyantu karutumvaṇṇam aṟiyēṉ tauviṇṇa muṭaiyaraṉpu ceyyumvaṇṇam potuvil teyvanaṭam purikiṉṟa caivaparam poruḷē.
translation: O Supreme Reality who performs the divine dance in the common hall so that those of clear understanding may offer their love! The crowns of the endless Vedas praise your supreme flower-like feet as the form of light and the form of space. Graciously walking until those tender feet ached, you reached the place where I was and opened the door. You joyfully called me and placed something beautiful in my hand. I do not know how to marvel at or even conceive of the nature of your grace.
commentary: The ancient scriptures praise the divine feet as the vastness of light and space, high above human reach. Yet those same exalted feet are tender, and they willingly ache to seek out the devotee in person. The experience leaves the heart in pure awe of a grace that brings the supreme reality right to a humble doorway.

translit: tirumālum urumāṟic cirañcīvi yākit tēṭiyuṅkaṇ ṭaṟiyāta cēvaṭikaḷ varunta varumālai maṇṇuṟattap peyarttunaṭan taruḷi vañcakaṉēṉ irukkumiṭam valintiravil tēṭit terumālaik katavutaṉait tiṟappittu niṉṟu cevvaṇṇat tiṭaippacanta tirumēṉi kāṭṭik kurumālaip peruvaṇṇak koḻuntoṉṟu koṭuttāy kurumaṇiniṉ tiruvaruḷaik kuṟittumakiḻn taṉaṉē.
translation: O supreme jewel! Even Vishnu took another form to live long and searched for your red feet but could not find them. Walking graciously on the earth until those very feet ached, you purposefully searched in the night for the place where this deceitful one stayed. You opened the street door, stood there, and revealed your divine form glowing golden-green amidst the red. You gave me a great, colorful, and radiant tender flame. I rejoiced contemplating your divine grace.
commentary: Even the greatest gods of the old traditions search the cosmos for the divine reality and fail to find it. But here, that supreme reality actively hunts through the night for someone who feels entirely unworthy. God steps through the door in glowing colors to hand over a bright, living flame of grace.

translit: aṉṟorunāḷ iraviṭaivan taṇikkavan tiṟappit taruṇmalarccē vaṭivāyiṟ paṭippuṟattum akattum maṉṟavaittuk koṇṭeṉṉai varavaḻaittu makaṉē varuntātē iṅkitaṉai vāṅkikkoḷ ḷeṉṉa oṉṟuciṟi yēṉmaṟuppa maṟittumvalin teṉatu orukaitaṉiṟ koṭuttiṅkē uṟaiti-eṉṟu maṟaintāy iṉṟatutāṉ aṉupavittuk kicaintatunā yaṭiyēṉ eṉṉatavam purintēṉō iṉittuyaroṉ ṟilaṉē.
translation: One day in the past, you came in the night, drew near, and opened the door. Placing your graceful, flower-like red feet firmly outside and inside the threshold, you summoned me. You said, "Son, do not sorrow. Take this." When this lowly one refused, you insisted, forcefully placed it in my hand, and vanished, saying, "Dwell here." Today I, a lowly servant, am ready to experience it. What penance have I done? I have no more sorrow now.
commentary: The divine approaches with the warmth of a parent, calling out directly to soothe all sorrow. When human insecurity hesitates and tries to refuse the gift, grace simply overrides it. God forces the blessing into his hand and commands him to stay rooted in that joy, wiping away all future grief.

translit: iravilaṭi varuntanaṭan teḻiṟkatavan tiṟappit teṉai-aḻaittu makaṉēnī ivvulakiṟ ciṟitum curaviṭaineñ cayarntiḷaittuk kalaṅkātē itaṉaik kaḷippoṭuvāṅ keṉa-eṉatu kaitaṉilē koṭuttu uraviṭai-iṅ kuṟaimakiḻn teṉattiruvāy malarnta uṉṉuṭaiya peruṅkaruṇaik koppilai-eṉ pukalvēṉ araviṭaiyil acaintāṭa ampalatti ṉaṭuvē āṉantat tirunaṭañcey tāṭṭukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: O King who performs the divine dance of bliss in the center of the hall, making the serpent on your waist sway! Walking in the night until your feet ached, you opened the beautiful door and called me. You said, "Son, do not let your heart grow weary, faint, or confused in the wilderness of this world. Take this with joy." Placing it in my hand, you opened your divine mouth and said, "Dwell here firmly in joy." Your great grace has no equal. What can I say?
commentary: Worldly life often feels like a harsh wilderness that drains the heart and confuses the mind. The divine brings a direct cure for this exhaustion, handing over a gift meant to be taken with pure joy. The cosmic dancer stops to offer deep, unshakable comfort, telling the soul exactly how to survive the world.

translit: iyaṅkāta iraviṭai-aṉ ṟorunāḷvan teḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭan taṉaittēṭik katavutiṟap pittuk kayaṅkāta malaraṭikaḷ kaviṉvāyiṟ paṭiyiṉ kaṭaippuṟattum akattumvaittuk kaḷitteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittu mayaṅkātē iṅkitaṉai vāṅkikkoṇ ṭulakil makaṉēnī viḷaiyāṭi vāḻka-eṉa uraittāy puyaṅkāniṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyātu tirintēṉ poyyaṭiyēṉ aṟintiṉṟu pūrittēṉ uḷamē.
translation: One day during the still night, you came seeking poor me. You searched for my dwelling and made me open the door. You placed your unfading flower-like feet on the beautiful doorstep, one outside and one inside. You joyfully called me there and said, "Do not be bewildered. Take this here in the world. My son, play and live happily." O Lord who wears the serpent, I wandered without knowing the rarity of your grace. Today I, a false devotee, finally understand it, and my heart swells with joy.
commentary: The Divine does not wait for the soul to find Him; He comes seeking the devotee in the dark. Like a loving parent, He stands at the threshold, offers a mysterious gift of grace, and tells him to live joyfully. Though the young poet did not grasp its immense value at the time, the memory now fills him with joy.

translit: orunāḷaṉ ṟiravilaṭi varuntanaṭan taṭiyēṉ uṟṟa-iṭan taṉaittēṭik katavutiṟap pittu marunāḷa malaraṭi-oṉṟuḷḷakattē peyarttu vaittumakiḻn teṉai-aḻaittu vāṅkitaṉai eṉṟu tarunāḷil yāṉmaṟuppa maṟittumvalin teṉatu taṭaṅkaitaṉiṟ koṭuttiṅkē cārka-eṉa uraittāy varunāḷil ataṉarumai aṟintumakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ maṇimaṉṟuḷ naṭampuriyum māṇikka maṇiyē.
translation: One night you walked until your feet ached. You searched for the place where this devotee stayed and made the door open. Placing one fragrant flower-foot inside, you rejoiced and called me. You said, "Take this." When you offered it and I refused, you insisted, forced it into my broad hands, and told me, "Join here." In these coming days, I understand its rarity and rejoice. O ruby gem dancing in the gem-set hall!
commentary: Grace is sometimes given even when the soul feels unready or afraid to accept it. God walks until His feet ache just to find the devotee, pressing the gift into his hands despite his hesitation. It is a vivid picture of divine persistence and unconditional love.

translit: neṭumālum paṉṟi-eṉa neṭuṅkālam viraintu nēṭiyuṅkaṇ ṭaṟiyātu nīṭiyapūm pataṅkaḷ toṭumālai yeṉavarupū makaḷmuṭiyiṟ cūṭṭit tolviṉaiyēṉ irukkumiṭan taṉaittēṭit toṭarntu kaṭumālai naṭu-iraviṟ katavutiṟap pittuk kaṭaiyēṉai aḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttuk koṭumālai viṭuttumakir eṉattiruvāy malarntāy kuṇakkuṉṟē innāḷniṉ koṭaiyai-aṟin taṉaṉē.
translation: Tall Thirumal searched for a long time as a rushing boar but could not find them. Yet you placed those tall flower-feet on the crown of the earth maiden who approached like a worn garland. You tracked down the dwelling of this devotee bound by old karma. In the dead of the dark night, you made me open the door. You called the lowest of the low, placed something in my hand, and opened your holy mouth to say, "Cast away your cruel delusion and rejoice." O mountain of virtues, today I understand your gift.
commentary: Traditional lore tells of the god Thirumal taking the form of a boar to dig for the bottom of the divine feet, failing completely. Yet those same unsearchable feet willingly walk through the dark night to stand at a humble devotee's door. The supreme reality lowers itself entirely to lift up the lowest of the low.

translit: maṟaimuṭikku maṇiyāki vayaṅkiyacē vaṭikaḷ maṇmītu paṭanaṭantu vantaruḷi aṭiyēṉ kuṟaimuṭikkum paṭikkatavan tiṟappittu niṉṟu kūvi-eṉai aḻaittoṉṟu koṭuttaruḷic ceytāy kaṟaimuṭikkuṅ kaḷattaracē karuṇaineṭuṅ kaṭalē kaṇṇōṅkum oḷiyēciṟ kaṉaveḷikkuḷ veḷiyē piṟaimuṭikkuñ caṭaikkaṭavuṭ peruntaruvē kuruvē periyamaṉṟuḷ naṭampuriyum periyaparam poruḷē.
translation: Your red feet shine as the crest-jewel of the Vedas. Those feet walked upon the earth to come to me. To end my flaws, you made the door open, stood there, called out to me, and gave me a gift of grace. O King with the dark-stained neck, O vast ocean of compassion! O light rising in the eye, O space within the dense space of consciousness! O great tree of a God with the crescent moon on your matted hair, O Guru! O great Supreme Reality dancing in the grand hall!
commentary: The ancient scriptures, the Vedas, hold the divine feet as their ultimate pinnacle. But rather than remaining an abstract truth, this supreme reality takes on form and walks on the common earth. God personally crosses the distance to cure the human heart of its flaws.

translit: aṉṟakattē aṭivarunta naṭanteṉṉai aḻaittiṅ kañcātē makaṉē-eṉ ṟaḷittaṉai-oṉ ṟataṉait tuṉṟakattuc ciṟiyēṉ nāṉ aṟiyātu vaṟitē cuḻaṉṟatukaṇ ṭiraṅkimikat tuṇintumakiḻ vippāṉ iṉṟakattē pukuntaruḷi eṉakkataṉait terivit tiṉpuṟaccey taruḷiyaniṉ irakkamevark kuḷatō maṉṟakattu naṭampurintu vayaṅkumoru kuruvē vallavarel lāmvaṇaṅkum nallaparam poruḷē.
translation: That day you walked into my home until your feet ached, called me, and said, "Fear not, my son." You gave me something. Being small and dense of mind, I did not understand it and wandered in vain. Seeing this, you took pity. Firmly resolving to bring me joy, you entered my home today, revealed its meaning to me, and gave me bliss. Who else possesses your compassion? O unique Guru who shines dancing in the hall! O good Supreme Reality worshipped by all the mighty!
commentary: Divine compassion does not abandon the devotee when a gift of grace is misunderstood. Seeing the soul wander in confusion, God returns later to explain the gift and awaken true joy. Spiritual understanding takes time, and the supreme reality provides both the gift and the wisdom to finally understand it.

translit: aṉparmaṉak kōyililē amarntaruḷi viḷaṅkum arumporuḷām uṉatumala raṭivarunta naṭantu vaṉparkaḷil talainiṉṟa vañcakaṉēṉ irunta maṉaikkatavu tiṟappittu makiḻnteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittut tuṉpamelām nīṅkuka-iṅ kitutaṉaivāṅ kukanī toḻumpaṉeṉṟa eṉṉuṭaiya turaiyēniṉ ṉaruḷai eṉpakarvēṉ eṉviyappēṉ eṅṅaṉamnāṉ maṟappēṉ eṉuyiruk kuyirāki ilaṅkicaṟ kuruvē.
translation: O rare treasure seated and shining in the temple of devotees' minds! You walked to the house where I, the chief among cruel deceivers, stayed, until Your lotus feet ached. You had the door opened, joyfully called me there, and said, "May all your sorrows vanish. Take this here. You are My servant." O my Lord! How can I speak of Your grace? How can I marvel at it? How can I ever forget it, O true Guru who shines as the life of my life?
commentary: God does not wait for the perfect seeker. The Divine searches actively for the lost, walking until His feet ache to find a person who feels entirely unworthy and deceitful. The grace offered here comes as a sudden, joyful gift that claims the soul and wipes away its sorrow.

translit: ñālanilai aṭivarunta naṭantaruḷi aṭiyēṉ naṇṇumiṭan taṉiṟkatavam naṉṟutiṟap pittuk kālanilai karutimaṉaṅ kalaṅkukiṉṟa makaṉē kalaṅkātē eṉṟeṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttuc cilanilai uṟavāḻka eṉattiruvāy malarnta civaperumāṉ niṉperumait tiruvaruḷeṉ ṉeṉpēṉ ālanilai maṇikaṇṭat tarumperuñcīr oḷiyē ampalattil tirunaṭañcey tāṭṭukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: Graciously walking on the earth until Your feet ached, You had the door to my dwelling fully opened. You told me, "O son whose mind is troubled thinking of the nature of time, do not be troubled." Giving something into my hand, Your divine mouth blossomed and said, "Live in a state of virtue." O Lord Siva! What can I say of Your great divine grace? O rare and immensely glorious Light, possessing a beautiful neck that holds the dark poison! O King who performs the divine dance in the Hall!
commentary: The fear of time and mortality often troubles the human mind. The Divine steps directly into this anxiety, opening the door to tell the seeker not to fear. To reassure the soul, God places a tangible gift of grace into their hand and simply commands them to live a virtuous life. The verse recalls the traditional image of God swallowing dark poison to save the world, showing a grace that absorbs the dangers of life.

translit: iruḷniṟainta iravilaṭi varuntanaṭan taṭiyēṉ irukkumiṭan taṉaittēṭik katavutiṟap pittu maruḷniṟainta maṉattālē mayaṅkukiṉṟa makaṉē mayaṅkātē eṉṟeṉṉai varavaḻaittup pukaṉṟu teruḷniṟainta toṉṟeṉatu ceṅkaitaṉiṟ koṭuttut tikaḻntuniṉṟa paramporuḷniṉ tiruvaruḷeṉ ṉeṉpēṉ aruḷniṟainta meypporuḷē aṭimuṭi-oṉ ṟillā āṉanta maṉṟilnaṭam āṭukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: In the dark night, You walked until Your feet ached, searched for the place where I live, and had the door opened. You summoned me and said, "O son who is bewildered by a mind filled with delusion, do not be bewildered." You placed a thing of pure clarity into my fair hand. O Supreme Reality who stood in splendor! What can I say of Your divine grace? O Reality filled with grace! O King who dances in the Hall of Bliss that has no beginning and no end!
commentary: Spiritual blindness feels like a dark night or a deluded mind. The Divine actively pierces this darkness, tracking down the bewildered soul to offer comfort. By placing a thing of pure clarity into the seeker's hand, God replaces confusion with the direct experience of the Supreme Reality, who dances endlessly in pure bliss.

translit: kaṉmayamuṅ kaṉivikkun tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntak kaṭaippulaiyēṉ irukkumiṭan taṉaittēṭi naṭantu toṉmayamām iraviṉiṭaik katavutiṟap pittut tuṇintaḻaitteṉ kaitaṉilē tūya-oṉṟai yaḷittu vaṉmayamil lāmaṉattāl vāḻka-eṉa uraitta māmaṇiniṉ tiruvaruḷiṉ vaṇmaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ taṉmayamē ciṉmayappoṉ ampalattē iṉpat taṉinaṭañcey taruḷukiṉṟa tattuvappē roḷiyē.
translation: You walked until Your divine feet, which can melt even stones, ached, searching for the place where I, the lowest wretch, live. In the middle of the ancient night, You had the door opened, called me with resolve, and placed a pure thing into my hand. You said, "Live with a mind free of cruelty." O great Gem, what can I say of the bounty of Your divine grace? O self-existent Reality! O supreme Light of Truth who graciously performs the matchless dance of bliss in the golden Hall of pure consciousness!
commentary: True grace demands a transformation of the heart. When the Divine arrives in the middle of the night to hand over a pure gift, the accompanying command is to live with a mind entirely free of cruelty. This reflects the core teaching of Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings), showing that spiritual life requires abandoning all harshness toward others.

translit: piraṇavattiṉ aṭimuṭiyiṉ naṭuviṉumniṉ ṟōṅkum peruṅkaruṇait tiruvaṭikaḷ peyarntuvarun tiṭavē karaṇamuṟṟu naṭantaṭiyēṉ irukkumiṭan tēṭik katavutiṟap pittaruḷik kaṭaiyēṉai aḻaittuc caraṇamuṟṟu varuntiya-eṉ makaṉē-iṅ kitaṉait tāṅku-eṉ ṟoṉṟeṉatu taṭaṅkaitaṉiṟ koṭuttu maraṇamaṟṟu vāḻka-eṉat tiruvārttai aḷittāy maṉṟuṭaiyāy niṉaruḷiṉ vaṇmai-evark kuḷatē.
translation: You moved Your greatly compassionate divine feet, which stand supreme at the base, crown, and middle of the Pranava, walking purposefully until they ached. You searched for the place where I live, graciously had the door opened, and called me, the lowest of all. You said, "O My son who suffered seeking refuge, hold this here," and gave something into my broad hand. You offered the divine word, "Live without death." O Lord of the Hall! Who else possesses the bounty of Your grace?
commentary: The ultimate promise of this spiritual path is a life beyond mortality. The Divine, whose feet span the very foundation of Pranava (the sacred syllable Om), searches out the lowest seeker to deliver a supreme guarantee. By placing the gift of grace into the seeker's hand, God speaks the defining command of this teaching: to live a life free from death.

translit: oṅkārat tuḷḷoḷiyāy avvoḷikkuḷ oḷiyāy upayavaṭi vākiyaniṉ apayapatam varunta īṅkāra naṭantiravil yāṉirukkum iṭampōn teḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittaṅ keṉṉaivalin taḻaittup pāṅkārum vaṇṇamoṉṟeṉ kaitaṉilē aḷittup paṇpoṭuvāḻn tiṭuka-eṉap paṇittaparam poruḷē āṅkāra vaṇṇamakaṉ ṟatai-aṟintu makiḻntē aṉupavikkiṉ ṟēṉpotuvil āṭukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: You are the inner light of the primal sound Om, and the light within that light. Your fearless feet of dual form endured hardship as you walked here in the night. You came to where I dwell, opened the beautiful door, and forcefully called me. You placed a beautiful thing in my hand and instructed me to live a noble life, O Supreme Reality. Casting away all ego, I understand this, rejoice, and experience it, O King who dances in the public hall.
commentary: The supreme light that rests deep inside the primal sound Om did not wait to be found. God personally walked through the dark night to reach the poet's door. By seeking him out and pressing a gift into his hand, the divine presence sweeps away the last traces of human ego. Grace here is a sudden, personal visitation that commands the recipient to live a noble life.

translit: aripiramā tiyarellām aṟintaṇuka oṇṇā arumperuñcīr aṭimalarkaḷ aṉṟorunāḷ varuntak kari-iravil naṭantaruḷi yāṉirukku miṭattē katavutiṟap pitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttu urimaiyoṭu vāḻka-eṉa uraittatuvum aṉṟi uvantiṉṟai iraviṉumvan tuṇarttiṉai-eṉ mītu piriyamuṉak kiruntavaṇṇam eṉpukalvēṉ potuvil perunaṭañcey aracē-eṉ piḻaipoṟutta kuruvē.
translation: Vishnu, Brahma, and all the gods cannot comprehend or approach your rarely glorious lotus feet. Yet on that day, your feet endured hardship as you walked in the pitch-dark night to where I live. You opened the door, placed something in my hand, and told me to live with rightful authority. You gladly came this night as well and awakened my realization. How can I describe your great love for me? O King who performs the great dance in the public hall, O Guru who forgave my faults.
commentary: There is a deep contrast between the great gods of tradition and a humble devotee. Vishnu and Brahma cannot even glimpse the feet of the Supreme Lord. Yet those same feet endured the hardship of walking through a pitch-dark night simply to find an ordinary person. This shows that ultimate grace is not won by divine status or power. It is given freely through immense, unmerited love.

translit: kāraṇaṉeṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟa nāraṇaṉum ayaṉum kaṉaviṭattuṅ kāṇpariya kaḻalaṭikaḷ varunta ūraṇavi naṭanteḷiyēṉ uṟaiyumiṭan tēṭi uvanteṉatu kaitaṉilē oṉṟukoṭut tiṅkē ēraṇavi uṟaikamakiḻt teṉa-uraittāy niṉcīr yātaṟintu pukaṉṟēṉmuṉ yātutavam purintēṉ pāraṇavi aṉparelām parintupukaḻn tēttap paṇi-aṇintu maṇimaṉṟuḷ aṇinaṭañcey patiyē.
translation: Narayana, who is called the source, and Brahma find it difficult to behold your anklet-adorned feet even in their dreams. Yet your feet endured hardship as you walked through the town and sought the place where this lowly one dwells. You gladly placed something in my hand and told me to abide here in joy. What did I ever know of your glory to praise it? What penance did I perform in the past? The devotees of the world lovingly sing your praises. You wear serpent adornments and perform a beautiful dance in the ruby hall, O Lord.
commentary: The traditional creator gods cannot see the ultimate reality even in their dreams. But this supreme divine presence physically walks through an ordinary town just to find a lowly seeker. The poet is overwhelmed by this intimate encounter. He wonders what past actions could have possibly earned such a direct, loving gift.

translit: turiyaveḷi taṉiṟparama nāta-aṇai naṭuvē cuyañcuṭaril tulaṅkukiṉṟa tuṇaiyaṭikaḷ varuntap piriyamoṭu naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭan tēṭip peruṅkatavan tiṟappittup pēyaṉeṉai aḻaittu uriyaporuḷ oṉṟeṉatu kaiyilaḷit tiṅkē uṟaikamakiḻn teṉa-uraitta uttamaniṉ ṉaruḷaip periyaporu ṉevaṟṟiṉukkum periyaporu ḷeṉṟē piṉṉaraṟin tēṉitaṟku muṉṉaraṟi yēṉē.
translation: Your twin feet shine with self-luminous light in the center of the supreme sound in the transcendent space. They endured hardship as you walked with love, seeking out the place where this lowly one lives. You opened the great door, called out to this fool, placed a rightful substance in my hand, and told me to abide here in joy. O Supreme One, I realized later that your grace is the greatest reality above all great realities. I did not know this before.
commentary: The divine feet that shine in the absolute highest state of consciousness step down to seek out someone who feels entirely unworthy. When God hands over this mysterious gift, the recipient experiences a massive shift in understanding. He realizes only after the fact that this freely given grace is the absolute highest reality in existence, greater than any other truth.

translit: nīḷāti mūlameṉa niṉṟavaṉum neṭunāḷ nēṭiyuṅkaṇ ṭaṟiyāta niṉṉaṭikaḷ varunta āḷānāṉ irukkumiṭam atutēṭi naṭantē aṇikkatavan tiṟappittuḷ eṉpoṭeṉai aḻaittu vāḷānī mayaṅkātē makaṉē-iṅ kitaṉai vāṅkikkoḷ eṉṟeṉatu malarkkaitaṉiṟ koṭuttāy kēḷāyeṉ uyirttuṇaiyāyk kiḷarmaṉṟil vēta kītanaṭam purikiṉṟa nātamuṭip poruḷē.
translation: Even the one who stood as the vast primal source searched for a long time but could never see your feet. Yet your feet endured hardship as you walked and sought the place where I dwell, though I am unfit to be your servant. You opened the beautiful door, called me inside with love, and said, "Do not be bewildered in vain, my son. Receive this." You placed it directly into my lotus hand. Listen, O companion of my life, you are the ultimate reality of sound who dances to Vedic songs in the radiant hall.
commentary: The supreme being addresses the seeker with absolute tenderness, calling him a son and telling him not to be confused. Even though the oldest gods searched the universe in vain for this truth, it arrives right at the poet's door. The ultimate reality is not something distant to be hunted down. It is a loving companion that comes directly to the soul to offer comfort and clarity.

translit: catta-oru vāmaṟaippoṟ cilampaṇintam palattē taṉinaṭañcey taruḷumaṭit tāmaraikaḷ varunta citta-uru vāki-iṅkē eṉaittēṭi naṭantu terukkatavan tiṟappitteṉ ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittu matta-uru vāmaṉattāl mayakkamuṟēl makaṉē makiḻntuṟaika eṉattiruvāy malarntakuṇa malaiyē cutta-uru vāyccutta aruvāki aḻiyāc cutta-aru uruvāṉa cuttaparam poruḷē.
translation: O Pure Supreme Reality! You are pure form, pure formlessness, and the indestructible pure form-and-formlessness. O Mountain of Virtues! Your lotus feet, adorned with golden anklets of the resounding Vedas, perform the unique dance in the Hall. Letting those lotus feet suffer, You took a physical form and walked here searching for me. You had the street door opened and placed a unique thing in my hands. You opened Your sacred mouth and said, "My son, do not be bewildered by your maddening mind. Rejoice."
commentary: God steps out of the transcendent realm to become deeply personal. Taking a physical form, the Divine walks through the streets to find a struggling soul, offering a tangible gift of grace to quiet the restless mind.

translit: palakōṭi maṟaikaḷelām ulakōṭi mayaṅkap paranāta muṭinaṭikkum pātamalar varuntac cilakōṭi naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṇaintu terukkatavan tiṟappitteṉ ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittē alakōṭi varuntēliṅ kamarka-eṉat tiruvāy alarnta-aruṭ kuruvēpoṉ ṉampalattem aracē vilakōṭi eṉattuyarkaḷ oṉṟoṭoṉṟu pukaṉṟu viraintōṭac ceytaṉai-iv viḷaivaṟiyēṉ viyappē.
translation: O Guru of Grace! O our King of the Golden Hall! While countless crores of Vedas run across the world in bewilderment, Your lotus feet dance on the crown of the supreme sound. Letting those lotus feet suffer, You walked a great distance, reached the place where I, a poor wretch, live, and opened the street door. Placing a unique thing in my hands, You opened Your sacred mouth and said, "Do not run aimlessly and suffer. Rest here." You made my sorrows scatter swiftly, telling each other to move aside and run away. I do not comprehend this wonderful outcome.
commentary: The ancient scriptures, known as the Vedas, search for the Divine in bewilderment. Yet God easily walks straight to the humblest devotee, bringing a direct experience of grace that instantly scatters all worldly sorrow and aimless searching.

translit: ceyvakai-oṉ ṟaṟiyātu tikaippiṉoṭē iruntēṉ tiṭukkeṉa-iṅ keḻuntiruppat terukkatavan tiṟappit tuyvakai-oṉ ṟeṉatukarat tuvantaḷittu makaṉē uykamakiḻn tiṉṟumutal oṉṟumañcēl eṉṟu meyvakaiyil pukaṉṟapiṉṉum añciyirun tēṉai mīṭṭumiṉṟai iraviluṇar vūṭṭi-accan tavirttāy aivakaiyāy niṉṟumaṉṟil āṭukiṉṟa aracē aṟputattāḷ malarvaruttam aṭaintaṉa-eṉ poruṭṭē.
translation: O King who stands as the fivefold functions and dances in the Hall! I sat in bewilderment, not knowing what to do. Startled, I stood up when You opened the street door. You joyfully placed a means of salvation in my hands. Even after You spoke the truth to me, saying, "My son, rejoice and be saved, and from today onward fear nothing," I remained afraid. Tonight, You awakened my realization once more and completely removed my fear. Your wonderful lotus feet suffered just for my sake.
commentary: Even when divine grace is first offered, human fear and doubt can linger. The Divine does not abandon the fearful soul, but returns again in the night to awaken deep inner realization and erase all terror completely.

translit: uḷḷiravi matiyāyniṉ ṟulakamelām naṭattum upayavakai yākiyaniṉ apayapatam varunta naḷḷiraviṉ mikanaṭantu nāṉirukkum iṭattē naṭaikkatavan tiṟappittu naṭaikkaṭaiyil aḻaittu eḷḷiravu niṉaintumayak keytiyiṭēl makaṉē eṉṟeṉkai taṉiloṉṟai īntumakiḻ vittāy aḷḷiravu pōlmiṭaṟṟil aḻakukiṟarn tāṭa ampalattil āṭukiṉṟa cempavaḷak kuṉṟē.
translation: O Hill of Red Coral dancing in the Hall, while the beauty of Your throat, dark as the pitch-black night, sways gracefully! Your protective feet act as the inner sun and moon, sustaining all the worlds. Letting those feet suffer, You walked a great distance in the dead of night to where I live. You opened the entrance door, called me to the porch, and said, "My son, do not harbor even a sesame seed of worry and become bewildered." You placed a unique thing in my hands and filled me with joy.
commentary: The same cosmic feet that sustain the entire universe as the sun and moon are willing to walk through the dead of night for a single person. God arrives in the darkness just to comfort a worried devotee and replace their anxiety with pure joy.

translit: viḷaṅkaṟivuk kaṟivāki meytturiya nilattē viḷaiyumaṉu pavamayamām mellaṭikaḷ varuntat tuḷaṅkuciṟi yēṉirukkum iṭantēṭi naṭantu toṭarkkatavan tiṟappittut toḻumpaṉeṉai aḻaittuk kaḷaṅkamilā oṉṟeṉatu kaitaṉilē koṭuttuk kaḷittuṟaika eṉattiruvāk kaḷitta-aruṭ kaṭalē kuḷaṅkoḷviḻip peruntakaiyē maṇimaṉṟil naṭañcey kurumaṇiyē aṉparmaṉak kōyililvāḻ kuruvē.
translation: O Ocean of Grace! O Great One with eyes brimming with compassion! O Master Jewel who dances in the Hall of Gems! O Guru who lives in the temple of Your devotees' hearts! Your soft feet are the intelligence within shining intelligence and the embodiment of experience blossoming in the true state of Turiya. Letting those feet suffer, You searched and walked to the place where I, a trembling little wretch, live. You opened the linked doors, called out to Your servant, and placed a flawless thing in my hands. You granted me Your sacred word, saying, "Stay in joy."
commentary: God is the deepest awareness hidden inside human intelligence. The state of Turiya is a profound level of spiritual consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. The Lord brings this supreme experience directly to the devotee's doorstep, offering flawless grace and commanding them to live in joy.

translit: vētamuṭi mēṟcuṭarāy ākattiṉ muṭimēl viḷaṅkumoḷi yākiyaniṉ mellaṭikaḷ varuntap pūtamuṭi mēlnaṭantu nāṉirukku miṭattē pōntiraviṟ katavutaṉaik kāppaviḻkkap purintu nātamuṭi mēlviḷaṅkun tirumēṉi kāṭṭi naṟporuḷeṉ kaitaṉilē nalkiyaniṉ perumai ōtamuṭi yāteṉileṉ pukalvēṉam palattē uyirkkiṉpan taranaṭaṉam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē.
translation: Supreme reality performing the dance in the Hall to grant bliss to souls! Your soft feet, which are the flame atop the crown of the Vedas and the shining light atop the Agamas, suffered as you walked upon the crown of the elements and came to the place where I was in the night. You caused the locks of the door to open, showed your sacred form that shines atop the crown of Nada, and placed the good substance into my hand. If your greatness cannot be fully spoken, what can I say?
commentary: The supreme divine light, which sits above the ancient scriptures known as the Vedas and Agamas, steps down into the physical world. The same feet that rest above the fundamental elements and the primordial sound of creation (Nada) willingly suffer the pain of walking to reach a locked door in the night. God personally opens the lock and places a tangible, sacred gift into the hands of the seeker.

translit: taṅkucarā caramuḻutum aḷittaruḷi naṭattun tāḷmalarkaḷ mikavaruntat taṉittunaṭan torunāḷ kaṅkulilyāṉ irukkumaṉaik katavutiṟap pittuk kaiyiloṉṟu koṭutta-uṉṟaṉ karuṇaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ iṅkuciṟi yēṉpiḻaikaḷ ettaṉaiyum poṟutta eṉkuruvē eṉuyiruk kiṉparuḷum poruḷē tiṅkaḷaṇi caṭaippavaḷac ceḻuñcōti malaiyē civakāma vallimakiḻ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Lord of the sacred dance who delights Sivakama Valli! Rich mountain of light like coral with matted hair adorned with the moon! My Guru who forgave all the countless faults of this lowly one here! Substance that grants bliss to my soul! One night, your lotus feet, which create, grace, and direct all the moving and unmoving things that exist, suffered greatly as you walked alone. You made the door of the house where I was open in the dark of night, and you gave something into my hand. How can I describe your compassion?
commentary: The divine force that creates and sustains every moving and unmoving thing in the universe takes on the intimate role of a personal teacher. Walking alone in the dark of night, God allows his own feet to suffer just to reach someone who feels entirely unworthy. By opening the door and placing a gift in his hand, God shows a compassion that forgives all past mistakes.

translit: māmāyai acaintiṭacciṟ ṟampalattē naṭittum varuntāta malaraṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taruḷi āmāṟaṉ ṟiraviṉiṭai aṇikkatavan tiṟappit taṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittiṉinī añcēleṉ ṟuvantu tēmāviṉ paḻampiḻintu vaṭittunaṟu neyyun tēṉumokkak kalantateṉat tiruvārttai aḷittāy kōmāṉniṉ aruṭperumai eṉuraippēṉ potuvil kūttāṭi eṅkaḷai-āṭ koṇṭaparam poruḷē.
translation: Supreme substance who dances in the common hall and rules us! Your lotus feet do not suffer even while dancing in the hall of consciousness causing the great Maya to move. Yet those feet suffered as you graciously walked. On that night, you caused the beautiful door to open, placed something in my palm, and happily said, "Do not fear anymore." You gave me sacred words that were like squeezing and filtering the fruit of a sweet mango and mixing it with fragrant ghee and honey. O King, how can I express the greatness of your grace?
commentary: God dances effortlessly to move the entire physical universe and its illusions, known as Maya, without his feet ever hurting. Yet those same feet suffer when he walks simply to comfort a human being. The divine presence hands over a gift and speaks words of total reassurance, telling him never to fear again in a voice sweeter than fresh fruit mixed with honey and fragrant ghee.

translit: paṭaippavaṉuṅ kāppavaṉum paṟpalanāḷ muyaṉṟu pārkkavirum piṉuṅkiṭaiyāp pātamalar varunta naṭaippulaiyēṉ poruṭṭāka naṭattiraviṟ katavam naṉkutiṟap pittoṉṟu nalkiyatum aṉṟi iṭaippaṭunā ḷiṉumvanteṉ itayamayak kellām irintiṭaccey taṉai-uṉṟaṉ iṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ taṭaippaṭumā ṟillāta pēriṉpap perukkē taṉimaṉṟil āṉantat tāṇṭavañcey aracē.
translation: King performing the dance of bliss in the unique hall! Flood of supreme bliss that knows no obstacle! Your lotus feet cannot be attained even if the creator and the protector desire and try to see them for many days. Yet those feet suffered as you walked for the sake of this lowly wretch. In the night, you made the door open properly, granted me something, and besides that, you came in the intervening days and made all the confusion of my heart vanish. How can I describe your sweet grace?
commentary: The traditional gods of creation and protection spend lifetimes trying to catch a single glimpse of the supreme divine, but they cannot. That same ultimate reality willingly walks through the night to reach an ordinary person. Along with the physical gift placed in his hand, this nightly visit brings an inner grace that wipes away all mental confusion and doubt.

translit: muṉṉaimaṟai muṭimaṇiyām aṭimalarkaḷ varunta muḻutiravil naṭanteḷiyēṉ muyaṅkamiṭat taṭaintu aṉṉaiyiṉum parintaruḷi aṇikkatavan tiṟappit taṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷitteṉaiyum aṉpiṉoṭu nōkki eṉṉai-iṉi mayaṅkātē eṉmakaṉē makiḻvō ṭirutti-eṉa uraittāyniṉ iṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ miṉṉainikar ceñcaṭaimēṉ matiyamacain tāṭa viyaṉpotuvil tirunaṭañcey vimalaparam poruḷē.
translation: Pure supreme substance performing the sacred dance in the vast common hall while the moon sways on your red matted hair that resembles lightning! Your lotus feet, the crown jewels of the ancient Vedas, suffered as you walked in the dead of night and reached the place where I, a poor soul, was residing. Showering more affection than a mother, you made the beautiful door open, gave something into my palm, looked at me with love, and said, "Do not be confused anymore, my son, remain in joy." How can I express your sweet grace?
commentary: The ultimate reality approaches the seeker with an affection far deeper than that of a human mother. God arrives in the dead of night, opens the locked door, and offers both a gift and a loving gaze. The supreme force of the universe calls him "my son" and tells him to leave all confusion behind and live in pure joy.

translit: mītāṉat taruḷoḷiyāy viḷaṅkiyaniṉ aṭikaḷ mikavarunta naṭantiravil viṉaiyēṉṟaṉ poruṭṭāc cītāṉak katavutaṉait tiṟappittuc ciṟiyēṉ ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittiṉinī ciṟitumañcēl iṅku mātāṉat tavarcūḻa vāḻka-eṉa uraittāy māmaṇiniṉ tiruvaruḷiṉ vaṇmai-evark kuḷatē ōtāṉat tavartamakkum uṇarvaritām poruḷē ōṅkiyaciṟ ṟampalattē oḷinaṭañcey patiyē.
translation: O Lord who performs the dance of light in the lofty Chitrambalam. O Reality difficult to realize even for those who chant and meditate. Your feet shine as the light of grace in the supreme state. For the sake of this karmic one, you walked in the night and caused great pain to your feet. You made the glorious door open, placed something in the red hands of this lowly one, and said, "Fear no more. Live here surrounded by great generous people." O great gem, who else possesses the bounty of your holy grace?
commentary: Vallalar describes a direct, intimate encounter with the Divine, who descends from the cosmic hall of consciousness (Chitrambalam). He says the Lord walked through the night, suffering the physical pain of the journey, just to reach him. Opening the door, the Divine placed a gift in Vallalar's hand and spoke words of comfort and blessing, taking away all his fear.

translit: vētānta cittāntam eṉṉumantam iraṇṭum viḷaṅka-amarn taruḷiyaniṉ mellaṭikaḷ varunta nātānta veḷitaṉilē naṭantaruḷum atupōl naṭantaruḷik kaṭaināyēṉ naṇṇumiṭat taṭaintu pōtānta micaiviḷakkun tirumēṉi kāṭṭip pulaiyēṉkai yiṭattoṉṟu poruntavaitta poruḷē cūtānta maṉaittiṉukkum appāṟpaṭ ṭirunta turiyaveḷik kēviḷaṅkum periya-aruṭ kuruvē.
translation: O great Guru of grace who shines in the transcendent space of Turiya beyond all boundaries of deception. Your soft feet rest graciously to illuminate both ends known as Vedanta and Siddhanta. Causing pain to those feet, you walked just as you graciously walk in the space beyond sound. You reached the place where this lowest dog resides, revealed your holy form that shines above the culmination of consciousness, and fittingly placed something in the hand of this base one, O Reality.
commentary: The Lord who stands above the highest philosophical schools of Vedanta and Siddhanta comes to Vallalar in a deeply personal way. Though the Divine exists in turiya (the state of awareness beyond ordinary waking, dreaming, and deep sleep) and beyond the limits of sound, he takes on a visible form. Reaching out to a devotee who feels unworthy, God physically hands him a gift of grace.

translit: orumaiyilē irumai-eṉa urukkāṭṭip potuvil oḷinaṭañcey taruḷukiṉṟa upayapatam varunta arumaiyilē naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintē aṇikkatavan tiṟappitteṉ aṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittup perumaiyilē piṟaṅkukanī eṉattiruvāy malarnta peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭalēniṉ peṟṟiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ karumaiyilē neṭuṅkālaṅ kalantukalak kuṟṟa kalakkamelān tavirttemmaik kāttaruḷum patiyē.
translation: O Lord who protects us and dispels all the confusion caused by mingling in darkness for a long time. Your two feet graciously perform the dance of light in the common hall, revealing duality within oneness. Causing pain to those feet, you walked with great difficulty and reached the place where this simple one resides. You opened the beautiful door, placed something in my palm, and opened your holy mouth to say, "May you shine in greatness." O ocean of great compassion, what can I say of your nature?
commentary: Vallalar marvels at the boundless compassion of God, who steps out of his cosmic dance of light to seek out a single struggling soul. The Divine brings clarity into the long darkness of worldly confusion, speaking a direct blessing of greatness while placing a physical gift in Vallalar's palm.

translit: vintunilai nātanilai irunilaikkum aracāy viḷaṅkiyaniṉ cēvaṭikaḷ mikavarunta naṭantu vantunilai peṟacciṟiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu maṇikkatavan tiṟappittu makaṉē-eṉ ṟaḻaittu intunilai muṭimutarān tiru-uruvaṅ kāṭṭi eṉkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittiṉpam eytuka-eṉ ṟuraittāy muntunilaic ciṟiyēṉcey tavamaṟiyēṉ potuvil muttarmaṉan tittikka niruttamiṭum poruḷē.
translation: O Reality who dances in the common hall so the minds of the liberated ones taste sweetness. Your red feet shine as the sovereign of both the state of Bindu and the state of Nada. Walking until they suffered great pain, you firmly arrived at the place where this small one resides. You opened the jeweled door, called out to me, "O son," and revealed your holy form crowned with the moon. You placed something in my hand and said, "Attain bliss." I do not know what penance this small one performed in the past to deserve this.
commentary: Here, God approaches not as a distant ruler, but as a loving parent. Though he is the sovereign of the cosmic principles of creation, bindu (light) and nāda (sound), the Lord calls Vallalar his "son" and tells him to find joy. Vallalar is overwhelmed by this tender visit, wondering what unknown good deeds from his past could have possibly earned it.

translit: navanilaikkum atikāram naṭattukiṉṟa aracāy naṇṇiyaniṉ poṉṉaṭikaḷ naṭantuvarun tiṭavē avanilaikkuṅ kaṭaippulaiyēṉ irukkumiṭat tiravil aṇaintaruḷik katavutiṟan taṭiyēṉai aḻaittē civanilaikkum paṭi-eṉatu ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittuc cittamakiḻn tuṟaika-eṉat tiruppavaḷan tiṟantāy pavanilaikkuṅ kaṭaināyēṉ payiṉṟatavam aṟiyēṉ paramparamā maṉṟilnaṭam payiṉṟapacu patiyē.
translation: O Pasupati who performs the dance in the supreme transcendent hall. Your golden feet approach as the sovereign wielding authority over all nine states. Causing them pain, you walked and graciously arrived at night at the place where this lowest base one of a ruined state resides. You opened the door, called out to this devotee, and placed something in my red hand so I could attain the state of Siva. Opening your coral lips, you said, "Reside here with a joyful heart." I, this lowest dog caught in the cycle of worldly existence, do not know what penance I practiced to receive this.
