commentary: Even though the Divine rules over all levels of existence, he willingly walks through the night to visit a devotee who feels entirely worthless. By handing over a gift meant to elevate Vallalar to the divine state of Siva, God shows that his grace reaches out to uplift the lowliest. Vallalar addresses him as Paśupati, the Lord and protector of all living souls.

translit: puṇṇiyartam maṉakkōyil pukuntamarntu viḷaṅkum poṉmalarccē vaṭivaruttam poruntanaṭan teḷiyēṉ naṇṇiya-ōr iṭattaṭaintu katavutiṟap pittu naṟporuḷoṉ ṟeṉkaitaṉil nalkiyaniṉ perumai eṇṇiyapō tellāmeṉ maṉamurukkum eṉṟāl emperumāṉ niṉaruḷai eṉṉeṉayāṉ pukalvēṉ taṇṇiyaveṇ mati-aṇinta ceñcaṭainiṉ ṟāṭat taṉittamaṉṟil āṉantat tāṇṭavañcey aracē.
translation: O King who performs the dance of bliss in the solitary hall while Your red matted hair, adorned with the cool white moon, dances along. Your beautiful golden lotus feet that enter and shine in the temple of virtuous hearts grew weary as You walked to where I, a poor wretch, stay. You had the door opened and placed a good substance into my hands. If thinking of Your greatness melts my heart every time, how can I describe Your grace, my Lord?
commentary: Vallalar describes a profound mystical experience where the Divine personally seeks him out. Instead of the devotee taking a difficult pilgrimage to God, God walks through the night, wearying His own feet, simply to knock on a poor poet's door and hand him a divine gift. The overwhelming intimacy of this grace leaves his heart melting.

translit: mūvarukkum eṭṭātu mūttatiru aṭikaḷ muḻutiravil varuntiyiṭa muyaṅkinaṭan taruḷi yāvarukkum iḻintēṉiṅ kirukkumiṭat taṭaintē eḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittuḷ eṉai-aḻaittu makaṉē tēvarukkum arititaṉai vāṅkeṉa-eṉ karattē cittamakiḻn taḷittaṉainiṉ tiruvaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ pūvarukkum poḻiṟṟillai ampalattē naṭaṉam purintuyiruk kiṉparuḷum pūraṇavāṉ poruḷē.
translation: O Perfect Great Reality who dances in the hall of Thillai surrounded by blossoming groves and grants bliss to souls. Your ancient holy feet, unattainable even by the three gods, grew weary in the deep night as You walked with difficulty to grace me. You reached the place where I, the lowest of all, stay, had the beautiful door opened, called me inside, and joyfully placed something in my hands, saying, "Son, receive this which is rare even for the gods." How can I describe Your holy grace?
commentary: The supreme Reality bypasses the highest traditional gods to visit a humble human being. Vallalar marvels that feet unattainable by the cosmic deities of creation, preservation, and destruction grew tired walking through the dark to find him. By calling him "son" and offering a secret denied even to the heavens, God shows that divine love reaches directly for the lowest and most desperate, ignoring all hierarchies.

translit: kaṟṟavartam karuttiṉiṉmuk kaṉiracampōl iṉikkum kaḻalaṭikaḷ varuntiyiṭak kaṭitunaṭan tiravil maṟṟavarkā ṇāteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu maṉaikkatavu tiṟappittu valinteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittu naṟṟavarkkum arititaṉai vāṅkeṉa-eṉ karattē nalkiyaniṉ peruṅkaruṇai naṭpiṉai-eṉ eṉpēṉ aṟṟavarkkum paṟṟavarkkum potuviṉilē naṭañcey aruṭkuruvē caccitā ṉantaparam poruḷē.
translation: O Guru of Grace who dances in the common hall for both the detached and the attached. O Supreme Reality of Existence, Consciousness, and Bliss. Your anklet-adorned feet, sweet as the juice of the three fruits in the minds of the learned, grew weary as You walked swiftly in the night. Unseen by others, You reached the place where I, a poor wretch, dwell, had the house door opened, compelled me to approach You, and placed something in my hands, saying, "Receive this which is rare even for great ascetics." How can I describe the friendship of Your immense compassion?
commentary: God is the ultimate reality of existence, consciousness, and bliss, dancing equally for those bound by the world and those entirely free from it. Vallalar notes that the divine feet are as sweet as the traditional three fruits (mango, jackfruit, and banana), yet they walked unseen through the dark to find him. The wonder here is that a grace sought by great ascetics through lifelong struggle was brought directly to his house as an act of pure friendship.

translit: karuṇaivaṭi vāyaṭiyār uḷḷakattē amarnta kaḻalaṭikaḷ varuntiyiṭak kaṅkulilē naṭantu maruṇiṟaiyuñ ciṟiyēṉnāṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu maṇikkatavan tiṟappittu makiḻntaḻaittu makaṉē poruṇiṟaiyum itaṉai-iṅkē vāṅkeṉa-eṉ karattē porunta-aḷit taruḷiyaniṉ poṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ aruṇiṟaiyum peruṅkaṭalē ampalattil paramā ṉantavuru vākinaṭam āṭukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: O great ocean full of grace. O King who dances as the form of supreme bliss in the hall. Your anklet-adorned feet, which sit as the form of compassion within the hearts of devotees, grew weary as You walked in the night. You reached the place where I, a small one filled with delusion, stay, had the jeweled door opened, joyfully called me, and properly placed something in my hands, saying, "Son, receive this which is full of meaning right here." How can I describe Your golden grace?
commentary: The Divine is an ocean of grace that actively pursues the lost soul. Even though Vallalar describes his own mind as small and clouded with delusion, God still arrives in the night to open his door and hand him a gift full of true meaning. It is a plain reminder that spiritual awakening is given freely by a compassionate God, not earned by a flawless mind.

translit: aruḷuruvāy aintoḻilum naṭattukiṉṟa aṭikaḷ acaintuvarun tiṭa-iravil yāṉirukkum iṭattē teruḷuruviṉ naṭantuteruk katavutiṟap pittuc ciṟiyēṉai aḻaitteṉatu ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittu maruḷuruviṉ maṟṟavarpōl mayaṅkēleṉ makaṉē makiḻntutiru aruḷvaḻiyē vārka-eṉa uraittāy iruḷuruviṉ maṉakkoṭiyēṉ yātutavam purintēṉ ellāmval lavaṉāki iruntapacu patiyē.
translation: O Lord of souls who remains all-powerful. Your feet, which perform the five cosmic acts in the form of grace, swayed and grew weary in the night as You walked to my place in a form of clarity. You had the street door opened, called me, a small one, and placed something into my red hands. You said, "My son, do not be deluded like others who embody ignorance. Come joyfully along the path of holy grace." What penance did I, a cruel-hearted one trapped in the form of darkness, ever perform to deserve this?
commentary: God reveals the purpose behind this midnight visitation by giving a direct command. Placing a gift in Vallalar's hands, the Lord tells him to leave behind the ignorance that traps ordinary people and to walk joyfully on the path of grace. The poet is left entirely humbled, wondering what he could possibly have done to deserve such a direct, personal rescue by the ruler of the universe.

translit: muḻutumuṇarn tavarmuṭimēl muṭikkumaṇi yāki mupporuḷu mākiyaniṉ oppilaṭi malarkaḷ kaḻutumuṇar variyanaṭuk kaṅkulilē varuntak kaṭitunaṭan taṭināyēṉ karutumiṭat taṭaintu paḻutupaṭā vaṇṇameṉaip parintaḻaittu makaṉē paṇintitaṉai vāṅkeṉa-eṉ pāṇiyuṟak koṭuttut toḻuteṉaippā ṭuka-eṉṟu coṉṉapacu patiniṉ tūya-aruṭ perumaiyai-eṉ colliviyak kēṉē .
translation: Your incomparable lotus feet are the three ultimate truths, and they become the crowning gem on the heads of those who have fully realized everything. You walked swiftly so that those feet suffered in the deep midnight, a time even ghouls cannot comprehend, and you reached the place where I, a lowly dog, dwell. Affectionately calling me "Son" so I would remain flawless, you placed something in my hands and said, "Bow and receive this." You commanded, "Worship and sing of me." O Pasupati, how can I ever speak of and marvel at the greatness of your pure grace?
commentary: The Lord of all souls comes directly to a humble home in the dead of night to deliver a gift and a command. Addressed as Pasupati (the Lord of all beings), the divine presence walks through the dark, calls the poet "Son," and places something directly into his hands with the instruction to sing. The ultimate truth humbles itself to seek out a devotee when the rest of the world is asleep.

translit: māṉiṉaitta aḷavellāṅ kaṭantappāl vayaṅkum malaraṭikaḷ varuntiyiṭa makiḻntunaṭan taruḷip pāṉiṉaitta ciṟiyēṉnāṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu paṇaikkatavan tiṟappittup parintaḻaittu makaṉē nīniṉaitta vaṇṇamelāṅ kaikūṭum itu-ōr niṉmalameṉ ṟeṉkaitaṉil nērntaḷittāy niṉakku nāṉiṉaitta naṉṟi-oṉṟum ilaiyēniṉ aruḷai nāyaṭiyēṉ eṉpukalvēṉ naṭarāja maṇiyē .
translation: O gem-like Nataraja! Your lotus feet shine far beyond every measure conceived by the mind. You walked joyfully so that those feet suffered and reached the place where I, a small one who yearned for milk, reside. You made the thick wooden door open. You affectionately called me "Son" and placed something directly in my hand, saying, "Everything you wished for will be fulfilled, and this is a flawless thing." I have not conceived of a single way to repay you. How can I, a lowly dog, express your grace?
commentary: The divine being, addressed as Nataraja (the Lord of the cosmic dance), performs an intimately personal act of grace. The limitless God walks through the night, physically opens a heavy wooden door, and offers a flawless gift with the promise that every wish will be fulfilled. This captures the overwhelming gratitude of receiving divine love that is completely unearned.

translit: cūriyacan tirarellān tōṉṟāmai viḷaṅkum cuyañcōti yākumaṭit tuṇaivarunta naṭantu kūriyamey aṟiveṉpa toruciṟituṅ kuṟiyāk koṭiyēṉnāṉ irukkumiṭaṅ kuṟittiravil naṭantu kāriyamuṇ ṭeṉakkūvik katavutiṟap pittuk kaiyil oṉṟai aḷittaṉai-uṉ karuṇaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ āriyartam aḷavukaṭan tappāluṅ kaṭanta āṉanta maṉṟilnaṭam āṭukiṉṟa aracē .
translation: O King who dances in the hall of bliss, far beyond the measure of the noble sages and beyond even that! You walked so that your twin feet, the self-luminous Jothi that outshines the sun and moon, suffered. You walked in the night to the exact place where I, a cruel one with not the slightest trace of sharp true knowledge, reside. Calling out, "I have a task for you," you made the door open and gave something into my hand. What can I say of your compassion?
commentary: The supreme divine light, or Jothi, outshines both the sun and the moon. Yet this ultimate reality chooses to walk through the darkness to find someone who feels ignorant and entirely unworthy. God opens the door and announces a specific task. Divine grace saves the soul and immediately gives it a vital purpose in the world.

translit: taṟpōtan tōṉṟāta talantaṉilē tōṉṟum tāḷmalarkaḷ varuntiyiṭat taṉittunaṭan taruḷi eṟpōtaṅ kakaṉṟiravil yāṉirukku miṭampōn teḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittiv veḷiyēṉai aḻaittup poṟpōta vaṇṇamoṉṟeṉ kaitaṉilē aḷittup pulaiyoḻinta nilaitaṉilē poruntuka-eṉ ṟuraittāy ciṟpōta mayamāṉa tirumaṇimaṉ ṟiṭattē civamayamām aṉupōkat tirunaṭañcey aracē
translation: O King who performs the divine dance of blissful experience filled with Sivam in the holy gem hall of pure consciousness! Your lotus feet appear in the realm where the ego does not arise. You graciously walked alone so that those feet suffered and came in the night, when sunlight had gone, to the place where I reside. You made the beautiful door open and called this lowly one. You gave something of golden beauty into my hand and said, "Settle into a state free from impurity."
commentary: The presence of God only appears in the space where human ego completely vanishes. Here, the divine brings a beautiful gift in the dark and issues a clear instruction to live in a state entirely free from impurity. This state is filled with Sivam, the supreme divine reality, transforming the soul into pure consciousness.

translit: kaṟpaṉaikaḷ ellāmpōyk karaintatalan taṉilē karaiyātu niṟaintiruk kaḻalaṭikaḷ varunta veṟpaṉaiyum iṉṟi-oru taṉiyāka naṭantu viraintiraviṟ katavutaṉaik kāppaviḻkkap purintu aṟpaṉai-ōr poruḷāka aḻaittaruḷi aṭiyēṉ aṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittaṉainiṉ aruḷiṉai-eṉ pukalvēṉ naṟpaṉavar tutikkamaṇi maṉṟakattē iṉpa naṭampuriyum peruṅkaruṇai nāyakamā maṇiyē .
translation: O great Gem, the supremely compassionate Lord who dances in bliss in the gem hall while good sages offer praise! Your ankleted feet rest fully and immortally in the realm where all mental fabrications dissolve and vanish. You walked completely alone without a companion so that those feet suffered. You swiftly came in the night and caused the door's lock to open. Treating me, a worthless one, as someone of worth, you graciously called me and placed something in my palm. How can I ever speak of your grace?
commentary: True spiritual reality exists only in the place where all human imagination and mental fabrications melt away. Leaving behind the praises of the sages, the divine walks entirely alone to unlock a closed door for someone the world might consider worthless. Grace ignores human status, treating the lowest individual as a treasure worthy of a personal visit.

translit: oṉṟāki iraṇṭāki oṉṟiraṇṭiṉ naṭuvē uṟṟa-aṉu pavamayamāy oḷiraṭikaḷ varunta aṉṟāra naṭantiravil yāṉuṟaiyum iṭattē aṭaintukata vantiṟappit taṉpoṭeṉai aḻaittu naṉṟāra eṉatukarat toṉṟaruḷi iṅkē naṇṇanī eṇṇiyavā naṭattuka-eṉ ṟaraittāy iṉṟāra vantataṉai uṇarttiṉainiṉ aruḷai eṉpukalvēṉ maṇimaṉṟil ilaṅkicaṟ kuruvē .
translation: O true Guru shining in the hall of gems! Your shining feet become one, become two, and become the pure experience between one and two. Letting those feet suffer, you walked through the night on that day and reached my dwelling place. You caused the door to open, called me with love, and graciously placed a good thing in my hand. You told me, "Approach here and conduct things just as you intend." Today you came and made me realize this. How can I describe your grace?
commentary: God's presence encompasses everything, holding total unity, the diversity of the world, and the direct experience that bridges them together. By walking through the night to hand him a gift and telling him to lead exactly as he sees fit, the Divine gives him complete spiritual authority. This shows that true guidance comes from a direct, personal encounter with grace rather than inherited tradition.

translit: eṅkumviḷaṅ kuvatāki iṉpamaya māki eṉṉuṇarvuk kuṇarvutarum iṇaiyaṭikaḷ varunta poṅkumira viṭainaṭantu nāṉuṟaiyum iṭattē pōntumaṇik katavutaṉaik kāppaviḻkkap purintu taṅkumaṭi yēṉai-aḻait taṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittē tayaviṉoṭu vāḻka-eṉat taṉittiruvāy malarntāy iṅkuniṉa taruṭperumai eṉṉuraippēṉ potuvil iṉpanaṭam purikiṉṟa eṉṉuṭainā yakaṉē .
translation: O my Lord who performs the blissful dance in the common hall! Your peerless feet shine everywhere, embody pure bliss, and grant feeling to my feeling. Letting those feet suffer, you walked through the deep swelling night and arrived at my dwelling. You caused the lock on the jeweled door to open. You called this servant who abides there, placed something in my palm, and compassionately opened your sacred mouth to say, "May you live long." How can I express the greatness of your grace here?
commentary: The Divine is the very awareness inside our own awareness. Vallalar describes a God who is completely intimate and personal. Walking through the dark to bless him with a long life, the Divine shows a tender, immediate care for the individual soul.

translit: cittevaiyum viyattiyuṟuñ cuttaciva cittāyc cittamatil tittikkun tiruvaṭikaḷ varunta matta-ira viṭainaṭantu vantaruḷi aṭiyēṉ vāḻumaṉait terukkatavu tiṟappittaṅ kaṭaintu attakaviṉ eṉai-aḻaitteṉ aṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittāy aṉṉaiyiṉum aṉpuṭaiyāy niṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ muttarkuḻuk kāṇamaṉṟil iṉpanaṭam puriyum mukkaṇuṭai āṉantac cekkarmaṇi malaiyē .
translation: O mountain of joyous red rubies with three eyes, performing the blissful dance in the hall for the assembly of liberated souls to witness! Your sacred feet are the pure supreme consciousness where all other consciousness manifests, and they taste sweet in the mind. Letting those feet suffer, you graciously walked through the dark night, reached the street door of the house where your servant lives, and caused it to open. Arriving there, you gracefully called me and placed something in my palm. You possess more love than a mother. How can I describe your grace?
commentary: God is the foundation of all consciousness, making every thought and moment of awareness possible. Yet this supreme reality is never an unfeeling force. By seeking Vallalar out in the dark and placing a gift in his hand, God shows a deep tenderness that surpasses even the love of a mother.

translit: cakalamoṭu kēvalamun tākkāta iṭattē taṟparamāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tāḷmalarkaḷ varuntap pakaloḻiya naṭuviravil naṭantaruḷi aṭiyēṉ pariyumiṭat taṭaintumaṇik katavutiṟap pittup pukaluṟuka varuka-eṉa aḻaitteṉatu karattē porunta-oṉṟu koṭuttaṉainiṉ poṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ ukaloḻiyap peruntavarkaḷ uṟṟumakiḻn tētta uyarpotuvil iṉpanaṭam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē .
translation: O Supreme Reality who dances blissfully in the high common hall while great ascetics, freed from sorrow, gather to rejoice and praise you! Your lotus feet shine as the Supreme Reality in a space untouched by worldly entanglement and dark isolation. Letting those feet suffer, you graciously walked in the middle of the night after the day had passed. You reached my dwelling, caused the jeweled door to open, and called me, saying, "Come here." You fittingly placed something in my hand. How can I describe your golden grace?
commentary: True spiritual reality exists entirely apart from both worldly entanglement and dark, empty isolation. Vallalar points to a divine presence that is perfectly free from all extremes of human experience. Even while shining in that pure state, this supreme reality willingly steps into the darkness of the world to call and guide a devoted soul.

translit: uḷḷurukun taruṇattē oḷikāṭṭi viḷaṅkum uyarmalarccē vaṭivarunta uvantunaṭan taruḷik kaḷḷamaṉat tēṉirukkum intēṭi aṭaintu katavutiṟap pittaruḷik kaḷitteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittu naḷḷulakil uṉakkitunām nalkiṉamnī makiḻntu nāḷumuyirk kitampurintu naṭatti-eṉa uraittāy teḷḷumamu tāyaṉpar cittamelām iṉikkum ceḻuṅkaṉiyē maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭanā yakaṉē .
translation: O rich fruit that becomes clear ambrosia and sweetens the minds of all devotees! O Lord of the sacred dance in the hall of gems! Your supreme red lotus feet reveal the light and shine at the very moment the heart melts. Letting those feet suffer, you joyously walked and sought out the house where I live with my deceitful mind. Arriving there, you graciously caused the door to open and joyfully called me to you. You said, "We have given this to you in this world. Rejoice, and live by doing good to all living beings every day."
commentary: The divine light reveals itself the very moment the human heart melts with love. When the Divine finally hands over this great gift, the accompanying instruction is incredibly direct and practical. God tells Vallalar to rejoice and live by doing good to all living beings every single day. This continuous compassion for all life is known as Jeevakarunyam, and it is the absolute foundation of the spiritual path.

translit: taṉṉuruvaṅ kāṭṭāta mala-iravu viṭiyun taruṇattē utayañcey tāḷmalarkaḷ varuntap poṉṉuruvat tirumēṉi koṇṭunaṭan taṭiyēṉ poruntumiṭat taṭaintukata vantiṟakkap purintu taṉṉuruvam pōṉṟatoṉṟaṅ keṉai aḻaitteṉ karattē tantaruḷi makiḻntiṅkē taṅkuka-eṉ ṟuraittāy eṉṉuruvam eṉakkuṇartti aruḷiyaniṉ perumai eṉṉuraippēṉ maṇimaṉṟil iṉpanaṭat taracē.
translation: O King of the blissful dance in the ruby hall, at the moment the formless night of impurity came to an end, you walked with your golden sacred form while your rising lotus feet grew weary. You reached the place where I stay, made me open the door, called out to me, and placed into my hand something that resembled your own form. Delighted, you told me to stay here. How can I describe your greatness, you who made me realize my own true form?
commentary: Vallalar describes a direct mystical encounter where God seeks him out at the exact moment his spiritual ignorance ends. He pictures the divine walking until his feet grow weary, coming to his very door to hand him a gift that mirrors God's own nature. This gift awakens the poet to his own true self, showing that the soul's real form is divine light.

translit: aṇṭavakai piṇṭavakai aṉaittumutit toṭuṅkum aṇimalarccē vaṭivaruttam aṭaiyanaṭan taruḷik kaṇṭavaruṅ kāṇāta naṭu-iravu taṉilyāṉ karutumiṭat taṭaintukata vantiṟakkap purintu toṇṭaṉeṉ eṉaiyumaḻait teṉkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittāy turaiyēniṉ aruṭperumait toṇmaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ uṇṭavarkaḷ uṇuntōṟum uvaṭṭāta amutē uyarpotuvil iṉpanaṭam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē.
translation: O Supreme Reality performing the blissful dance in the high public hall, O nectar that never cloys no matter how much one consumes it. Your beautiful red lotus feet, from which all types of universes and physical bodies emerge and resolve, grew weary as you walked. In the middle of the night unseen by anyone, you reached my place, made me open the door, called me, your servant, and placed something in my hand. O Lord, how can I describe the ancient nature of your supreme grace?
commentary: The supreme reality that creates and dissolves entire universes humbles itself to walk in the dark to find a single servant. God visits in the secrecy of midnight, unseen by anyone else, making this spiritual awakening deeply intimate. The poet marvels at a grace that actively searches for the seeker.

translit: aṟivuṭaiyār uḷḷakappō talarukiṉṟa taruṇat taruḷmaṇattē ṉāki-uṟṟa aṭi-iṇaikaḷ varuntap piṟivuṭaiyēṉ irukkumiṭan tēṭinaṭan taṭaintu peruṅkatavan tiṟappittup pēyaṉeṉai aḻaittuc ceṟivuṭaiyāy ituvāṅkeṉ ṟutavavumnāṉ maṟuppat tirumpavumeṉ kaitaṉilē cēra-aḷit taṉaiyē poṟivaṟiyēṉ aḷaviṉiluṉ karuṇaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ poṟpotuvil naṭampuriyum pūraṇavāṉ poruḷē.
translation: O perfect heavenly Reality dancing in the golden hall. Your pair of feet, which manifest as the fragrant honey of grace when the inner lotus of the wise blossoms, grew weary. You searched, walked, and reached the place where I live separated from you. You had the great door opened, called me, a madman, and offered a gift saying, "O resolute one, take this." When I refused, you placed it once more into my hand. I am devoid of understanding. How can I express your boundless compassion?
commentary: The divine pursues the soul relentlessly, even when the soul feels unworthy and tries to decline the gift of grace. Vallalar calls himself a madman who initially rejects the offering, but God insists and places the gift directly into his hand. This shows a divine compassion that completely overrides human hesitation and ignorance.

translit: viṭaiyamoṉṟuṅ kāṇāta veḷinaṭuvē oḷiyāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cēvaṭikaḷ mikavarunta naṭantu kaṭaiyaṉaiyuṅ kuṟikkoṇṭu karutumiṭat taṭaintu katavutiṟap pitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭukka iṭaiyiṉatu nāṉmaṟuppu maṟukkēleṉ makaṉē eṉṟupiṉṉuṅ koṭuttāyniṉ iṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ uṭaiyaparam poruḷē-eṉ uyirttuṇaiyē potuvil uyyumvakai aruḷnaṭaṉañ ceyyumoḷi maṇiyē.
translation: O Supreme Reality who owns me, O companion of my life, O radiant gem performing the dance of grace in the public hall so that we may be saved. Your red feet, shining as light in the center of the vast expanse devoid of sensory objects, grew very weary from walking. Keeping even this lowest person in mind, you reached my dwelling, had the door opened, and offered something into my hand. When I refused it, you offered it again, saying, "Do not refuse, my son." How can I describe your sweet grace?
commentary: God exists in a pure realm of light far beyond the physical senses, yet deliberately steps down to seek out the lowliest person. When Vallalar tries to refuse the divine gift out of a sense of unworthiness, God simply says, "Do not refuse, my son." This tender address reveals a parental love that gently overcomes all resistance.

translit: nāṉtaṉikkun taraṇattē tōṉṟukiṉṟa tuṇaiyāy nāṉtaṉiyā iṭatteṉakkut tōṉṟāta tuṇaiyāy ēṉṟaruḷun tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taruḷi yāṉuṟaiyum iṭattaṭaintu katavutiṟap pittu āṉṟa-eṉai aḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttāyk kaṟivilayēṉ ceyyumvakai aṟiyēṉniṉ karuṇai īṉṟavaṭkum illai-eṉa naṉkaṟintēṉ potuvil iṉpanaṭam purikiṉṟa eṉṉuyirnā yakaṉē.
translation: O Lord of my life performing the blissful dance in the public hall. You are the companion who appears when I am alone, and the unseen companion when I am not alone. Your sacred feet that accept and bestow grace grew weary as you walked. You reached the place where I live, had the door opened, called me, and placed something in my hand. Lacking wisdom, I do not know what to do. I realized clearly that not even a mother possesses your level of compassion.
commentary: God is a constant companion who protects the soul in deep solitude. Looking at the sheer effort the divine makes to find him and bless him, Vallalar realizes this compassion far exceeds even a mother's love. It is God who takes the initiative, walking until his feet ache just to deliver salvation to a person completely lacking in wisdom.

translit: aruḷviḷaṅkum uḷḷakattē atu-atuvāy viḷaṅkum aṇimalarccē vaṭivaruttam aṭaiyanaṭan taruḷip poruḷviḷaṅkā naṭu-iravil nāṉuṟaiyum iṭattē pōntuteruk kāppaviḻkkap purinteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittut teruḷviḷaṅkum oruporuḷeṉ ceṅkaitaṉil aḷittāy civaperumāṉ peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattiṉai-eṉ eṉpēṉ maruḷviḷaṅki uṇarcciyuṟat tirumaṇimaṉ ṟiṭattē maṉṉuyirk kiṉparuḷa vayaṅkunaṭat taracē.
translation: O dancing King! You dance in the holy ruby hall to grant bliss to enduring souls, clearing their delusion and awakening true feeling. Your beautiful, lotus-like red feet, which manifest as all things within the grace-filled heart, grew weary as you graciously walked. In the dead of night when nothing could be seen, you came to where I live. You had the street door unlocked, called me there, and placed a shining object of wisdom into my red hands. What can I say of Lord Siva's immense grace?
commentary: God's compassion actively seeks out the soul, moving through the deepest darkness to awaken it. The verse recounts a profound personal moment where the Divine arrived at the poet's door in the dead of night, walking until his holy feet were weary, just to place a gift of spiritual clarity directly into his hands.

translit: paruvamuṟu taruṇattē carkkaraiyum tēṉum pāluneyyum aḷintanaṟum paḻaracamum pōla maruvumuḷam uyiruṇarvō ṭellāntit tikka vayaṅkumaṭi yiṇaikaḷmika varuntanaṭan taruḷit teruvaṭaintu nāṉirukku maṉaikkāpput tiṟakkac ceytaruḷip poruḷoṉṟeṉ ceṅkaitaṉil aḷittāy tirumaṇimaṉ ṟiṭainaṭikkum perumāṉniṉ karuṇait tiṟattiṉai-ic ciṟiyēṉnāṉ cepputaleṅ ṅaṉamē.
translation: O great Lord dancing in the holy ruby hall! Like sugar, honey, milk, ghee, and the juice of ripe fragrant fruit blending at the right moment, you sweeten my heart, my life, and my consciousness. Your shining feet grew very weary as you graciously walked, reached my street, had the doors of my house unlocked, and placed a single object into my red hands. How can a small one like me describe the nature of your grace?
commentary: The experience of divine grace permeates every part of a person, sweetening the heart, life, and consciousness like a perfect blend of honey, milk, and fruit. The astonishing part of this grace is the divine effort: the Lord walks until his feet ache just to reach a humble devotee's home and deliver a priceless gift.

translit: eṉaṟivai uṇṭaruḷi eṉṉuṭaṉē kūṭi eṉiṉpam eṉakkaruḷi eṉṉaiyuntā ṉākkit taṉaṟivāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa poṉṉaṭikaḷ varuntat taṉinaṭantu terukkatavan tāḷtiṟappit taruḷi muṉṉaṟivil eṉai-aḻaitteṉ kaiyiloṉṟu koṭutta muṉṉavaniṉ iṉṉaruḷai eṉeṉayāṉ moḻivēṉ maṉaṟivuk kaṟivāmpoṉ ṉampalattē iṉpa vaṭivāki naṭikkiṉṟa mākaruṇai malaiyē.
translation: O mountain of immense grace! You dance as the embodiment of bliss in the golden hall, acting as the intelligence within all enduring intelligence. You graciously consumed my awareness, united with me, granted me my bliss, and made me Yourself. Your golden feet, shining as absolute intelligence, grew weary as you walked alone. You had the street door unbolted, called me forth into primal awareness, and placed an object in my hands. O primal Lord, how will I speak of your sweet grace?
commentary: True spiritual union means the Divine consumes our limited awareness and replaces it entirely with divine bliss. The Lord makes the soul into Himself, dissolving the separation between them. Even after this profound merging, the divine presence continues to act with intense love, unlocking doors and calling the soul into ultimate realization.

translit: parayōka aṉupavattē akampuṟantōṉ ṟāta parañcōti yākumiṇaip pātamalar varunta varayōkar viyappa-aṭi yēṉirukkum iṭattē vantuteruk katavutaṉaik kāppaviḻkkap purintu tirayōkark karititaṉai vāṅkuka-eṉ ṟeṉatu ceṅkaitaṉil aḷittāyniṉ tiruvaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ urayōkar uḷampōla viḷaṅkumaṇi maṉṟil uyirkkiṉpan taranaṭaṉam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē.
translation: O Supreme Reality! You dance to grant bliss to souls in the ruby hall that shines like the hearts of steadfast yogis. In the experience of supreme yoga, your pair of lotus feet, which are the supreme light where inner and outer vanish, grew weary as you walked. While great yogis marveled, you came to where this servant lives. You had the locks of the street door opened, and saying, "This is rare even for steadfast yogis, receive it," you placed it into my red hands. What can I say of your divine grace?
commentary: The ultimate truth, which even the greatest yogis (steadfast spiritual seekers) struggle to reach through intense effort, is freely given by grace. God walks directly to a humble servant's door to hand over a treasure that ascetic practice alone cannot win. This divine light is so absolute that all boundaries between inner and outer experience completely disappear.

translit: coṉṉiṟainta poruḷumataṉ ilakkiyamum ākit turiyanaṭu virunta-aṭit tuṇaivarunta naṭantu koṉṉiṟainta iraviṉiṭai eḻuntaruḷik katavam koḻuṅkāppai aviḻvittuk koṭiyēṉai aḻaittu eṉṉiṟainta oruporuḷeṉ kaiyilaḷit taruḷi eṉmakaṉē vāḻka-eṉa eḻiltiruvāy malarntāy taṉṉiṟainta niṉkaruṇait taṉmaiyai-eṉ pukalvēṉ taṉimaṉṟil āṉantat tāṇṭavañcey aracē.
translation: O King who performs the dance of bliss in the peerless hall! Your two feet, which rest in the center of the transcendent state as the true meaning of words and the literature describing it, grew weary from walking. Graciously arriving in the middle of the vast night, you had the heavy lock of the door opened, called out to this wretched one, and placed a wholly fulfilling object into my hands. You beautifully opened your holy lips and said, "My son, may you flourish!" How will I speak of the nature of your absolute grace?
commentary: The Divine is both the ultimate truth and the very words used to describe it. In a deeply intimate moment, this supreme reality not only delivers a gift of total fulfillment in the vast night but speaks with the warmth of a parent, saying, "My son, may you flourish." It shows that ultimate grace is not a distant force, but a personal, loving presence.

translit: mutti-oṉṟu viyatti-oṉṟu kāṇmiṉeṉṟā kamattiṉ muṭikaḷmuṭit turaikiṉṟa aṭikaḷmika varuntap patti-oṉṟum illāta kaṭaippulaiyēṉ poruṭṭāp paṭiṟṟuḷattēṉ irukkumiṭan taṉaittēṭi naṭantu citti-oṉṟu tirumēṉi kāṭṭimaṉaik katavam tiṟappittaṅ keṉai-aḻaitteṉ ceṅkaiyilē makiḻntu catti-oṉṟu koṭuttāyniṉ taṇṇaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ taṉimaṉṟuḷ āṉantat tāṇṭavañcey aracē.
translation: The crowns of the Agamas declare that liberation is one and manifestation is one. Your holy feet, praised by those scriptures, suffered greatly. For the sake of me, the lowliest one, devoid of any devotion, You searched for the place where I lived with a deceitful heart and walked there. Showing Your divine form of perfect accomplishment, You made the door of the house open. You called me there and joyfully placed a divine power into my red hands. What can I say of Your cool grace, O King who performs the blissful dance in the unique Hall!
commentary: God's grace does not wait for a person to become worthy. Even though the sacred scriptures (Agamas) praise the divine feet as the ultimate reality, God allows those feet to suffer the physical exertion of walking just to seek out a deceitful, un-devoted person. Arriving at the door, the Divine opens it and places a tangible spiritual power directly into the seeker's hands.

translit: eṉakkunaṉmai tīmaiyeṉpa tiraṇṭumotta iṭattē iraṇṭumottut tōṉṟukiṉṟa eḻiṟpataṅkaḷ varuntat taṉakkunalla vaṇṇamoṉṟu tāṅkinaṭan taruḷit taṉittiravil kaṭaippulaiyēṉ taṅkumiṭat taṭaintu kaṉakkumaṉait terukkatavaṅ kāppaviḻkkap purintu kaḷippoṭeṉai aḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttu uṉakkiṉiya vaṇṇamiteṉ ṟuraittaruḷic ceṉṟāy uṭaiyavaniṉ aruṭperumai uraikkamuṭi yātē.
translation: When good and evil appeared the same to me, Your beautiful feet, which manifest equally in both states, suffered. Bearing a form pleasing to Yourself, You walked gracefully in the lonely night and reached the place where I, the lowliest one, stayed. You caused the heavy street door of the house to unlock, called me with joy, and placed something in my hand. You told me, 'This is the state sweet to you,' and departed. O Master, the greatness of Your grace cannot be told.
commentary: When a person reaches a state of total equanimity, where good and evil appear exactly the same, the Divine responds directly. God comes in the lonely night, enduring the hardship of the road, to unlock a heavy door and place a tailored spiritual gift directly into the seeker's hand. It is a deeply personal grace, given with the assurance that it is the exact state meant for them.

translit: immaiyiṉō ṭammaiyiṉum eytukiṉṟa iṉpam eṉaittoṉṟum vēṇṭāta iyaṟkaivarun taruṇam emmaiyiṉum niṟaicorupa cuttacukā rampam iyaṟcorupa cuttacuka aṉupavameṉ ṟiraṇṭāyc cemmaiyilē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntac ciṟiyēṉpāl aṭainteṉatu ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittāy ummaiyilē yāṉceytavam yāteṉavum aṟiyēṉ uyarpotuvil iṉpanaṭam uṭaiyaparam poruḷē.
translation: At the very moment a nature arose in me desiring none of the pleasures found in this world or the next, Your holy feet suffered. Those feet shine perfectly as two states: the beginning of pure bliss in complete natural form and the experience of pure bliss in inherent natural form. Reaching me, the lowly one, You placed something into my red hands. I do not know what penance I performed in my previous births, O Supreme Reality who dances in bliss in the high public Hall!
commentary: The very moment all desire for the pleasures of this world and the next falls away, the Divine arrives. God's feet represent two distinct phases of ultimate joy: the dawn of pure bliss, and the full immersion into it. Yet, rather than remaining distant in that perfection, God endures the physical journey to seek out someone lowly and place this pure bliss right into their hands.

translit: aṉpaḷippu toṉṟupiṉṉar iṉpaḷippa toṉṟeṉ ṟaṟiñarelām matikkiṉṟa aṭimalarkaḷ varunta eṉpaḷitta uṭalkaḷtoṟum uyirkkuyirāy irukkum emperumāṉ naṭantaruḷik katavutiṟap pittut tuṉpaḷikkum neñcakatteṉ ṟaṉaikkūvi aḻaittut tūya-iḷa nakaimukattē tuḷumpa-eṉai nōkki muṉpaḷitta teṉṟaṉatu kaiyiloṉṟai aḷittāy muṉṉavaniṉ aruṭperumai muṉṉa-aṟi yēṉē.
translation: All the wise revere Your lotus feet as giving love first and giving bliss later. Those feet suffered as You, my Lord who exists as the life of lives in all embodied beings, walked gracefully. You made the door open, called out to me who possessed a sorrowful heart, looked at me with a pure, gentle smile overflowing on Your face, and placed something in my hand, saying it was given before. O Primal One, I cannot fathom the greatness of Your grace.
commentary: The divine presence is the life breathing within all living beings. Even so, the Divine takes physical form, walking until those holy feet ache, just to comfort a sorrowful heart. With an overflowing smile, God places a gift into his hands and declares that it is something given long ago, revealing this grace as an eternal bond.

translit: mōka-iruṭ kaṭalkaṭattum puṇai-oṉṟu niṟainta mōkaṉacukam aḷippikkum tuṇai-oṉṟeṉ ṟuraikkum yōkamalart tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taruḷi uṇarviliyēṉ poruṭṭāka iruṭṭiravil naṭantu pōkamaṉaip peruṅkatavan tiṟappittuṭ pukuntu pulaiyēṉai aḻaittoṉṟu porunta-eṉkai koṭuttāy nākamaṇip paṇimiḷira ampalattē naṭañcey nāyakaniṉ peruṅkaruṇai naviṟṟamuṭi yātē.
translation: Your yogic lotus feet are praised as a raft to cross the dark ocean of delusion and a companion to grant full, enchanting bliss. Those feet suffered as You walked gracefully. For the sake of me, a person devoid of understanding, You walked in the dark night. You made the large door of the house open, entered, called me, the lowliest one, and placed something fitting into my hand. O Lord who dances in the Hall adorned with shining serpent gems, Your great compassion cannot be expressed.
commentary: God's feet serve as a raft to cross the confusing ocean of worldly delusion and lead to absolute joy. Yet God does not sit waiting on the far shore for the seeker to cross. Instead, the Divine walks through the dark night, seeking out someone who lacks all understanding, to unlock their door and press the perfect spiritual gift into their hands.

translit: kāṇukiṉṟa kaṇkaḷukkuk kāṭṭukiṉṟa oḷiyāyk kāṭṭukiṉṟa oḷitaṉakkuk kāṭṭuvikkum oḷiyāy pūṇukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taṭiyēṉ poruntumiṭat taṭaintukata vantiṟakkap purintu kōṇukiṉṟa maṉattālē nāṇuvatēṉ makaṉē kuṟaivaṟavāḻ keṉamakiḻntu koṭuttaṉai-oṉ ṟeṉakku māṇukiṉṟa niṉṉaruḷiṉ perumaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ maṇimaṉṟil āṉanta mānaṭañcey aracē.
translation: O King performing the great dance of bliss in the hall of gems! You are the light that reveals things to the seeing eyes. You are the light that reveals things to that showing light itself. Walking until your adorned sacred feet suffered, you reached the place where this devotee stays and made the door open. You asked, "My son, why do you feel shy with a wavering mind? Live without any lack," and happily gave me a unique gift. How can I describe the greatness of your glorious grace?
commentary: God is the ultimate source of all perception, the light that makes both our eyes and our inner awareness function. The divine does not wait to be sought out, but actively searches for the devotee in the dark. Walking until his feet ache, God opens the door and gently asks why the devotee is hesitating. The divine gives a direct, joyous gift to dispel all anxiety, showing a deeply personal and loving grace.

translit: āṟaṟu tattuvattiṉ corūpamutal aṉaittum aṟivikkum oṉṟavaṟṟiṉ appālē irunta vīṟāya taṟcorupa mutalaṉaittum aṟivil viḷakkuvikkum oṉṟeṉṟu viḷaivaṟintōr viḷampum pēṟāya tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan tiravil pēyaṭiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭainteṉṉai aḻaittuc cōṟāya poruḷoṉṟeṉ karattaḷittāy potuvil cōtiniṉa taruṭperumai ōtimuṭi yātē.
translation: The wise who know the ultimate fruit declare that one of your sacred feet reveals the nature of the thirty-six principles and everything else, while the other foot illuminates in our consciousness the majestic true self-nature and all that lies beyond. Walking in the night until those precious sacred feet suffered, you reached the place where this ghost-like devotee stays. You called me and placed into my hand a unique substance that serves as supreme nourishment. O Jothi in the common hall, the greatness of your grace can never be fully told!
commentary: The two feet of the divine serve two distinct purposes. One foot reveals the thirty-six tattvas, the fundamental principles of physical and mental existence. The other foot reveals the deeper truth of the soul that lies entirely beyond them. Even though the devotee feels completely unworthy, the divine actively seeks him out in the night to place the supreme nourishment of grace directly into his hands.

translit: karuvikaḷai nammuṭaṉē kalantuḷattē iyakkik kāṭṭuvatoṉ ṟakkaruvi karaṇaṅkaḷ aṉaittum oruvi-appāṟ paṭuttinamai orutaṉiyāk kuvatoṉ ṟupayameṉap periyarcolum apayapatam varuntat turuvi-aṭi yēṉirukkum iṭattiravil aṭaintu tuṇinteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu cōtiyuṟak koṭuttu veruviyiṭēl iṉṟumutal mikamakiḻka eṉṟāy vittakiniṉ tiruvaruḷai viyakkamuṭi yātē.
translation: The great ones declare that one of your feet of refuge unites the faculties with us, operates them in the mind, and reveals the world, while the other foot separates all those instruments and faculties, casts them away, and leaves us in solitary oneness. Walking until those two feet of refuge suffered, you searched for me in the night and reached the place where this devotee stays. You resolutely placed a luminous gift into my hands and said, "Do not fear. Rejoice greatly from this day forward!" O wondrous Lord, the greatness of your divine grace cannot be fully marveled at!
commentary: The divine guides the soul through two opposite experiences. First, one foot of God connects us to our physical and mental faculties so we can experience the world. Then, the other foot strips all these instruments away, leaving the soul in a state of absolute, solitary oneness. Seeking the devotee in the dark, God personally delivers a luminous gift with a simple command to cast away all fear and live in joy.

translit: ātiyilē kalappoḻiya āṉmacutti aḷittāṅ katu-atu-āk kuvatoṉṟām atu-atuvāy ākkum cōtiyilē tāṉākic cūḻvatoṉṟām eṉṟu cūḻcci-aṟin tōrpukalum tuṇaiyaṭikaḷ varunta vītiyilē naṭantaṭiyēṉ irukkumiṭan tēṭi virumpi-aṭain teṉaikkūvi viḷaivoṉṟu koṭuttāy pātiyilē oṉṟāṉa pacupatiniṉ karuṇaip paṇmaipa-aṟin tēṉoḻiyā naṇpai-aṭain tēṉē.
translation: Those who know the subtle truth declare that one of your companion-feet removes primordial entanglements, grants purity to the soul, and transforms it into the divine state, while the other foot merges it into the Jothi itself to encompass all things. Walking through the street until those companion-feet suffered, you searched for the place where this devotee stays. You reached me with love, called me, and gave me a supreme fruit. O Lord of Souls who shares half your form with the Goddess, I have realized the abundant nature of your compassion. I have attained an everlasting friendship with you.
commentary: Here, the two feet represent the complete journey of purification and union. One foot untangles the soul from its ancient impurities and makes it pure. The other foot merges that purified soul directly into the Jothi, the supreme divine light, so that it becomes one with everything. God walks the ordinary streets to find the devotee and deliver this state, creating an eternal bond of friendship between the soul and the divine.

translit: iruṭṭāya malacciṟaiyil irukkumnamai ellām eṭuppatoṉṟām iṉpanilai koṭuppatoṉṟām eṉavē poruṭṭāyar pōṟṟukiṉṟa poṉṉaṭikaḷ varuntap poṟaiyiravil yāṉirukkum iṭantēṭip pukuntu maruṭṭāyat tiruntēṉaik kūvivara vaḻaittu vaṇṇamoṉṟeṉ kaitaṉilē makiḻntaḷittāy niṉṟaṉ aruṭṭāyap perumaitaṉai eṉṉuraippēṉ potuvil āṉantat tirunaṭañcey taruḷukiṉṟa aracē.
translation: "One foot lifts us all from the dark prison of impurity, while the other grants us the state of bliss." So praise those who possess the true wealth of meaning. Walking in the silent night until your golden feet suffered, you searched for the place where I stay and entered it. You called me, who was bound in delusion, summoned me near, and joyfully placed a unique beautiful gift into my hand. How can I express the supreme treasure of your grace? O King, you who graciously perform the sacred dance of bliss in the common hall!
commentary: God's grace acts both to rescue and to reward. One foot lifts the soul out of the dark prison of its own ignorance, while the other foot establishes it in a state of permanent bliss. God walks through the silent night to find the devotee still trapped in delusion, personally calling him forward to place this beautiful gift of liberation into his hands.

translit: uṉmaṉiyiṉ uḷḷakattē oḷiruvatoṉ ṟāki uṟṟa-ataṉ veḷippuṟattē ōṅkuvatoṉ ṟākic ciṉmayamāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntac ciṟunāyēṉ poruṭṭākat teruvilnaṭan taruḷip poṉmayamān tirumēṉi viḷaṅka-eṉpāl aṭaintu poruḷoṉṟeṉ kaitaṉilē porunta-aḷit taṉaiyē niṉmalaṉē niṉṉaruḷai eṉpukalvēṉ potuvil niṟainta-iṉpa vaṭivāki niruttamiṭum patiyē.
translation: One foot shines within the realm of Unmani. The other rises outside of it. Your holy feet, shining as pure consciousness, grew weary as You graciously walked the streets for the sake of this little cur. Your golden holy form radiating light, You came to me and placed an object perfectly into my hand. O flawless one, how can I describe Your grace? You are the Lord who dances in the public hall, taking the form of perfect bliss.
commentary: The divine shows incredible humility in its search for the devotee. God's feet exist both within Unmani (the highest state of spiritual stillness) and completely beyond it, shining as pure consciousness. Yet this supreme being chose to walk the ordinary physical streets to find Vallalar, letting his feet grow weary to place a gift directly into his hand. Grace is not a distant concept, but an intimate force that actively seeks out the individual.

translit: aivarkaḷuk kaintoḻilum aḷittiṭuva toṉṟām attoḻiṟkā raṇampurintu kaḷittiṭuva toṉṟām teyvaneṟi eṉṟaṟiñar pukaḻntupukaḻn tēttun tiruvaṭikaḷ mikavaruntat teruviṉiṭai naṭantu kaivarayāṉ irukkummaṇaik katavutiṟap pittuk kaḷitteṉai-aṅ kaḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttāy caivamaṇi maṉṟiṭattē taṉinaṭaṉam puriyum taṟparaniṉ aruṭperumai cāṟṟamuṭi yātē.
translation: One foot grants the five functions to the five gods. The other rejoices in serving as the cause of those functions. The wise constantly praise them as the divine path. Those holy feet suffered greatly, walking through the street. You caused the door of the house where I stayed to open, rejoiced, called me there, and gave something into my hand. O Supreme One performing the incomparable dance in the beautiful hall of Saivism, the greatness of Your grace cannot be expressed.
commentary: God's cosmic power exists alongside deeply personal compassion. The divine feet drive the five universal functions (creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace) carried out by the major gods. Even with this immense universal authority, God willingly walked through the streets and knocked on a house door to hand Vallalar a gift. The supreme lord steps down from the cosmic stage to show profound care for a single person.

translit: aruḷutikkun taruṇattē amutavaṭi vāki āṉanta mayamāki amarntatiru vaṭikaḷ iruḷutikkum iraviṉiṭai varuntanaṭan taruḷi yāṉirukkum maṉaikkatavan tiṟappittaṅ kaṭaintu maruḷutikkum maṉattēṉai varavaḻaittu nōkki makiḻnteṉatu karattoṉṟu vaḻaṅkiyacaṟ kuruvē teruḷutikkum maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭañcey aracē civaperumāṉ niṉkaruṇait tiṟattaiviyak kēṉē .
translation: At the moment grace dawns, Your holy feet take the form of nectar and abide as pure bliss. Graciously walking through the dark, gathering night, those feet grew weary. You made the door of my house open, entered, and summoned me whose mind breeds delusion. You looked at me, rejoiced, and offered an object into my hand, O true Guru. O King performing the holy dance in the beautiful hall where clarity dawns! O Lord Siva, I marvel at the nature of Your compassion.
commentary: God does not wait for the individual to become perfect before offering grace. Vallalar says his own mind was full of darkness and confusion, yet the divine came to him anyway as the true teacher. The holy feet, which are pure bliss and sweet nectar, walked through the dark night and grew physically tired just to reach his door. Grace arrives right at the house of the confused mind to bring clarity.

translit: nāṉkaṇṭa pōtucuyañ cōtimaya māki nāṉpiṭitta pōtumati naḷiṉavaṇṇa mākit tēṉkoṇṭa pāleṉanāṉ cintikkun tōṟun tittippa tāki-eṉṟaṉ ceṉṉimicai makiḻntu tāṉkoṇṭu vaitta-annāḷ cilleṉṟeṉ uṭampum taka-uyiruṅ kuḷirvitta tāṇmalarkaḷ varunta vāṉkoṇṭu naṭantiṅku vanteṉakkum aḷittāy maṉṟilnaṭat taracēniṉ mākaruṇai viyappē.
translation: When I saw them, they were a natural mass of radiant light. When I held them, they took the hue of a beautiful lotus. Whenever I think of them, they taste sweet like milk mixed with honey. Rejoicing, You placed them upon my head that day, completely cooling my body and my worthy soul. Those lotus feet grew weary walking through the vast space to come here and grant this to me. O King of the dance in the hall, Your great compassion is a marvel.
commentary: The experience of the divine engages all the senses. The holy feet appear as brilliant light to the eyes, feel like a soft lotus to the touch, and taste like milk mixed with honey to the mind. When God placed them on Vallalar's head, the touch profoundly cooled his physical body and his soul. He stands in awe that the lord of the universe would cross vast cosmic spaces and endure weariness to grant this soothing grace.

translit: yōkānta micai-iruppa toṉṟukalān tattē uvantiruppa toṉṟeṉamey yuṇarvuṭaiyōr uṇarvāl ēkāntat tiruntuṇarum iṇaiyaṭikaḷ varunta eṉporuṭṭāy yāṉirukkum iṭantēṭi naṭantu vākāntac caṇikkatavan tiṟappittaṅ keṉṉai varavaḻaitteṉ kaitaṉilē makiḻntoṉṟu koṭuttāy mōkānta kāramaṟut tavarēttap potuvil muyaṅkinaṭam purikiṉṟa mukkaṉuṭai aracē.
translation: One foot rests at the summit of yoga. The other joyfully rests at the summit of the kalas. Those of true awareness realize this in solitude. Those twin feet grew weary walking and searching for the place where I stayed, all for my sake. You opened the sturdy front door, summoned me, and joyfully placed something into my hand. O three-eyed King dancing intimately in the public hall, praised by those who have severed the dark blindness of delusion!
commentary: The divine reality sits at the absolute peak of spiritual discipline and the subtle energies of the universe (kalas). Wise sages sit in deep solitude simply to understand this truth. Yet those same cosmic feet willingly walked and searched for Vallalar's exact physical address, growing tired to bring him a direct gift. The supreme being who destroys delusion does not remain aloof, but actively pursues the devotee to offer grace.

translit: makamatikku maṟaiyummaṟai yāṉmatikkum ayaṉum makiḻntayaṉāṉ matikkumneṭu mālumneṭu mālāṉ mikamatikkum uruttiraṉum uruttiraṉāl matikkum mēlavaṉum avaṉmatikka viḷaṅkucatā civaṉum takamatikkun tōṟumavar avaruḷattiṉ mēlum talaimēlum maṟaintuṟaiyun tāḷmalarkaḷ varunta akamatikka naṭanteṉpāl aṭaintoṉṟu koṭuttāy ampalattil āṭukiṉṟāy aruṭperumai viyappē.
translation: The Vedas remain hidden from great intellects. The Vedas esteem Brahma. Joyful Brahma esteems great Vishnu. Vishnu greatly esteems Rudra. Rudra esteems the Lord above him. The Lord above him esteems shining Sadasiva. Whenever they meditate, your flower-like feet remain hidden within their hearts and above their heads. Yet, letting those feet suffer, you walked to me so my heart could rejoice, and you gave me one thing. You dance in the hall. The greatness of your grace is a wonder.
commentary: The highest gods in traditional religion, from Brahma and Vishnu to Rudra and Sadasiva, cannot find the Lord's feet even in deep meditation. Yet, Vallalar says, those same divine feet walked to him in person, enduring the pain of the journey, simply to bring him joy and hand him a precious gift. This shows that true grace ignores cosmic hierarchies and comes directly to a heart filled with devotion.

translit: iruviṉai-op pākimala paripākam poruntal ettaruṇam attaruṇat tiyalñāṉa oḷiyām uruviṉaiyuṟ ṟuḷḷakattum piraṇavamē vaṭivāy uṟṟuveḷip puṟattumeḻun tuṇartti-urait taruḷum tiruvaṭikaḷ mikavarunta naṭanteḷiyēṉ poruṭṭāt terukkavan tiṟappittuc ciṟiyēṉai aḻaittuk kuruvaṭivaṅ kāṭṭi-oṉṟu koṭuttāy eṉkarattē kuṇakkuṉṟē niṉṉaruṭkeṉ kuṟṟamelāṅ kuṇamē.
translation: When the two karmas balance and the impurities ripen, at that moment your holy feet take the form of the natural light of wisdom within. They take the form of the primal sound outside, rising to awaken and teach. Letting those holy feet suffer greatly, you walked for the sake of this poor one. You made the street door open, called out to this lowly one, revealed your Guru form, and placed one thing in my hand. O mountain of virtues, to your grace, all my faults appear as virtues.
commentary: In spiritual life, there comes a moment when past good and bad deeds balance out, and the mind's impurities fall away. At that exact moment, Vallalar says, the Divine appears as a guiding light inside and a teaching voice outside. God took the physical form of a teacher, walked to his door, and placed a gift in his hand, looking past all of his faults with pure grace.

translit: tammaṭiyār varuntilatu cakiyātak kaṇattē cārntuvarut taṅkaḷelān tayaviṉoṭu tavirttē emmaṭiyār eṉṟukoḷum iṇaiyaṭikaḷ varunta iraviṉiṭai naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu kammaṭiyāk katavuperuṅ kāppaviḻap purintu kaṭaiyēṉai aḻaitteṉatu kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttu nammaṭiyāṉ eṉṟeṉaiyun tiruvuḷattē aṭaittāy naṭampuriyum nāyakaniṉ naṟkaruṇai viyappē.
translation: If your devotees suffer, you cannot bear it for even a moment. You approach them and compassionately remove all their afflictions. Letting your peerless feet suffer, the feet that claim them saying, "These are our devotees," you walked in the night and reached the place where this poor one lives. You made the heavy locks of the smith-forged door fall open, called this lowest one, and placed one thing in my hand. Taking me into your divine heart, you said, "He is our devotee." O dancing Lord, your good grace is a wonder.
commentary: The Divine cannot bear to see living beings suffer for even a moment. Walking through the dark night, the Lord caused heavy, locked doors to fall open by themselves just to reach Vallalar. He placed a gift in his hand and claimed him directly, proving that absolute grace shatters all physical and worldly barriers to reach a devotee.

translit: umparukkuṅ kiṭaipparinām maṇimaṉṟil pūta uruvaṭivaṅ kaṭantāṭun tiruvaṭika ḷiṭattē cemparukkaik kalluṟattat teruvilnaṭan tiravil terukkatavan tiṟappittuc ciṟiyēṉai aḻaittu vamparukkup peṟalaritām oruporuḷeṉ karattē makiḻntaḷittut tuyartīrntu vāḻka-eṉa uraittāy imparukkō amparukkum ituviyappām eṅkaḷ iṟaivaniṉ taruṭperumai icaippatevaṉ aṇintē.
translation: Your holy feet dance in the gem-set hall, transcending elemental physical forms, and they are difficult even for celestials to attain. Letting the sharp red pebbles hurt those feet, you walked in the street at night. You had the street door opened, called this little one, and joyfully gave a unique treasure into my hand, a treasure unattainable for the unworthy. You said, "May your sorrow end, and may you live well." This is a wonder for those in this world and in the celestial world. O our Lord, how can anyone fully praise the greatness of your grace?
commentary: The Lord’s feet exist beyond all physical elements and remain out of reach even to heavenly beings. Yet, out of pure love, those same feet walked over sharp stones in the dark streets to reach Vallalar's house. God gave him a rare treasure and a simple, warm blessing: an end to his sorrow and a promise of a joyful life.

translit: uruvamoru nāṉkāki aruvamumav vaḷavāy uru-aru-oṉ ṟāki-ivai oṉpāṉuṅ kaṭantu turuvamuṭi yāpparama turiyanaṭu virunta corupa-aṉu pavamayamān tuṇaiyaṭikaḷ varuntat teruvamicai naṭantuciṟu cemparaṟkal uṟuttac ciṟiyēṉpāl aṭainteṉatu ceṅkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittāy maruva-iṉi yāymaṉṟil naṭampurivāy karuṇai mākaṭalē niṉperumai vaḻuttamuṭi yātē.
translation: Taking four formed states, four formless states, and one state both formed and formless, you transcend these nine. Your twin feet reside in the center of the supreme state of Turiya that defies investigation, fully embodying the experience of your true nature. Letting those feet suffer, hurt by small red pebbles, you walked on the street and reached this lowly one, placing one thing in my red hand. You are sweet to embrace, and you dance in the hall! O great ocean of compassion, your greatness is beyond praise.
commentary: The Divine exists far beyond the nine cosmic states of form and formlessness, dwelling in Turiya, the supreme state of pure consciousness beyond ordinary waking or sleep. Despite resting in this unimaginable height, the Lord walked on hard, stony streets to press a gift directly into Vallalar’s hands. It is this boundless, intimate compassion that makes the Divine so sweet to experience and so impossible to fully praise.

translit: pakkuvattāl uyarvāḻaip paḻaṅkaṉintāṟ pōlum paraṅkaruṇai yāṟkaṉinta pattarcittan taṉilē pokkamilap paḻantaṉilē teḷḷamutaṅ kalantāṟ pōṟkalantu tittikkum poṉṉaṭikaḷ varunta mikka-iruḷ iraviṉiṭai naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkum viyaṉmaṉaiyil aṭaintukata vantiṟakkap purintu okka-eṉai aḻaittoṉṟu koṭuttiṅkē iru-eṉ ṟuraittaṉai-em perumāṉniṉ uyarkaruṇai viyappē.
translation: Just as a fine banana perfectly ripens in its season, the minds of devotees ripen through supreme grace. Your golden feet merge and taste sweet within those flawless minds, like clear nectar mixed into that fruit. Letting those golden feet suffer, you walked through the deep darkness of the night, reached the great house where this poor one resides, and made me open the door. You called me close, gave me a thing, and said, "Stay here." My Lord, your supreme grace is a wonder!
commentary: The Divine usually dwells in the pure, ripened minds of great devotees, tasting as sweet as nectar. But here, the Lord does something astonishing: he leaves that perfect space and walks through the dark night, letting his own feet suffer, just to reach the poet's door. It is a deeply personal vision of grace, showing that God actively seeks out the humble to offer a secret gift.

translit: uḷavaṟintōr tamakkellām upaniṭatap poruḷāy uḷavaṟiyārk kikaparamum uṟuvikkum poruḷāy aḷavaṟinta aṟivālē aṟintiṭaniṉ ṟāṭum aṭimalarkaḷ varuntiyiṭa naṭantiravil aṭaintu kaḷavaṟintēṉ taṉaikkūvik katavutiṟap pittuk kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttāyniṉ karuṇaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ viḷaveṟintōṉ ayaṉmutalōr paṇintēttap potuvil viḷaṅkunaṭam purikiṉṟa tuḷaṅkoḷimā maṇiyē.
translation: To all those who know the inner truth, you are the essence of the Upanishads. To those who do not know it, you are the reality that grants the blessings of this world and the next. Your lotus feet dance to be realized through measured wisdom. Letting those feet suffer, you walked in the night, reached me, and called out to this one who knows only deception. You made me open the door and placed a thing in my hand. What can I say of your grace? O brilliant great gem, you perform the luminous dance in the public hall while Brahma and the lord who threw the calf at the wood-apple tree bow and praise you.
commentary: To the wise, God is the deepest spiritual truth; to ordinary people, he is the giver of earthly blessings; to the highest gods, he is the supreme master. Yet this same cosmic Lord walks through the night to knock on the door of someone who feels entirely unworthy. The ultimate reality of the universe acts with an intimate, seeking love.

translit: evvulakum evvuyirum ecceyalum tōṉṟi iyaṅkumiṭa māki-ellām muyaṅkumiṭa mākit tevvulakum naṇpulakuñ camaṉākak kaṇṭa cittarkaḷtam cittattē tittikkum pataṅkaḷ ivvulakil varuntanaṭan teṉporuṭṭāl iravil eḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittaṅ keṉkaiyiloṉ ṟaḷittāy avvulaka mutalulakam aṉaittumakiḻn tētta ampalattē naṭampuriyum cempavaḷak kuṉṟē.
translation: You are the space where every world, every soul, and every action appears and moves. You are the space where everything ultimately dissolves. Your feet taste sweet in the minds of the realized beings who see the world of foes and the world of friends equally. For my sake, you let those feet suffer by walking in this world during the night. You made me open the beautiful door and placed a thing in my hand. O hill of red coral, you perform your dance in the hall as all the worlds, starting from the supreme world, rejoice and praise you.
commentary: Realized beings, known as Siddhas, experience God because they have learned to look at both friends and enemies with perfect equality. The Lord is the infinite space where every world and soul is born and dies. Yet this infinite being accepts the physical pain of walking on the earth purely for the sake of one devotee.

translit: māṉiṉoṭu mōkiṉiyum māmāyai yuṭaṉē vaintuvamum oṉṟiṉoṉṟu vatintacaiya acaittē ūṉiṉoṭum uyiruṇarvuṅ kalantukalap puṟumā ṟuṟuvittup piṉkaruma oppuvarun taruṇam tēṉiṉoṭu kalanta-amu teṉarucikka irunta tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taṭiyēṉpāl aṭaintu vāṉiṉoṭu viḷaṅkuporuḷ oṉṟeṉakkum aḷittāy maṉṟilnaṭat taracēniṉ mākaruṇai viyappē.
translation: You set into motion the principles of man, mohini, the great maya, and vainduvam, making them reside and move within one another. You made the flesh and the soul's consciousness blend together completely. Then, at the time when the soul's deeds reach perfect balance, your holy feet taste like nectar mixed with honey. Letting those feet suffer, you walked, reached this servant, and gave me a supreme entity that shines with the heavens. O king of the dance in the hall, your great grace is a wonder!
commentary: The Lord orchestrates the massive cosmic forces of illusion and matter that bind the soul to the flesh. When a soul's good and bad deeds finally reach a state of perfect balance, the divine presence becomes as sweet as honey. The master of the universe's complex machinery is also a personal king who walks to his servant to hand him a heavenly reality.

translit: pacupāca pantamaṟum pāṅkutaṉaik kāṭṭip paramāki uḷḷiruntu paṟṟavum purintē acamāṉa māṉacivā ḷanta-aṉu pavamum aṭaivittav vaṉupavantām ākiyacē vaṭikaḷ vacumītu varuntiyiṭa naṭantaṭiyēṉ irukkum maṉaiyai-aṭain taṇikkavan tiṟappittu niṉṟu vicuvāca muṟa-eṉai-aṅ kaḻaittoṉṟu koṭuttāy viṭaiyavaniṉ aruṭperumai eṉpukalvēṉ viyantē.
translation: You showed the way to sever the ties binding the soul and the world. Becoming the supreme reality within, you made me grasp you, and you bestowed the unequaled experience of supreme bliss. Your red feet, which are that very experience, suffered upon the earth as you walked. You reached the house where this servant resides, made me open the tightly shut door, stood there, called me with deep affection, and gave me a thing. O Lord riding the bull, how can I express my wonder at the greatness of your grace?
commentary: Breaking the tight bonds that tie the soul to the world is the ultimate spiritual goal. The Lord cuts those bonds and grants the highest bliss. In a beautiful twist, those divine feet do not just bring the experience of bliss: they are the experience itself, and they willingly suffer the hard earth to bring that joy directly to the devotee's door.

translit: ātiyumāy antamumāy naṭuvāki āti antanaṭu villāta mantaṇavāṉ poruḷāyc cōtiyumāyc cōtiyelān tōṉṟupara mākit turiyamumāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tuṇaiyaṭikaḷ varunta pātiyira viṭainaṭantu nāṉirukkum iṭattē paṭarntuteruk katavaṅkāp paviḻttiṭavum purintu ōtiyilaṅ keṉaiyaḻaitteṉ karattoṉṟu koṭuttāy uṭaiyavaniṉ aruṭperumai eṉṉuraippēṉ uvantē.
translation: You are the beginning, the end, and the middle. You are the secret supreme reality without beginning, end, or middle. You are the light. You are the supreme from which all lights appear. Your pair of feet that shine as the transcendent state grew weary as you walked in the middle of the night to the place where I live. Reaching there, you caused the locked street door to open. You called out to me and placed something in my hand. O Master, how can I joyfully express the greatness of your Grace?
commentary: God is the ultimate reality and the source of all light, yet acts with deeply personal intimacy. The supreme divine walks through the night, growing weary, simply to open a locked door and hand a gift to a single devotee. This shows that the highest truth is not distant, but actively reaches out to find those who seek it.

translit: pāṭukiṉṟa maṟaikaḷelām orupuṟañcūḻn tāṭap pattaroṭu muttarelām pāttāṭap potuvil āṭukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭan taṭiyēṉ aṭaiyumiṭat taṭaintiraviṟ kāppaviḻkkap purintu nāṭukiṉṟa ciṟiyēṉai aḻaittaruḷi nōkki nakaimukañcey teṉkarattē nalkiṉai-oṉ ṟitaṉāl vāṭukiṉṟa vāṭṭamelān tavirntumakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ maṉṉavaniṉ poṉṉaruḷai eṉṉeṉavāḻt tuvaṉē.
translation: While all the chanting Vedas gather on one side and dance, and devotees and liberated souls watch and dance, your holy feet that dance in the public hall grew weary. You walked to the place I dwell, arriving in the night and causing the lock to open. Calling out to this seeking, lowly one, you looked at me with grace. Smiling, you gave something into my hand. Because of this, all my withering sorrow is gone, and I rejoice. O King, how can I praise your golden Grace?
commentary: The divine leaves the grand arenas of scripture and traditional worship to come directly to a humble seeker. While the ancient sacred texts known as the Vedas and liberated souls watch the cosmic dance, God's feet grow tired walking through the dark to find this one individual. A simple smile and a direct gift from God are enough to erase all human sorrow.

translit: emmatattil evarevarkkum iyainta-aṉu pavamāy ellāmāy allavumāy iruntapaṭi iruntē ammatappoṉ ṉampalattil āṉanta naṭañcey arumperuñcē vaṭiyiṇaikaḷ acaintumika varunta immatattil eṉporuṭṭāy iravilnaṭan taruḷi eḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittaṅ koṉai-aḻaitteṉ karattē cammapatattāl oṉṟaḷitta tayaviṉai-eṉ pukalvēṉ tammai-aṟin tavaraṟiviṉ maṉṉumoḷi maṇiyē.
translation: Remaining exactly as you are, you are the agreeable experience for everyone in every religion. You are everything and you are none of those things. You dance joyously in that golden hall of wisdom. Your rare, great, and beautiful pair of feet moved and grew very weary as you walked in the night specifically for my sake. You caused the beautiful door to open, called me there, and placed something in my hand with balanced grace. How can I describe this compassion? O shining gem of light enduring in the awareness of those who know themselves!
commentary: God is the core of every religious experience, yet remains entirely beyond all of them. The divine is present in all forms of worship without being limited by any single tradition. Out of pure compassion, this universal presence takes on a personal form, walking in the night to hand a gift directly to the seeking soul.

translit: pūtaveḷi karaṇaveḷi pakutiveḷi māyā pōkaveḷi māmāyā yōkaveḷi pukalum vētaveḷi aparavintu veḷi-apara nāta veḷi-ēka veḷiparama veḷiñāṉa veḷimā nātaveḷi cuttaveṟu veḷiveṭṭa veḷiyā nalilkiṉṟa veḷikaḷalām naṭikkumaṭi varunta ēta-eḷi yēṉporuṭṭā naṭanteṉpāl aṭaintē eṉkaiyiṉoṉ ṟaḷittaṉainiṉ irakkamevark kuḷatē.
translation: Your dancing feet grew weary traversing all the spoken expanses: the expanse of the elements, the expanse of the faculties, the expanse of nature, the expanse of illusory experience, the expanse of great illusory yoga, the Vedic expanse, the lower bindu expanse, the lower nada expanse, the singular expanse, the supreme expanse, the expanse of wisdom, the great nada expanse, the pure empty expanse, and the absolute open expanse. Walking for the sake of this flawed and lowly one, you reached me. You placed something in my hand. Who possesses compassion like yours?
commentary: The divine crosses through every conceivable layer of reality to reach a single flawed human being. These spaces range from the physical elements to the highest spiritual realms of bindu (subtle light) and nada (subtle sound), reaching all the way to absolute emptiness. Despite spanning all these vast cosmic dimensions, God's compassion brings him directly to the seeker's door.

translit: vāṉatuvāyp pacumalampōyt taṉittuniṟkun taruṇam vayaṅkuparā ṉantacukam vaḷaintukoḷḷun taruṇam tāṉatuvāy atutāṉāyc cakacamuṟun taruṇam taṭaiyaṟṟa aṉupavamān taṉmaiyaṭi varunta māṉatuvāy naṭanteḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu maṇikkatavan tiṟappittu makiḻnteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittu āṉatoru poruḷaḷittāy niṉṉaruḷeṉ eṉpēṉ ampalattē naṭampuriyum emperuñcō tiyaṉē.
translation: Your feet embody the nature of unobstructed experience: the moment of becoming the vastness when the soul's impurity vanishes and one stands alone, the moment the shining supreme blissful joy surrounds one, and the moment of attaining the natural state where one becomes That and That becomes one. These feet grew weary as you walked with great dignity to reach the place where this lowly one dwells. You caused the jeweled door to open, joyfully called me there, and gave me a supreme object. What can I say of your grace? O my Great Jothi who dances in the hall!
commentary: The very feet that represent the highest states of spiritual liberation take on the physical effort of walking to a seeker's home. The verses describe ultimate freedom, where all inner flaws vanish, immense bliss surrounds the soul, and the individual becomes one with the divine. Yet this supreme light, the great Jothi, willingly steps into the ordinary world to hand down its grace.

translit: puṉṟaṉai talaiyeṉanāṉ aṟiyāmal orunāḷ poruttiyapō tiṉiṟcivantu poruntiyapoṉ ṉaṭikaḷ iṉṟalaiviṉ mikaccivantu varuntanaṭan teḷiyēṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaittukata vantiṟakkap purintu maṉṟaliṉaṅ keṉai-aḻaittēṉ kaiyiloṉṟu koṭuttāy maṉṉavaniṉ peruṅkaruṇai vaṇmaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ poṉṟavilāc cittarmuttar pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟil puyaṅkanaṭam purikiṉṟa vayaṅkoḷimā maṇiyē.
translation: One day, without my realizing my head was lowly, you placed your golden feet upon it, and they turned red. Today, those same feet walked in distress, reddening greatly from the exertion, and reached the place where I, a poor wretch, stay. You made the door open, called me with sweetness, and placed something in my hand. O King, how can I describe the bounty of your great grace? You are the great gem of shining light who performs the snake dance in the hall of gems, praised by immortal ascetics and liberated souls.
commentary: God's grace is intensely personal. The divine feet, which once reddened just from touching a mortal head, have now walked through the dark night to reach him. The supreme being who dances in a cosmic hall takes on physical exhaustion simply to bring a gift to a single suffering person. Divine love cares nothing for status or distance.

translit: tañcamuṟum uyirkkuṇarvāy iṉpamumāy niṟainta tamperumai tāmaṟiyāt taṉmaivāy orunāḷ vañcakaṉēṉ puṉṟalaiyil vaittiṭavuñ civantu varuntiyacē vaṭipiṉṉum varuntanaṭat taruḷi eñcilā iraviṉiṭai yāṉirukkum iṭañcērn teḻiṟkatavan tiṟappittaṅ keṉai-aḻaittoṉ ṟaḷittāy viñcuparā ṉantanaṭam viyaṉpotuviṟ puriyum mēlavaniṉ aruṭperumai viḷampalevaṉ viyantē.
translation: You fill all refuge-seeking souls as their consciousness and bliss. Your nature is such that you are unaware of your own greatness. One day, you placed your feet upon the lowly head of this deceitful one, and they turned red. Later, those beautiful red feet walked again in distress through the dark night and graciously reached my dwelling. You caused the beautiful door to be opened, called me, and granted me something. O Supreme One who performs the transcendent dance of bliss in the vast hall, how can I express the wondrous greatness of your grace?
commentary: The supreme being sustains the consciousness of every living creature but acts without a trace of ego, completely unaware of its own greatness. The same boundless God who fills the universe chose to walk through the dark like an ordinary traveler to comfort a devoted soul. This absolute humility is the true nature of divine grace.

translit: eḻuttiṉoṭu patamāki mantiramāy puvaṉam ellāmāyt tattuvamāy iyampukalai yāki vaḻuttumivaik kuḷḷākip puṟamāki naṭattum vaḻiyāki naṭattuvikkum maṉṉiṟaiyu māki aḻuttuṟamiṅ kivaiyellām allaṉavāy appāl ākiyataṟ kappālum āṉapatam varunta iḻaittunaṭan tiravileṉpāl aṭaintoṉṟu koṭuttāy emperumāṉ niṉperumai eṉṉuraippēṉ viyantē.
translation: You became the letter, the word, the mantra, all the worlds, the fundamental principles, and the spoken arts. You exist inside and outside of all these praised forms. You are the guiding path and the sovereign fullness that sustains them. Yet you remain separate from all these, existing far beyond them and even beyond that beyond. Even so, your feet walked in distress through the night, reached me, and gave me something. O my Lord, how can I express your wondrous greatness?
commentary: The divine is the source of all language, sacred sounds, and the fundamental building blocks of reality, yet exists far beyond all of them. The marvel here is the immense contrast between that unimaginable vastness and a God who physically walks through the night, tiring his feet, simply to hand a gift to someone in need. The ultimate truth of the cosmos is intimately close and profoundly caring.

translit: māviṉmaṇap pōrviṭaimēl nantiviṭai mēlum vayaṅki-aṉpar kuṟaitavirttu vāḻvaḷippa taṉṟip pūviṉmaṇam pōluyiruk kuyirāki niṟaintu pōkamaḷit taruḷkiṉṟa poṉṉaṭikaḷ varuntat tāvinaṭan tiraviṉmaṉaik katavutip pittē tayavuṭaṉaṅ keṉai-aḻaittut takkatoṉṟu koṭuttāy nāviṉmaṇan tuṟappulavar viyantēttum potuvil naṭampuriyum nāyakaniṉ naṟkaruṇai ituvē.
translation: You appear on the great warring bull and on the bull Nandi, dispelling the sorrows of your devotees and granting them a flourishing life. Like the fragrance within a flower, you fill all beings as the soul of their souls, granting joyous experiences through your grace. Yet your golden feet suffered as you walked swiftly through the night and caused the door of my house to open. With compassion, you called me and gave me something fitting. O Lord who dances in the universal hall, praised in wonder by poets whose tongues are fragrant with sweet words, this indeed is your boundless grace.
commentary: God is already the soul within every soul, present inside us exactly as fragrance is present inside a flower. Yet this invisible, all-pervading presence still takes the physical trouble to walk through the night and knock on a door to offer help. Grace is an active, compassionate force that responds immediately to human struggles.

translit: maṇappōtu vīṟṟiruntāṉ mālavaṉmaṟ ṟavarum maṉa-aḻukkā ṟuṟacciṟiyēṉ varuntiyanāḷ antō kaṇappōtun tariyāmaṟ karuṇai-aṭi varuntak kaṅkulilē naṭanteṉṉaik karuti-oṉṟu koṭuttāy uṇappōtu pōkkiṉaṉmuṉ uḷavaṟiyā maiyiṉāl uḷavaṟintēṉ innāḷeṉ uḷḷamakiḻ vuṟṟēṉ taṇappōtu maṟaikaḷelān taṉittaṉiniṉ ṟēttat taṉimaṉṟil āṉantat tāṇṭavañcey aracē.
translation: Brahma seated on the fragrant lotus, Vishnu, and the other gods felt envy in their hearts while I, a lowly one, suffered in the past. Alas, unable to bear my sorrow even for a moment, you walked through the night so that your compassionate feet suffered, sought me out, and gave me something. In the past, I wasted my time in ignorance, not knowing the secret truth. Today I have learned the secret, and my heart rejoices. O King who performs the dance of bliss in the peerless hall while all the Vedas stand apart and praise you with fresh flowers!
commentary: The highest divine compassion responds directly to human pain, moving so intimately that even traditional gods like Brahma and Vishnu watch in envy. God could not bear to see a single person suffer for even a moment and rushed through the night to bring relief. Experiencing this direct, overwhelming love is the secret truth that brings total joy, leaving the ancient scriptures standing far away in awe.

translit: naṭuṅkamalak kaṇkuṟuki neṭuṅkamalak kaṇviḷaṅkum nallatiru vaṭivarunta valiravil naṭantu toṭuṅkavan tiṟappittut tuṇinteṉaiyaṅ kaḻaittut tuyaramelām viṭuka-itu toṭuka-eṉak koṭuttāy koṭuṅkuṇattēṉ aḷaviṉileṉ kuṟṟamelāṅ kuṇamāk koṇṭakuṇak kuṉṟēniṉ kuṟippiṉai-eṉ pukalvēṉ iṭuṅkiṭuka eṉṟuṇartti ēṟṟukiṉṟa aṟivōr ēttamaṇip potuvilaruṭ kūttuṭaiya poruḷē.
translation: O Reality performing the dance of Grace in the ruby Hall, praised by the wise who realize the truth of giving and uplift others! Walking in the harsh night until your good holy feet, shining like long lotuses, ached, you made me open the fastened door. You resolutely called me out and gave me something, saying, "Let go of all sorrow, take hold of this." O Mountain of virtue who accepted all my faults as virtues despite my cruel nature, what can I say of your intention?
commentary: The Divine does not wait for the seeker to approach, but actively walks through the dark night to reach them. Vallalar describes a profound personal experience where God arrives at his door, enduring hardship to hand him a gift of grace and command him to leave all sorrow behind. This boundless mercy transforms the seeker's very faults into virtues.

translit: veyyapavak kōṭaiyilē mika-iḷaittu melinta meyyaṭiyar tamakkellām virumpukuḷir cōlait tuyyaniḻa lāyamutāy melivaṉaittun tavirkkum tuṇaiyaṭikaḷ mikavaruntat tuṇintunaṭan taṭiyēṉ uyyanaṭu iraviṉilyāṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintē uyarkatavan tiṟappittaṅ kuvantaḻaittoṉ ṟaḷittāy vaiyakamum vāṉakamum vāḻamaṇip potuvil mānaṭañcey aracēniṉ vaṇmai-evark kuḷatē.
translation: O King performing the great dance in the ruby Hall so that earth and heaven may flourish, who possesses your generosity? For all your true devotees who are greatly exhausted and thinned in the harsh summer of worldly existence, your companion feet serve as a desired cool grove, pure shade, and nectar, removing all their fatigue. Yet you resolutely walked until those feet ached greatly, reaching the place where I was in the middle of the night to save me. You made the high door open, joyfully called me out, and gave me one thing.
commentary: The sheltering presence of God is usually a resting place for souls exhausted by the harshness of worldly life. Yet here, the Divine gives up that rest and takes on the pain of a long journey to rescue a single person. Vallalar expresses awe at this overwhelming generosity, marveling that the ruler of heaven and earth would walk through the night just to hand him a gift of salvation.

translit: ciṟayavaṉēṉ ciṟumaiyelām tiruvuḷaṅkoḷ ḷāteṉ ceṉṉimicai amarntaruḷum tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntac ceṟiyiravil naṭantaṇaintu nāṉirukku miṭattē terukkatavan tiṟappittuc ciṟappiṉeṉai aḻaittup piṟivilatiṅ kitutaṇainī peṟukaveṉap parintu pēci-oṉṟu koṭuttāyniṉ perumaiyai-eṉ eṉpēṉ poṟiyiṉaṟa vōrtutikkap potuvilnaṭam puriyum poruḷēniṉ aruḷēmeyp poruḷeṉattērn taṉaṉē.
translation: O Reality performing the dance in the Hall, praised by ascetics of flawless senses! I have realized that your Grace is the true Reality. Not taking the pettiness of my small self into your divine heart, you walked in the dense night until your holy feet, which graciously sit upon my head, ached. Reaching where I was, you made the street door open and called me out with special regard. Affectionately saying, "Receive this inseparable companion here," you spoke and gave me one thing. What can I say of your greatness?
commentary: The true nature of the Divine is pure Grace, and it overlooks all human flaws. Vallalar recounts how God arrived in the darkest hours to hand him an inseparable companion, meaning the constant and guiding presence of divine mercy. He declares plainly that this Grace is the only lasting reality there is.

translit: aṭināḷil aṭiyēṉai aṟivukuṟik koḷḷā tāṭkoṇṭēṉ ceṉṉimicai amarntapatam varuntap paṭināḷil naṭantiravil aṭaintaruḷit teruvil paṭarkatavan tiṟappittup parinteṉai-aṅ kaḻaittup piṭināḷu makiḻntuṉatu maṉaṅkoṇṭa paṭiyē pēraṟañcey tuṟuka-eṉap pēci-oṉṟu koṭuttāy poṭināḷum aṇintumaṇip potuvilnaṭam puriyum poruḷēniṉ aruḷēmeyp poruḷeṉattērn taṉaṉē.
translation: O Reality always wearing sacred ash and dancing in the ruby Hall! I have realized that your Grace is the true Reality. In my early days, not minding my limited knowledge, you claimed me. Walking on the earth in the night until your feet, which sit upon my head, ached, you graciously arrived. You made the wide street door open and affectionately called me out. Saying, "Hold this, rejoice always, and perform great acts of dharma according to your heart's desire," you spoke and gave me one thing.
commentary: The divine gift comes with a clear instruction to perform great acts of dharma, meaning selfless charity and righteous action. Vallalar shows that experiencing God's grace is not meant to pull a person away from the world. Instead, it empowers them to live joyfully and act with deep compassion toward all living beings.
