translit: ulakiyalō ṭaruḷiyalum oruṅkaṟiyac ciṟiyēṉ uṇarvilirun tuṇartti-eṉa tuyirkkuyirāy viḷaṅkit tilakameṉat tikaḻnteṉatu ceṉṉimicai amarnta tiruvaṭikaḷ varuntanaṭai ceytaruḷi aṭiyēṉ ilakumaṉaik kataviravil tiṟappittaṅ keṉṉai iṉitaḻaittoṉ ṟaḷittumakiḻn tiṉṉumneṭuṅ kālam pulavartoḻa vāḻka-eṉṟāy potuvilnaṭam puriyum poruḷēniṉ aruḷēmeyp poruḷeṉattērn taṉaṉē.
translation: O Reality dancing in the Hall! I have realized that your Grace is the true Reality. So that I, a small one, might know both worldly ways and the ways of Grace together, you instructed me from within my awareness and shone as the life of my life. Shining like a sacred mark and sitting upon my head, your holy feet ached as you graciously walked. In the night, you made the door of my shining house open, sweetly called me out, and gave me one thing. Rejoicing, you said, "May you live for a long time yet, praised by the wise."
commentary: Spiritual life and practical worldly life are not opposed to each other. Vallalar explains that God acts as the inner teacher, guiding the soul to master both the material and the spiritual paths at once. The ultimate blessing of Grace is not an escape into another world, but a long and radiant life here on earth, guided by inner truth and respected by the wise.

note: Editor's note: verse 9, the two great ones are Patanjali and Vyaghrapada (Sa. Mu. Kandasamy Pillai).
translit: tiru-urukkoṇ ṭeḻuntaruḷic ciṟiyēṉmuṉ aṭaintu tirunīṟṟup pai-aviḻttuc ceñcuṭarppū aḷikkat taruvurukkoṇ ṭetirvaṇaṅki vāṅkiyanāṉ mīṭṭum tayānitiyē tirunīṟum taruka-eṉak kēṭpa maruvurukkoṇ ṭaṉṟaḷittām tirunīṟiṉ ṟuṉakku makiḻntaḷittāy ivai-eṉṟu vāymalarntu niṉṟāy kuru-urukkoṇ ṭampalattē aruḷnaṭaṉam puriyum kurumaṇiyē eṉṉaimuṉṉāṭ koṇṭakuṇak kuṉṟē.
translation: You assumed a divine form and appeared before this lowly one. You untied the pouch of holy ash and offered me a flower of bright red flame. Standing like a rooted tree, I bowed in reverence, received it, and asked again, "O treasure of compassion, please give me holy ash as well." You spoke and said, "We gave you holy ash on that day in a fragrant form. Today we joyfully give you these flowers." O supreme Guru who assumes the form of a Guru and performs the dance of grace in the hall of Ambalam! O mountain of virtue who claimed me in the days of old!
commentary: A mystical vision unfolds here with the Lord appearing as a spiritual teacher. While holy ash is the traditional blessing given to devotees, God hands over a flower made of red flame instead. When the speaker asks for the ash, the Divine replies that he had already received it long ago, showing that he is now being offered a higher, rarer initiation of light.

translit: eṉvaṭivan taḻaippa-oru poṉvaṭivan tarittē eṉmuṉaṭain teṉainōkki aunakaicey taruḷit taṉvaṭivat tirunīṟṟut taṉippai-aviḻt teṉakkut takucuṭarppū aḷikkavumnāṉ tāṉvāṅkik kaḷittu miṉvaṭivap peruntakaiyē tirunīṟum tarutal vēṇṭumeṉa muṉṉaratu virumpiyaḷit taṉamnām uṉvaṭiviṟ kāṇṭiyeṉa uraittaruḷi niṉṟāy oḷinaṭañcey ampalattē veḷinaṭañcey aracē.
translation: So that my being might flourish, you assumed a golden form and appeared before me. Looking at me, you smiled gracefully, untied your unique pouch of holy ash, and offered me a fitting flower of flame. I received it and rejoiced. Then I said, "O great Lord with the form of lightning, you must give me holy ash as well." You spoke and said, "We happily gave that to you before. See it upon your own body." O King who performs the dance of light and the dance of open space in the hall of Ambalam!
commentary: The vision continues with God appearing in a radiant golden body. Again, the speaker is handed a flower of fire instead of the customary ash. Upon asking for the familiar blessing, the Lord tells him to look at his own body, revealing that he is already entirely purified and ready for this new grace.

translit: aḻakuniṟain tila-oru tirumēṉi tarittē aṭiyēṉmuṉ eḻuntaruḷi aruḷnakaikoṇ ṭaṭiyār kaḻakanaṭu eṉai-irutti avarkkellām nīṟu kaḷittaruḷi eṉṉaḷaviṟ karuṇaimuka malarntu kuḻakiyaṟceñ cuṭarppūvaip pokkaṇattil eṭuttuk koṭuttaruḷi niṉṟaṉainiṉ kuṟippaṟiyēṉ kuruvē maḻakaḷiṟṟiṉ uriviḷaṅka maṇippotuviṟ cōti mayavaṭivō ṭiṉpanaṭam vāyntiyaṟṟum patiyē.
translation: You assumed a divine form brimming with beauty and appeared before your servant. With a graceful smile, you seated me amidst the assembly of devotees and happily distributed holy ash to all of them. But when you turned to me, your compassionate face blossomed, and you took a tender flower of red flame from your pouch and gave it to me. O Guru, I do not understand your divine intention. O Lord who performs the blissful dance in a form of light in the gem-like public hall, wearing the shining hide of a young elephant!
commentary: In a gathering of followers, God gives the standard blessing of holy ash to everyone else but singles out this one devotee. By handing him alone the flower of red flame, the Lord marks him for a unique spiritual destiny. He humbly expresses awe, asking the Divine what this profound, separate grace truly means.

translit: vilaikaṭanta maṇi-eṉa-ōr tirumēṉi tarittu viṉaiyēṉmuṉ eḻuntaruḷi meyyaṭiyar virumpak kalaikaṭanta poruṭkellāṅ karaikaṭantu nātak katikaṭanta peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭaikkaṇmalarn taruḷi alaikaṭanta kaṭalmalarnta maṇacceḻumpū aṭiyēṉ aṅkaitaṉil aḷittaṉainiṉ aruṭkuṟippē taṟiyēṉ malaikaṭanta neṭuntōḷil itaḻi-acain tāṭa maṉṟilnaṭam purikiṉṟa vaḷḷalaruṭ kuruvē.
translation: You assumed a divine form like a priceless gem and appeared before this karma-bound one. While true devotees looked on with desire, you opened the outer corners of your eyes with great compassion that surpasses the bounds of all things beyond learning and transcends the realm of sound. You placed a fragrant, rich flower that bloomed in the waveless ocean into the palm of your servant. I do not understand the intention of your grace. O bountiful Lord, O Guru of grace who dances in the hall with cassia flowers swaying on your tall shoulders that rise above the mountains!
commentary: The Lord's compassion is presented as a force that surpasses all worldly learning and subtle sound. While the rest of the assembly watches eagerly, the devotee receives a flower that blooms in a waveless ocean. This ocean is an image of perfect spiritual stillness and ultimate grace.

translit: ularntamaran taḻaikkumoru tiru-uruvan tāṅki uṇarviliyēṉ muṉṉaruvan tuṟukaruṇai tuḷumpu malarntamukam kāṭṭiniṉṟu tirunīṟṟup paiyai malarkkarattāl aviḻttaṅku vatintavarkaṭ kellām alarntatiru nīṟaḷittup piṉṉareṉṟaṉ karattil aruḷmaṇappū aḷittaṉainiṉ aruṭkuṟippē taṟiyēṉ kalantavaraik kalantumaṇik kaṉakamaṉṟil naṭañcey karuṇaineṭuṅ kaṭalē-eṉ kaṇamarnta oḷiyē.
translation: You assumed a divine form that could make a withered tree flourish and joyfully appeared before this senseless one, revealing a blossoming face brimming with deep compassion. You untied the pouch of holy ash with your lotus hands and distributed the radiant ash to everyone gathered there. Then you placed a fragrant flower of grace into my hand. I do not understand the intention of your grace. O vast ocean of compassion who mingles with those who unite with you and dances in the gem-like golden hall! O light seated in my eyes!
commentary: The sheer presence of the Divine is powerful enough to make a dead tree burst into green life. The central contrast of the poem is made final here: the crowd receives the traditional ash, but the chosen devotee is handed the living flower of grace by the supreme light that now rests directly inside his own eyes.

translit: piḻai-alatoṉ ṟaṟiyāta ciṟiyēṉmuṉ purinta peruntavamō tiruvaruḷiṉ perumaiyitō aṟiyēṉ maḻai-eṉaniṉ ṟilakutiru maṇimiṭaṟṟil paṭika vaṭantikaḻa naṭantukuru vaṭivatukoṇ ṭaṭaintu viḻaiviṉoṭeṉ etirniṉṟu tirunīṟṟuk kōyil virittaruḷi aruṇmaṇappū viḷakkamoṉṟu koṭuttāy kuḻai-acaiyac caṭai-acaiyak kulavupoṉṉam palattē kūttiyaṟṟi eṉṉaimuṉṉāṭ koṇṭacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O tender shoot of Siva. You claimed me in days past. You dance in the celebrated Golden Hall, your earrings and your matted locks swaying. Did I perform great penance, or is this the greatness of divine grace? I do not know. I am a lowly one who knows nothing but faults. Yet you approached me in the form of a Guru. A crystal garland shone on your beautiful throat, dark as a raincloud. You stood before me with affection, opened a pouch of sacred ash, and gave me a radiant, fragrant flower of grace.
commentary: The divine takes the accessible, loving form of a Guru to bestow grace directly. The dark throat of Siva refers to the ancient story of the Lord swallowing deadly poison to save all living beings from destruction. This detail highlights God's boundless compassion. Here, that same compassion is offered as a radiant flower to a soul who feels entirely unworthy of the gift.

translit: muttēvar aḻukkāṟṟiṉ mūḻkiyiṭat taṉitta muḻumaṇipōṉ ṟoruvaṭiveṉ muṉkoṭuvan taruḷi ettēvar tamakkumika ariya-eṉum maṇappū eṉkarattē koṭuttaṉainiṉ eṇṇamiteṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ cittē-eṉ pavarumoru kattē-eṉ pavarum tēṟiyapiṉ oṉṟākat terintukoḷḷum potuvil attēvar vaḻutta-iṉpa uruvāki naṭañcey āramutē eṉṉuyiruk kāṉaperun tuṇaiyē.
translation: O rare nectar dancing as the embodiment of bliss while those gods praise you. You are the great companion of my life. You dance in the universal hall where those who speak of consciousness and those who speak of the One realize they are the same after gaining clarity. The three gods plunged into the river of envy, but you graciously appeared before me in a unique form resembling a flawless gem. You placed in my hand a fragrant flower that is exceedingly rare for any god to attain. I do not know your intention in this.
commentary: The universal hall of grace is a space where different philosophical paths finally merge and recognize their absolute oneness. While traditional gods are caught in envy and spiritual competition, the true Divine approaches the humble seeker directly. This supreme grace is represented as a flower that even the highest deities cannot attain, yet it is placed freely into human hands.

translit: teḷḷamutam aṉaiya-oru tiru-uruvan tāṅkic ciṟiyēṉmuṉ eḻuntaruḷic ceḻumaṇappū aḷittāy uḷḷamutam ākiyaniṉ tirukkuṟippē tuṇarēṉ uṭaiyavaḷai uṭaiyavaṉē ulakuṇarā oḷiyē kaḷḷamilā aṟivāki avvaṟivuk kaṟivāyk kalantuniṉṟa peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭalē-eṉ kaṇṇē koḷḷutoṟum karaṇamelāṅ karaintukaṉin tiṉikkum koḻuṅkaṉiyē kōṟṟēṉē potuviḷaṅkuṅ kuruvē.
translation: O Lord who possesses the Goddess. O light the world cannot comprehend. You become pure intelligence free of deceit, blending as the awareness within that intelligence. O ocean of great mercy. O my very eye. You are the rich fruit that melts, ripens, and sweetens all my faculties whenever I consume it. O pure honey from the highest branch. O Guru shining in the universal hall. You took a sacred form like clear nectar, graciously appeared before this lowly one, and gave me a rich, fragrant flower. O nectar within, I do not understand your divine intention.
commentary: God is pure intelligence that merges intimately with human awareness. The experience of this divine connection is not dry or abstract. It softens the heart and sweetens the mind, transforming all the senses with a joy as rich as ripe fruit and pure honey.

translit: kaṇviruppaṅ koḷakkaraṇaṅ kaṉintukaṉin turukak karuṇaivaṭi veṭuttaruḷik kaṭaiyēṉmuṉ kalantu maṇviruppaṅ koḷumaṇappū makiḻnteṉakkuk koṭuttu vāḻka-eṉa niṉṟaṉainiṉ maṉakkuṟippē taṟiyēṉ peṇviruppan tavirkkumoru civakāma vallip peṇviruppam peṟa-iruvar periyaruḷaṅ kaḷippap paṇviruppan tarumaṟaikaḷ palapalaniṉ ṟēttap paramacitam paranaṭaṉam payiṉṟapacu patiyē.
translation: O Pasupati performing the supreme dance in Chidambaram. The goddess Sivakama Valli, who dispels worldly desires, attains her loving desire for you. The two great sages rejoice in their hearts. The musical Vedas stand and praise you in many ways. You took a form of compassion and graciously approached me, the lowest of the low. My eyes filled with love, and my faculties melted and ripened. You joyfully gave me a fragrant flower desired by the whole earth and stood there saying, "May you prosper." I do not know your mind's intention.
commentary: Pasupati means the Lord and protector of all living souls, while Chidambaram is the famous temple town that represents the inner sky of human consciousness. Ancient sages and the Vedas (the oldest sacred scriptures) spend eternity praising the Divine from afar. Yet this same supreme power takes a form of pure compassion to stand face to face with the lowest seeker, offering a simple and direct blessing.

translit: uṉṉutaṟkum uṇarvataṟkum uvaṭṭāta vaṭivam oṉṟeṭuttu meyyaṉpar uvakka-eḻun taruḷi muṉṉataṟkōr aṇuttuṇaiyun taramillāc ciṟiyēṉ mukanōkkic ceḻumaṇappū mukamalarntu koṭuttāy tuṉṉutaṟkiṅ karitāmniṉ tiru-uḷḷak kuṟippait tuṇintaṟiyēṉ eṉṉiṉumōr tuṇiviṉuvak kiṉṟēṉ poṉṉutaṟkut tilakameṉuñ civakāma vallip pūvai-oru puṟaṅkaḷippap potunaṭañcey poruḷē.
translation: O Reality performing the universal dance while the lady Sivakama Valli, the auspicious mark on the golden forehead, rejoices on your side. You took a form that never tires the mind or the senses, and you graciously appeared to the delight of true devotees. You looked at the face of this lowly one, who lacks even an atom of merit, and with a blossoming face you gave me a rich, fragrant flower. I cannot certainly know the intention of your divine heart, which is so hard to approach. Even so, I rejoice with a steady conviction.
commentary: The presence of the Divine never exhausts the human mind or senses, bringing instead an endless and fresh joy. The speaker admits having not even a single atom of merit to deserve such attention. Even without understanding the mysterious reasons behind God's choice, the soul finds complete peace and absolute certainty in the gift of grace itself.

translit: tiruvaruṭun tiruvaṭippoṟ cilampacaiya naṭanteṉ cintaiyilē pukuntuniṉpāṟ cērntukalan tiruntāḷ terumaralaṟ ṟuyarntamaṟaic cirattamarnta puṉitai civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippap poruvarumey yaṉpuṭaiyār iruvaruṅkaṇ ṭuvantu pōṟṟamaṇip potuvilnaṭam purikiṉṟa turaiyē paruvaralaṟ ṟaṭicciṟiyēṉ peruvarampeṟ ṟuṉaiyē pāṭukiṉṟēṉ periya-aruṭ paruvamaṭain taṉaṉē.
translation: Walking with golden anklets jingling on her divine feet radiating grace, she entered my mind and merged with you. She is the pure one seated on the high peak of the Vedas, free from delusion. To make the heart of this great goddess Sivakama Valli rejoice, O Lord, you perform the dance in the hall of gems while the two incomparable true devotees watch with joy and praise you. Free from sorrow, I, your humble servant, have received a great boon and sing of you. I have attained the great season of grace.
commentary: The divine power of grace is experienced here as the Goddess Sivakama Valli entering the poet's mind to merge with God. Vallalar describes the Lord dancing to delight her while two legendary sages watch in joy. He says that reaching this state of grace has completely freed him from sorrow.

translit: caṇpaimaṟaik koḻuntumakiḻ tara-amutaṅ koṭuttāḷ tayavuṭaiyāḷ eṉaiyuṭaiyāḷ carvacatti yuṭaiyāḷ ceṇpakappoṉ mēṉiyiṉāḷ ceyyamalarp patattāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippap paṇpakarpoṉ ampalattē āṉanta naṭañcey paramparaniṉ tiruvaruḷaip pāṭukiṉṟēṉ makiḻntu eṇpakarkuṟ ṟaṅkaḷelāṅ kuṇamākak koḷḷum enturai-eṉ ṟeṇṇukiṉṟa eṇṇamata ṉālē.
translation: She lovingly gave nectar to make the tender shoot of the Vedas from Sanpai rejoice. She is compassionate, she claims me as her own, and she possesses all powers. Her golden form is like the champak flower and her feet are red lotuses. To make the heart of this great goddess Sivakama Valli rejoice, O Supreme Lord, you perform the dance of bliss in the golden hall praised by music. I joyfully sing of your divine grace. I do so knowing you are my Lord who accepts all my countless faults as virtues.
commentary: God accepts all of our flaws and treats them as virtues. Vallalar recalls the famous story of the Goddess feeding divine milk to a crying child saint in the town of Sanpai, showing her nature as a compassionate mother. Secure in that same motherly grace, he sings of the Lord's joyful dance.

translit: aruḷuṭaiya nāyaki-eṉ ammai-aṭi yārmēl aṉpuṭaiyāḷ amutaṉaiyāḷ aṟputappeṇ ṇaraci teruḷuṭaiya cintaiyilē tittikkum patattāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippa maruḷuṭaiya māyaiyelān tēyamaṇi maṉṟiṉ mānaṭañcey turaiyēniṉ maṉṉaruḷiṉ tiṟattai iruḷuṭaiya maṉacciṟiyēṉ pāṭukiṉṟēṉ paruvam eytiṉaṉeṉ ṟaṟiñarelām eṇṇimatit tiṭavē.
translation: The gracious Lady is my mother. She loves her devotees, she is like nectar, and she is the wondrous queen of women. Her feet taste sweet in minds possessing clarity. To make the heart of this great goddess Sivakama Valli rejoice, O Lord, you perform the great dance in the hall of gems so that all delusive maya wears away. I, a humble person with a dark mind, sing of the nature of your enduring grace so that all the wise will recognize and respect that I have attained the season of grace.
commentary: The Lord's cosmic dance is what wears away maya, the delusion that binds the mind to the material world. Vallalar calls the Goddess his own mother, whose presence brings absolute clarity. He sings to share the enduring nature of this grace with those who have the wisdom to recognize it.

translit: māṭaiyēṉ piḻai-aṉaittum poṟuttavara maḷittāḷ maṅkaiyarkaḷ nāyakināṉ maṟai-aṇinta patattāḷ tēcuṭaiyāḷ āṉantat teḷḷamuta vaṭivāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippak kācuṭaiya pavakkōṭaik korutiniḻalām potuvil kaṉanaṭañcey turaiyēniṉ karuṇaiyaiyē karuti ācuṭaiyēṉ pāṭukiṉṟēṉ tuyaramelān tavirntēṉ aṉparpeṟum iṉpanilai aṉupavikkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: She forgave all my ignorant mistakes and granted me boons. She is the queen of women. Her feet are adorned by the four Vedas. She is radiant and her form is the clear nectar of bliss. To make the heart of this great goddess Sivakama Valli rejoice, O Lord, you perform the grand dance in the hall that serves as the single shade against the fierce heat of flawed worldly existence. I, a person full of faults, sing only of your grace. I am freed from all sorrow. I am experiencing the state of bliss attained by true devotees.
commentary: The grace of God is the only true shade from the harsh heat of worldly life. Even though he feels full of faults, Vallalar finds that the divine mother forgives everything out of sheer love. Sheltered by this grace, he experiences the exact same bliss that the greatest devotees feel.

translit: poyyāta varameṉakkup purintaparam paraivāṉ pūtamutaṟ karuviyelām pūṭṭuvikkun tiṟattāḷ ceyyāḷuṅ kalaiyavaḷum uruttiraiyum vaṇaṅkum civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippak kaiyāta iṉpanaṭaṅ kaṉakamaṇip potuvil kaḷittiyaṟṟun turaiyēniṉ karuṇaiyaināṉ karuti naiyāta vaṇṇamelām pāṭukiṉṟēṉ paruvam naṇṇiyapuṇ ṇiyarellām nayantumakiḻn tiṭavē.
translation: The Supreme Goddess granted me an unfailing boon. She possesses the power to join together all the elements starting with space and all the instruments of action. She is worshipped by the Goddess of Wealth, the Goddess of Arts, and Rudrani. To make the heart of this great goddess Sivakama Valli rejoice, O Lord, you joyfully perform the sweet dance of bliss in the golden hall of gems. Thinking of your grace, I sing without distress so that all the meritorious ones who have reached the mature season of grace will appreciate it and rejoice.
commentary: The power of grace directs the entire physical universe, from the vastness of space to the actions of our own bodies. Vallalar notes that the traditional goddesses of wealth, art, and destruction all bow to this supreme grace, personified as Sivakama Valli. He sings of the Lord's sweet dance so that others who have reached this spiritual maturity might share in his profound joy.

translit: aṟaṅkaṉinta aruṭkoṭi-eṉ ammai-amu taḷittāḷ akilāṇṭa vallicivā ṉanticaun taricīrt tiṟaṅkalanta nātamaṇic cilampaṇinta patattāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippa maṟaṅkaṉintār mayakkamelān teḷiyamaṇip potuvil mānaṭañcey turaiyēniṉ vaṇmaitaṉai aṭiyēṉ puṟaṅkaviyap pāṭukiṉṟēṉ akaṅkaviyap pāṭum puṇṇiyarel lāmivaṉōr putiyaṉeṉak koḷavē.
translation: The vine of grace ripe with virtue, my Mother who fed me ambrosia, the ruler of the universe, Sivanandi, Soundari, whose feet wear anklets made of sounding gems, Sivakama Valli, the great Goddess. To make her heart rejoice and to clear all the delusion of those steeped in sin, O Lord, you perform the great dance in the ruby hall. I, your servant, sing of your bounty outwardly, so that all the meritorious ones who sing inwardly will consider me a newcomer.
commentary: Vallalar humbly contrasts his own outward singing with the deep, inward communion of advanced devotees. He asks to be welcomed into their company as a newcomer, despite his own sense of unworthiness. He describes God's dance as an act of immense mercy, performed to clear the confusion of those who are lost in wrongdoing.

translit: uḷḷamutam ūṟṟuvikkum uttami-eṉ ammai ōṅkāra pīṭamicaip pāṅkāka iruntāḷ teḷḷamuta vaṭivuṭaiyāḷ celvanalkum patattāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippak kaḷḷamaṟut taruḷviḷakkum vaḷḷaṉmaṇip potuvil kālniṟuttik kāleṭuttuk kaḷittāṭun turaiyē eḷḷalaṟap pāṭukiṉṟēṉ niṉṉaruḷai aruḷāl ippāṭṭiṟ piḻaikuṟittal eṅṅaṉamiṅ ṅaṉamē.
translation: The noble one who makes ambrosia spring in the heart, my Mother who sits beautifully on the seat of Omkara, whose form is clear ambrosia, whose feet grant wealth, Sivakama Valli, the great Goddess. To make her heart rejoice, O generous Lord, you cut off deceit and illuminate grace, planting one foot and lifting the other to dance in joy in the ruby hall. I sing of your grace by your grace, free of mockery. How could faults be found in this song here?
commentary: A song born entirely of divine grace cannot contain any faults. Vallalar says he sings only by God's own grace, praising the Lord who roots out deceit and brings truth to light. The Goddess is described as sitting on the Omkara, the primordial sound "Om", bringing spiritual ambrosia to the devotee's heart.

translit: pārpūtta pacuṅkoṭipoṟ pālaivayarkaḷ araci paramparaiciṟ paraiparā parainimalai yāti cīrpūtta teyvamaṟaic cilampaṇinta patattāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippa ērpūtta maṇimaṉṟil iṉpanaṭam puriyum eṉṉarumait turaiyēniṉ iṉṉaruḷai niṉaintu kārpūtta kaṉaimaḻaipōl kaṇkaḷiṉnīr corintu kaṉintumikap pāṭukiṉṟa kaḷippai-aṭain taṉaṉē.
translation: The green vine that bloomed on earth, the queen of golden women, the supreme one, the consciousness, the absolute, the flawless one, the primal one, whose feet wear anklets of the divine and excellent Vedas, Sivakama Valli, the great Goddess. To make her heart rejoice, O my precious Lord, you perform the dance of bliss in the beautiful ruby hall. Thinking of your sweet grace, I shed tears from my eyes like a heavy rain from dark clouds, and I have attained the joy of singing with a deeply melting heart.
commentary: Remembering God's grace brings Vallalar to tears of overwhelming, melting joy. He weeps like a heavy rain, deeply moved by the bliss of the Lord's dance. The Goddess is praised as the supreme consciousness, wearing the ancient scriptures known as the Vedas as the ringing anklets on her feet.

translit: pūraṇiciṟ pōtaiciva pōkiciva yōki pūvaiyarkaḷ nāyaki-aim pūtamuntā ṉaṉāḷ tēraṇiyum neṭuvitit tillainaka ruṭaiyāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippa ēraṇiyum maṇimaṉṟil iṉpavaṭi vāki iṉpanaṭam purikiṉṟa emmuṭaiya turaiyē tāraṇiyil uṉaippāṭun tarattai-aṭain taṉaṉeṉ taṉmaiyelām naṉmai-eṉac cammatitta vāṟē.
translation: The perfect one, the pure consciousness, the experiencer of Siva, the ascetic of Siva, the queen of women, she who became the five elements herself, the lady of Thillai city with long streets adorned with chariots, Sivakama Valli, the great Goddess. To make her heart rejoice, O our Lord, you become the form of bliss and perform the dance of bliss in the beautiful ruby hall. I have attained the fitness to sing of you on this earth, for you have accepted all my nature as good.
commentary: Vallalar marvels that God has chosen to accept his entire nature as good. This unconditional divine acceptance is what gives him the standing to sing these praises on earth. The Goddess whose joy inspires the Lord's dance is here identified as the very fabric of the universe, embodying the five elements of earth, water, fire, air, and space.

translit: taṉṉoḷiyil ulakamelān tāṅkukiṉṟa vimalai taṟparai-am paraimāci tamparaiciṟ catti ciṉṉavaya tiṉileṉṉai āḷaniṉak kicaittāḷ civakāma valliperun tēvi-uḷaṅ kaḷippa maṉṉiyapoṉ maṇippotuvil iṉpanaṭam purintu vayaṅkukiṉṟa turaiyēniṉ mākaruṇait tiṟattai uṉṉi-uvan tuṇarnturukip pāṭukiṉṟēṉ eṅkaḷ uṭaiyāṉē niṉṉaruḷiṉ aṭaiyāḷam ituvē.
translation: The pure one who supports all worlds in her own light, the supreme one, the space, the great space of consciousness, the energy of consciousness, she consented for you to rule me at a young age. Sivakama Valli, the great Goddess. To make her heart rejoice, O shining Lord, you perform the dance of bliss in the enduring golden ruby hall. I think of your great compassion, rejoice, realize it, and melt as I sing. O our Master, this itself is the mark of your grace.
commentary: The ability to feel God's compassion, to melt with joy, and to sing with a full heart is itself the truest proof of having received divine grace. Vallalar looks back to his childhood, recognizing that the Goddess approved of the Lord taking charge of his life from a very young age. Her light, he says, is the pure consciousness that supports all the worlds.

note: Editor's note: verse 3, vāḷ (வாள்) means light; it can also mean a sword (Sa. Mu. Kandasamy Pillai).
translit: aruḷuṭaiyāy aṭiyēṉnāṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu maruḷuṭaiyēṉ taṉai-aḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē makiḻntaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai vaṇṇameṉṟaṉ maṉamum teruḷuṭaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum terikiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ cintai-uru kilatē iruḷuṭaiya cilaiyumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord of grace, I am your servant. I do not know the greatness of your grace. You forgave all the faults of my ignorant rejection. You called me, a person filled with delusion, and joyfully gave it back into my hands. The nature of this great compassion has not left my mind and my clear eyes. Even though it still remains visible, my heart does not melt. It is not impossible for even a dark stone to melt at this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: The divine offers boundless forgiveness. Even when a person rejects grace out of ignorance, God lovingly places it right back into their hands. The central sorrow expressed here is emotional numbness. The speaker is fully aware of this immense mercy, yet he laments that his heart remains unmelted, noting that even a dark, lifeless stone would soften if shown such love.

translit: aṉpuṭaiyāy aṭiyēṉnāṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu vaṉpuṭaiyēṉ taṉai-aḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē valintaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai vaṇṇameṉṟaṉ maṉamum iṉpuṭaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ veyyamaṉam urukā eṉpuṭaiya uṭalumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord of love, I am your servant. I do not know the greatness of your grace. You forgave all the faults of my ignorant rejection. You called me, a person filled with hardness, and forcefully gave it back into my hands. The nature of this great compassion has not left my mind and my joyful eyes. Even though it still shines brightly, my cruel mind does not melt. It is not impossible for even a body of bone to melt at this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: The intensity of divine grace is so strong that it pursues the soul even when it is stubborn. The Lord practically forces grace back upon the devotee, overpowering all resistance. This active compassion stands in sharp contrast to human rigidity. A mind that cannot soften is harder than dry bones, which would easily dissolve in the presence of such love.

translit: āḷuṭaiyāy ciṟiyēṉnāṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu vāḷuṭaiyēṉtaṉai-aḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē valintaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai vaṇṇameṉṟaṉ maṉamum nīḷuṭaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum nikaḻkiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ neñcamuru kilatē ēḷuṭaiya malaiyumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord who rules me, I am small and do not know the greatness of your grace. You forgave all the faults of my ignorant rejection. You called me, a person possessing a sword-like cruelty, and forcefully gave it back into my hands. The nature of this great compassion has not left my mind and my long eyes. Even though it still manifests, my heart does not melt. It is not impossible for even a firm mountain to melt at this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: The contrast between divine patience and human flaw deepens here. Past ignorance is seen as a sword-like cruelty, yet God responds only by pouring out grace. There is a painful disconnect between seeing this mercy clearly and feeling it emotionally. A solid mountain would melt at such forgiveness before an unyielding human heart.

translit: āramutē aṭiyēṉnāṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu vāramuṟa eṉaiyaḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē makiḻntaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai vaṇṇameṉṟaṉ maṉamum cīruṭaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum terikiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ cintai-uru kilatē īramilā maramumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O rare ambrosia, I am your servant. I do not know the greatness of your grace. You forgave all the faults of my ignorant rejection. You called me with love and joyfully gave it back into my hands. The nature of this great compassion has not left my mind and my excellent eyes. Even though it still remains visible, my heart does not melt. It is not impossible for even a dry tree without moisture to melt at this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: God is addressed here as rare ambrosia, a sweet nectar of life. The divine calls out with pure love rather than punishment for past rejections. The tragedy of the stubborn mind is its unresponsiveness. Even a dead, dry tree would soften in devotion when touched by this level of compassion.

translit: aṟputaniṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyēṉnāṉ ciṟitum aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai āyiramum poṟuttu vaṟpuṟuvēṉ taṉai-aḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē valintaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai vaṇṇameṉṟaṉ maṉamum kaṟpuṭaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum kāṇkiṉṟa teṉṉiṉumeṉ kaṉmaṉamō urukā iṟpuṭaiya irumpumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord of wonder, I do not know even a little of the greatness of your grace. You forgave the thousands of faults of my ignorant rejection. You called me, a stubborn person, and forcefully gave it back into my hands. The nature of this great compassion has not left my mind and my chaste eyes. Even though it is still seen, my stony mind does not melt. It is not impossible for even hard iron to melt at this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: Total forgiveness wipes away thousands of faults without hesitation. The core spiritual experience here is the recognition of one's own smallness in the face of absolute, unmerited grace. True devotion requires the total melting of the heart. To remain rigid and unmoved by this immense love is to be harder than solid iron.

translit: āṇṭavaniṉ aruḷarumai aṟiyātē tirintēṉ aṉṟiraviṉ maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu vēṇṭi-eṉai arukaḻaittut tirumpavumeṉ karattē mika-aḷitta aruḷvaṇṇam viṉaiyuṭaiyēṉ maṉamum kāṇtakaiya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum kāṇkiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ karutturukak kāṇēṉ īṇṭurukāk karaṭumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord! I wandered without knowing the preciousness of your Grace. You forgave all my faults of refusing it that night. You desired me, called me near, and again placed the nature of your Grace abundantly into my hands. Although it remains visible even now and never leaves the mind and seeing eyes of this karmic being, I do not see my heart melting. Even a hard unmelting rock would easily melt for this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: God's forgiveness is absolute, reaching out even when we turn away. Vallalar describes a profound personal moment where he initially refused divine Grace, only for God to call him back and place it directly into his hands. He wonders at his own numbness, noting that such boundless compassion would melt solid rock. The divine is addressed as Siva, a name for the ultimate reality, seen here as a tender, dancing flame of grace.

translit: aracēniṉ tiruvaruḷiṉ arumai-oṉṟum aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu viravumaṉpil eṉai-aḻaittu valiyavumeṉ karattē viyantaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai viḷakkameṉṟaṉ maṉamum uravumalark kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum oḷirkiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ uḷḷamuru kilatē iravuniṟat tavarumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O King! I know nothing of the preciousness of your holy Grace. You forgave all my faults of refusing it in ignorance. With mingling love, you called me and forced into my hands that wondrous manifestation of your great compassion. Although it still shines and never leaves my mind and my powerful flower-like eyes, my heart does not melt. Even those with the nature of the dark night would easily melt for this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: Divine love does not wait for perfect understanding. Even when faced with a refusal born of ignorance, God actively forces compassion upon the soul. Vallalar contrasts this radiant, overwhelming grace with the spiritual stubbornness he feels inside, saying that even the darkest and most hardened minds would soften before such a gift.

translit: aiyāniṉ aruṭperumai arumai-oṉṟum aṟiyēṉ aṟiyātē maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu meyyā-aṉ ṟeṉai-aḻaittu valiyavumeṉ karattē viyantaḷitta peruṅkaruṇai viḷakkameṉṟaṉ maṉamum kaiyātu kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum kāṇkiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ karutturukak kāṇēṉ eyyāvaṉ paralumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Master! I know nothing of the preciousness and greatness of your Grace. You forgave all my faults of refusing it in ignorance. O Truth, you called me that day and forced into my hands that wondrous manifestation of your great compassion. Although it is still seen and never leaves my mind and my unfailing eyes, I do not see my heart melting. Even unyielding hard pebbles would easily melt for this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: The vision of divine compassion is vivid and constant, remaining brightly before the seeker's eyes. Yet, a deep sense of unworthiness makes Vallalar feel disconnected from his own experience. He marvels that God's grace was given to him despite his past ignorance, feeling that even lifeless pebbles would be moved by such relentless love.

translit: appāniṉ tiruvaruṭpēr amutarumai aṟiyēṉ aṉṟiraviṉ maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu ippāril eṉai-aḻaittu valiyavumeṉ karattē iṉitaṉitta peruṅkaruṇai iṉpameṉṟaṉ maṉamum tuppāya kaṇkaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum tōṉṟukiṉṟa tāyiṉumit tuṭṭaneñcam urukā eppāvi neñcumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Father! I do not know the preciousness of the great nectar of your holy Grace. You forgave all my faults of refusing it that night. You called me in this world and sweetly forced into my hands the bliss of your great compassion. Although it still appears and never leaves my mind and my pure eyes, this wicked heart does not melt. The heart of any sinner would easily melt for this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: Grace is offered as a sweet nectar that brings pure bliss. God's compassion is so vast that it overlooks outright rejection, calling the soul back to bestow the very gift that was refused. Vallalar feels that his own heart must be uniquely stubborn to remain unmoved by this, believing that even the worst of sinners would melt in gratitude at such unconditional forgiveness.

translit: ammāṉniṉ aruṭcatti arumai-oṉṟum aṟiyēṉ aṉṟiraviṉ maṟuttapiḻai attaṉaiyum poṟuttu vemmāyai akaṟṟi-eṉai arukaḻaitteṉ karattē mika-aḷitta peruṅkaruṇai viḷakkameṉṟaṉ maṉamum maimmāḻai viḻikaḷumviṭ ṭakalātē iṉṉum vatikiṉṟa tāyiṉumeṉ vañcaneñcam urukā emmāya neñcumitaṟ kurukalari talavē iṉittanaṭam purintumaṉṟil taṉittacivak koḻuntē.
translation: O Lord! I know nothing of the preciousness of the power of your Grace. You forgave all my faults of refusing it that night. Dispelling cruel illusion, you called me near and placed abundantly into my hands the manifestation of your great compassion. Although it still resides and never leaves my mind and my dark collyrium-lined eyes, my deceitful heart does not melt. Any heart steeped in illusion would easily melt for this. O peerless tender flame of Siva performing the sweet dance in the Hall!
commentary: True grace actively dispels the cruel illusions that keep us separated from the divine. God removes these blindfolds and places the clear light of compassion directly into the seeker's hands. Facing this overwhelming reality, Vallalar laments his own perceived deceitfulness, feeling that even a mind completely lost in worldly deception would break open and melt before such pure love.

translit: cēlōṭum iṇaintaviḻic celviperun tēvi civakama valliyoṭu civapōka vaṭivāy mēlōṭu kīḻnaṭuvuṅ kaṭantōṅku veḷiyil viḷaṅkiyaniṉ tiru-uruvai uḷaṅkoḷumpō tellām pālōṭu paḻampiḻintu tēṉkalantu pākum pacuneyyuṅ kūṭṭi-uṇṭa paṭi-iruppa teṉṟāl mālōṭu kāṇkiṉṟa kaṇkaḷukkaṅ kirunta vaṇṇaminta vaṇṇameṉa eṇṇavumoṇ ṇātē.
translation: Whenever I hold in my heart your sacred form shining in the exalted space that transcends the top, bottom, and middle, manifesting as the embodiment of supreme bliss along with the great goddess Sivakami whose eyes rival the carp, it feels like tasting squeezed fruit mixed with milk, honey, syrup, and fresh cow's ghee. If merely thinking of it feels like this, it is impossible even to imagine the state of the eyes that gaze upon it with intense love.
commentary: The divine form exists in a space beyond all physical dimensions, yet it can be held in the heart. Remembering this presence brings a tangible sweetness, as vivid as tasting honey, fruit, and ghee mixed together. If merely thinking of God yields such physical delight, the joy of directly seeing the divine is beyond human imagination.

translit: iṉparuḷum peruntāyeṉ itayēttē iruntāḷ iṟaiviyoṭum ampalattē ilaṅkiniṉ vaṭivai vaṉpuṟukaṉ maṉakkoṭiyēṉ niṉaikkumiṭat tellām maṉaṅkaraintu cukamayamāy vayaṅkumeṉil antō aṉpuṭaiyār niṉṟuniṉṟu kaṇṭukoṇṭa kālam āṅkavarkaṭ kiruntavaṇṇam eṅkevarkaḷ pukalvār tuṉpuṟutal illāta cuttanilai uṭaiyār toḻukiṉṟa tōṟumakiḻn teḻukiṉṟa turaiyē.
translation: O Lord who joyously arises whenever those in a pure sorrowless state worship you. Whenever I, a cruel person with a hard stony heart, think of your form shining in the assembly along with the Goddess, the great mother who grants bliss and dwells in my heart, my heart melts and becomes pure bliss. If it is so for me, who can ever describe the state of those loving devotees who stand and gaze upon it endlessly?
commentary: The speaker feels unworthy, calling his own heart hard and stony. Yet even his flawed meditation melts his mind into pure bliss. This contrast highlights the power of divine grace, which softens the hardest heart and brings joy to true devotees.

translit: civayōka cantitarum tēvi-ula kuṭaiyāḷ civakāma valliyoṭuñ cempoṉmaṇip potuvil navayōka urumuṭikkaṇ viḷaṅkiyaniṉ vaṭivai nāykkaṭaiyēṉ nāṉniṉaitta nāḷeṉakkē maṉamum pavayōka intiyamum iṉpamaya māṉa paṭi-eṉṟāl meyyaṟiviṟ paḻuttaperuṅ kuṇattut tavayōkar kaṇṭaviṭat tavarkkirunta vaṇṇam taṉṉai-inta vaṇṇameṉa eṉṉai uraippatuvē.
translation: On the day I, a person lower than a dog, thought of your form shining at the crown of the nine yogic forms in the public hall of pure gold and gems, along with Sivakami, the goddess who rules the world and grants the union of divine yoga, my mind and my worldly senses became entirely filled with bliss. If it is so for me, how can I describe the state of the ascetics of great virtue, ripened in true knowledge, when they behold it?
commentary: Even the ordinary worldly senses are transformed into total joy simply by holding the Lord in thought. The divine form is envisioned at the peak of yogic attainment, accompanied by the Goddess who grants this union. The speaker continues to marvel at how this grace elevates even those who feel utterly low, leaving the experience of true ascetics completely beyond description.

translit: cittiyelām aḷittaciva catti-eṉai yuṭaiyāḷ civakāma valliyoṭu civañāṉap potuvil muttiyelān taraviḷaṅkum muṉṉavaniṉ vaṭivai mūṭamaṉac ciṟiyēṉnāṉ nāṭavarum poḻutu puttiyelām oṉṟākip puttamutam uṇṭāṟ pōlumirup patu-ataṟku mēlumirup patuvēl patti-elām uṭaiyavarkaḷ kāṇumiṭat tirukkum paṭitāṉep paṭiyō-ip paṭi-eṉpa taritē.
translation: O primal Lord, your form shines in the hall of divine wisdom to grant every kind of liberation, alongside Sivakami, the divine energy who possesses me and grants all attainments. When I, a lowly person with a foolish mind, seek it, my intellect unifies and it feels like drinking fresh nectar or even something beyond that. If it is so for me, what must the state be for those filled with perfect devotion when they behold it? It is impossible to say it is exactly like this.
commentary: Focusing on the divine form gathers and unifies a scattered mind. This singular focus brings a feeling sweeter than fresh nectar. The divine energy, personified as the Goddess Sivakami, grants this total liberation and all spiritual attainments.

translit: teyvamelām vaṇaṅkukiṉṟa tēvi-eṉai aḷittāḷ civakāma valliyoṭu tirumali-am palattē caivamelān taraviḷaṅku niṉvaṭivaik koṭiyēṉ tāṉniṉaitta pōteṉaiyē nāṉniṉaitta nilaiyēl aivakai-in tiyaṅkaṭantār kaṇṭaviṭat tirunta aṉupavattiṉ vaṇṇamatai yārpukala vallār uyvakai-an nāḷ uraitta taṉṟiyumin nāḷil untiravil vantuṇarvu tantaciva kuruvē.
translation: O divine Guru, you taught me the way of salvation in days past, and on this day you came in the middle of the night and granted me awareness. Your form shines in the auspicious assembly, alongside Sivakami, the goddess worshipped by all divinities who nurtured me, granting all spiritual states. When I, a cruel person, merely think of it, I become aware of my true self. If it is so for me, who can possibly describe the experience of those who have transcended the five senses when they behold it?
commentary: The Lord acts as the ultimate spiritual teacher, granting profound awareness even in the dark of night. Simply remembering this divine presence allows a person to awaken to their true, inner self. If a single passing thought brings such clear self-realization, the experience of masters who have transcended their senses is truly impossible to put into words.

translit: teṉmoḻippeṇ ṇaraci-aruṭ celvameṉak kaḷittāḷ civakāma valliyoṭu cempoṉmaṇip potuvil vāṉmoḻiya niṉṟilaṅku niṉvaṭivaic ciṟiyēṉ maṉaṅkoṇṭa kālattē vāytta-aṉu pavattai nāṉmoḻiya muṭiyātēl aṉparkaṇṭa kālam naṇṇiyamey vaṇṇamatai eṇṇi-evar pukalvār nūṉmoḻikkum poruṭkummika nuṇṇiyatāy ñāṉa nōkkuṭaiyār nōkkiṉilē nōkkiyameyp poruḷē.
translation: The queen of the southern language gave me the wealth of grace. O True Reality, perceived only in the vision of those possessing the gaze of wisdom, subtler than the words of scriptures and their meanings! You stand shining in the golden hall of red gold and gems alongside Sivakama Valli, beyond the praise of the heavens. If my lowly mind cannot express the experience it gained when it grasped your form, who can ever conceive of and describe the true state attained by true lovers when they behold you?
commentary: The divine reality is far too subtle to be captured by the words of religious scriptures. It can only be known through the direct gaze of spiritual wisdom. Vallalar marvels that if his own mind cannot express the fraction of grace he has felt, the overwhelming joy experienced by true lovers of God must be entirely beyond human speech.

translit: ciṟṟiṭai-em perumāṭṭi tēvartoḻum patattāḷ civakāma valliyoṭu ciṟantamaṇip potuvil uṟṟiṭainiṉ ṟilaṅkukiṉṟa niṉvaṭivaik koṭiyēṉ uṉṉuntoṟum uḷamiḷakit taḷataḷa-eṉ ṟuruki maṟṟiṭaiyil valiyāmal āṭukiṉṟa teṉṟāl vaḻiyaṭiyar viḻikaḷiṉāl makiḻntukaṇṭa kālam paṟṟiṭaiyā tāṅkavarkaṭ kiruntavaṇṇan taṉaiyār pakarvārē pakarvārēl pakavaṉnikar vārē.
translation: Our Great Lady with a slender waist is Sivakama Valli, whose feet the gods worship. You stand beside her, shining in the excellent gem-studded hall. Whenever I, a cruel person, think of your form, my heart softens, melting completely and dancing unsteadily. If this is my state, who can describe the unwavering state of your steadfast devotees when they joyfully behold you with their eyes? If anyone can speak of it, they are equal to God Himself.
commentary: Just the thought of the divine presence causes Vallalar’s heart to melt and his body to tremble unsteadily. He wonders at the profound, unwavering peace experienced by advanced devotees who live continually in that vision. Their spiritual state is so exalted, he says, that anyone capable of describing it would have to be equal to God Himself.

translit: āramutam aṉaiyavaḷeṉ ammai-api rāmi āṉanta valliyoṭum ampalattē viḷaṅkum pēramuta mayamāmuṉ tiruvaṭivaik kuṟittup pēcukiṉṟa pōtumaṇam vīcukiṉṟa toṉṟō cīramuta māki-ellān tittippa taṉpōr ciṟitumilāk kaṭaippulaiyēṉ tiṟattukkiṅ keṉṟāl ūramutap pēraṉpar pēcumiṭat tavarpāl uṟṟavaṇṇam iṟṟiteṉṉa uṉṉamuṭi yātē.
translation: My mother Abhirami, Ananda Valli, is like rare nectar. You shine alongside her in the hall. When I speak of your sacred form made of great nectar, it emits a sweet fragrance. It also becomes excellent nectar, making everything taste sweet. If this happens to me, a base one with not even a little love, it is impossible to even imagine the state attained by devotees of great and flowing love when they speak of you.
commentary: The experience of the divine is deeply physical and sensory, filling the air with fragrance and the mouth with the taste of sweet nectar. Vallalar calls himself a base one without a drop of true love, yet he still receives this overwhelming sweetness just by speaking of God. He leaves the reader to imagine the absolute bliss enjoyed by those whose hearts overflow with real devotion.

translit: poṟpatattāḷ eṉṉaḷaviṟ poṉṉācai tavirttāḷ pūraṇi-ā ṉantaciva pōkavalli yōṭu coṟpatamuṅ kaṭantamaṉṟil viḷaṅkiyaniṉ vaṭivait tūymaiyilēṉ nāṉeṇṇun tōṟummaṉam iḷakic ciṟpatattiṟ parañāṉa mayamākum eṉṟāl teḷivuṭaiyār kāṇkiṉṟa tiṟattilavark kirukkum naṟpatamet taṉmaiyatō uraipparitu mikavum nātamuṭi taṉiṟpuriyum ñāṉanaṭat taracē.
translation: O King of the dance of wisdom, performed at the crown of sound! The lady with golden feet removed my desire for gold. You shine in the hall that transcends words alongside Poorani, the creeper of blissful Siva experience. Whenever I, an impure person, think of your form, my mind softens and becomes the embodiment of supreme wisdom in the realm of consciousness. If this is my state, the excellent state attained by clear-minded devotees when they behold you is extremely difficult to describe.
commentary: True spiritual grace entirely removes the craving for material wealth, just as Vallalar notes the Goddess freed him from his desire for gold. When he turns his attention to the divine, his ordinary, flawed mind dissolves and transforms into pure, supreme wisdom. If a passing thought can bring such a profound transformation, the unbroken vision granted to the purest saints remains a mystery beyond all words.

translit: eṉpiḻaiyā vaiyumpoṟuttāṉ eṉṉaimuṉṉē aḷittāyḷa iṟaiviciva kāmavalli eṉṉammai yuṭaṉē iṉpaṭi vāyppotuvil ilaṅkiyaniṉ vaṇṇam iṟṟeṉanāṉ niṉaittiṭuṅkāl eṟṟeṉavum moḻivēṉ aṉpuruvāy atu-atuvāy aḷintapaḻam āki appaḻaccā ṟāki-ataṉ aruñcuvaiyum āki eṉpuruka maṉañāṉa mayamākum eṉṟāl eṟṟōmey aṉpuṭaiyār iyaintukaṇṭa iṭattē.
translation: She forgave all my faults and brought me forth in the beginning. She is the Goddess, Sivakama Valli, my mother. You shine alongside her in the open hall of bliss. When I think of your nature, how can I ever express it? It becomes the form of love. It becomes everything. It becomes a ripe fruit, the juice of that fruit, and its rare sweetness. My bones melt and my mind becomes the embodiment of wisdom. If this happens to me, what can be said of the state of true devotees when they unite with you and behold your vision?
commentary: The thought of God is not an abstract idea, but a living force that takes the shape of absolute love. Vallalar compares it to a ripe fruit, its sweet juice, and the very essence of sweetness itself, seeping in so deeply that his bones physically melt in devotion. This sweetness turns the ordinary mind into pure spiritual wisdom, offering a fleeting glimpse of the boundless joy waiting for those who fully unite with the divine.

translit: karumpaṉaiyāḷ eṉṉiraṇṭu kaṇkaḷilē iruntāḷ kaṟpakappoṉ valliciva kāmavalli yuṭaṉē virumpumaṇip potuviṉilē viḷaṅkiyaniṉ vaṭivai viṉaiyuṭaiyēṉ niṉaikkiṉṟa vēḷaiyileṉ pukalvēṉ irumpaṉaiya maṉamnekiḻntu nekiḻnturuki orupēr iṉpamaya mākumeṉil aṉparkaṇṭa kālam arumpimalarn tiṭṭacivā ṉanta-aṉu pavattai yāraṟivār nī-aṟivāy ampalattem aracē.
translation: She who is sweet as sugarcane remained in my two eyes. When I, burdened by past actions, merely think of your form shining in the beloved gem-adorned Hall alongside the golden Kalpaka vine Sivakami, what can I say? My iron-like heart softens, melts, and becomes a state of immense bliss. If this happens just by thinking, who can comprehend the experience of divine bliss that blossoms when true devotees actually behold you? Only you know, our King of the Hall.
commentary: The mere thought of the divine presence is enough to melt a hard, iron-like heart into absolute joy. If simply picturing this vision in the mind brings such overwhelming bliss, the actual experience of true devotees must be completely beyond human understanding. Only God, the King of the Hall, knows its true depth.

translit: kāmacatti yuṭaṉkaḷikkum kālaiyilē aṭiyēṉ kaṉañāṉa cattiyaiyum kalantukoḷap purintāḷ vāmacatti civakāma valliyoṭum potuvil vayaṅkiyaniṉ tiruvaṭiyai maṉaṅkoḷumpō tellām āmacattaṉ eṉumeṉakkē āṉanta veḷḷam atutatumpip poṅkivaḻin tāṭumeṉil antō ēmacattar eṉumaṟiñar kaṇṭaviṭat tirunta iṉpa-aṉu pavapperumai yāvarpukal vārē.
translation: While I was rejoicing with the power of worldly desire, she made me unite with the supreme power of wisdom. Whenever my mind grasps your holy feet shining in the Hall alongside the beautiful power Sivakami, a flood of bliss brims, overflows, and surges within me, a weak and powerless man. If this is so for me, who can ever describe the greatness of the blissful experience attained by those wise and powerful sages when they behold you?
commentary: Divine grace lifts the soul out of worldly attachments and fills it with supreme wisdom. Even a person who feels weak and powerless experiences an overflowing flood of joy just by holding God's feet in their mind. If a fleeting thought brings this much bliss, the direct vision granted to advanced sages remains completely indescribable.

translit: akkō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ ayaṉmutalōr neṭuṅkālam mayaṉmutalnīt tiruntu mikkōla miṭavumavark karuḷāmal iruḷāl mikamaruṇṭu matiyiliyāy viṉaiviriya virittu ikkōlat tuṭaṉiruntēṉ aṉpaṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṉ eṉaikkaruti eṉṉiṭattē eḻuntaruḷi eṉaiyum takkōṉeṉ ṟulakicaippat taṉvaṇamoṉ ṟaḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oh friend, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What shall I say? Brahma and the other gods spent a long time renouncing illusion and crying out loudly. He did not grant them grace. I was deeply bewildered by darkness. I lacked understanding and multiplied my karmic actions. I remained in this worldly form. I knew no love. I am small. Yet thinking of me, He came to my place and granted me His own radiant form so that the world might praise me as a worthy man. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Divine grace does not always reward traditional spiritual endurance. The creator god Brahma spent ages renouncing the world without receiving grace. Yet the divine presence actively sought out the poet despite his worldly confusion and karmic flaws. The closing image names Sivakama Valli, the goddess who represents divine grace, watching the joyful, sweet dance of the supreme light.

translit: accē-ī taticayamī taticayamī pukalvēṉ arimutalōr neṭuṅkālam purimutalnīt tiruntu naccōla miṭavumavark karuḷāmal maruḷāl nāḷkaḻittuk kōḷkoḻikkum naṭaināyiṟ kaṭaiyēṉ eccōṭum iḻiviṉukkoḷ ṟillēṉnāṉ pollēṉ eṉaikkaruti yāṉirukkum iṭattileḻun taruḷit tarcōti vaṇapporuḷoṉ ṟeṉakkaḷittuk kaḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oh friend, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What shall I say? Vishnu and the other gods spent a long time renouncing their attachments and crying out with longing. He did not grant them grace. I wasted my days in delusion. I am lower than a wandering dog that sifts through refuse. I hold nothing but degradation. I am wicked. Yet thinking of me, He came to the place where I live. He joyfully gave me the true substance of His own Jothi. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: The divine light gives itself freely to the lowest, bypassing the highest cosmic deities. Even the protector god Vishnu cried out with longing in vain. Meanwhile, the poet compares himself to a dog scavenging in refuse, yet he receives the true substance of Jothi (divine light). Grace operates on its own boundless compassion, ignoring conventional scales of spiritual merit.

translit: attō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ antaṇarel lārummaṟai mantaṇamē pukaṉṟu ottōla miṭavumavark koruciṟitum aruḷāṉ ōtiyaṉaiyēṉ vitiyaṟiyēṉoruṅkēṉvaṉ kuraṅkēṉ ittōṭa mikavuṭaiyēṉ kaṭaināykkuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ eṉaikkaruti yāṉirukkum iṭantēṭi naṭantu cattōṭa muṟa-eṉakkum cittiyoṉṟu koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oh friend, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What shall I say? All the sages chanted the secrets of the Vedas and cried out together. He did not grant them even a little grace. I am like a chameleon. I do not know my duty. I never concentrate my mind. I am a wild monkey. I possess immense faults. I am lower than the lowest dog. Yet thinking of me, He walked in search of the place where I live. He gave me a supreme attainment to unite with the truth. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Mastery of scriptures and sacred chants cannot force the divine hand. Sages recited the deepest secrets of the Vedas to no avail, while the divine walked directly to the poet, who admits his mind is as restless as a wild monkey. The reward given is a supreme spiritual attainment, proving that true union is a pure gift rather than a prize won through ritual knowledge.

translit: antē-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aṟivuṭaiyār aimpulaṉum ceṟivuṭaiyār āki vantōla miṭavumavark karuḷāmal maruḷāl maṉañceṉṟa vaḻiyellān tiṉañceṉṟa matiyēṉ entē-eṉ ṟulakiyampa viḻivaḻiyē uḻalvēṉ eṉaikkaruti eḷiyēṉnāṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu cantōṭa muṟa-eṉakkum taṉvaṇamoṉ ṟaḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oh friend, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What shall I say? The wise mastered their five senses, came to Him, and cried out. He did not grant them grace. I am a fool whose mind wanders every day into delusion, following whatever path it chooses. I roam along the path of degradation as the world points out my low state. Yet thinking of me, He reached the place where I live as a poor wretch. He joyfully granted me His own radiant form. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Controlling the five senses is often seen as the ultimate spiritual requirement, but here it is shown to be completely insufficient on its own. The wise who perfectly mastered themselves were left waiting. The divine instead sought out a self-proclaimed fool whose mind wandered endlessly, offering a warm message that grace seeks us exactly where we are broken.

translit: appā-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aruntavarkaḷ virumpimika varunti-uḷam muyaṉṟu ippāril iruntiṭavum avarkkaruḷāṉ maruḷāl ivvulaka naṭaiviḻaintu vevviṉaiyē purintu eppālum iḻintumaṉat ticcaipuri kiṉṟēṉ eṉaikkaruti yāṉirukkum iṭantēṭi aṭaintu tappāta oḷivaṇṇan tanteṉṉai aḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oh friend, this is a wonder. This is a wonder. What shall I say? Those performing rare austerities yearned for Him. They suffered greatly, strove in their hearts, and remained on this earth. He did not grant them grace. Out of delusion, I desired worldly ways. I committed cruel deeds. I degraded myself everywhere and simply followed my mind's cravings. Yet thinking of me, He searched out the place where I live and reached it. He gave me His unfailing form of light and saved me. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Severe physical austerities and bodily suffering do not guarantee spiritual liberation. Those who tortured themselves through harsh disciplines were passed over, while the divine went out searching for someone caught up in worldly cravings. The gift of this unfailing light of grace is entirely unearned, shattering the idea that humans must perfect themselves before the divine will approach them.

translit: ammā-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aṉparelām muyaṉṟumuyaṉ ṟiṉpaṭaivāṉ varunti emmāyeṉ ṟēttiṭavum avarkkaruḷāṉ maruḷāl itunaṉmai itutīmai eṉṟuniṉai yāmē maimmāliṟ kaḷiciṟantu valviṉaiyē puriyum vaṅcakaṉēṉ taṉaikkaruti vantumakiḻ teṉakkum tammāṉa muṟaviyantu cammāṉa maḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: O mother, this is a wonder, this is a wonder, what shall I say? All the devotees strive and strive, suffering to attain bliss. They praise him as our Great One, yet he does not grant them grace. Deluded, without thinking about what is good and what is evil, I rejoice in dark ignorance and perform only cruel deeds. I am a deceiver. Yet, considering me, he came and rejoiced, marveled at his own greatness, and bestowed honor upon me. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: God gives grace freely, even to those completely lost in ignorance. Vallalar marvels that dedicated devotees exhaust themselves trying to earn divine favor, while God simply steps in and honors someone who has done nothing to deserve it.

translit: āvā-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aṭiyarelām niṉaintuniṉain taviḻntakanek kuruki ōvāmal araṟṟiṭavum avarkkaruḷāṉ māyai ulakaviṭa yāṉantam uvantuvantu muyaṉṟu tīvāya narakiṉiṭai viḻakkaṭavēṉ eṉaittāṉ civayānama eṉappukalum teḷivuṭaiyaṉ ākkic cāvāta varaṅkoṭuttut taṉakkaṭimai paṇittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Ah, this is a wonder, this is a wonder, what shall I say? All the devotees think and think of him, their hearts opening, softening, and melting. They call out to him ceaselessly, yet he does not grant them grace. I rejoice endlessly in the illusory pleasures of the world, striving for them, bound to fall into the fierce mouth of hell. Yet he gave me the clarity to chant Sivayanama, granted me the boon of deathlessness, and made me his servant. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: The ultimate gifts of clarity and endless life come as a pure shock of grace. Vallalar says he was entirely distracted by worldly pleasures and headed for ruin. Yet God suddenly turned him into a servant and taught him the sacred mantra Sivayanama (salutation to Siva), bypassing the weeping devotees entirely.

translit: aṇṇa-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aṟaṅkarainta nāviṉarkaḷ akaṅkaraintu karaintu kaṇṇara nīrperukki varuntavumaṅ karuḷāṉ kaṭaināyiṟ kaṭaiyēṉmeyk katiyai-oru ciṟitum eṇṇāta koṭumpāvip pulaimaṉattuc ciṟiyēṉ eṉaikkaruti valiyavumnāṉ irukkumiṭat taṭaintu taṇṇārveṇ matiyamutam uṇavoṉṟu koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: O brother, this is a wonder, this is a wonder, what shall I say? Those whose tongues speak righteousness melt and melt in their hearts, shedding floods of tears from their eyes and suffering, yet he does not grant them grace. I am lower than the lowest dog. I am a cruel sinner with a base heart who does not think even a little about the true path. Yet, considering me, he came on his own accord to the place where I was and gave me the cooling, white lunar nectar as food. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: God does not wait to be found, choosing instead to seek out the lost. While righteous people weep for a glimpse of the divine, God arrives uninvited at the door of a self-confessed sinner. There, the divine provides the cooling lunar nectar, an inner spiritual nourishment that brings total peace.

translit: aiyā-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ arumai-aṟin taruḷvirumpi urimaipala iyaṟṟip poyyāta nilainiṉṟa puṇṇiyarkaḷ irukkap pulaimaṉattuc ciṟiyēṉōr pullunikar illēṉ ceyyāta ciṟutoḻilē ceytuḻaluṅ kaṭaiyēṉ cerukkuṭaiyēṉ eṉaittaṉatu tiruvuḷattil aṭaittē caiyāti antanaṭuk kāṭṭi-oṉṟu koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: O sir, this is a wonder, this is a wonder, what shall I say? The virtuous ones, who know his greatness, desire his grace, perform many rightful duties, and stand firmly in truth, remain waiting. I am a small one with a base heart, not even equal to a blade of grass. I am a lowly one, full of arrogance, who wanders about doing petty deeds that should never be done. Yet he kept me in his divine heart, revealed the beginning, the end, and the middle, and gave me the singular truth. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: True spiritual vision is a gift of grace rather than a reward for good behavior. The virtuous follow all the rules and still wait in the dark. Meanwhile, God takes a flawed, arrogant person into his heart and instantly reveals the entire truth of existence from beginning to end.

translit: aṉṉō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aruḷarumai aṟintavarkaḷ aruḷamutam virumpi eṉṉō-iṅ karuḷāmai eṉṟukavaṉ ṟiruppa yātumoru naṉṟiyilēṉ tītuneṟi naṭappēṉ muṉṉōpiṉ ṉumaṟiyā mūṭamaṉap pulaiyēṉ muḻukkoṭiyēṉ eṉaikkaruti muṉṉareḻun taruḷit taṉṉōṭum iṇaintavaṇṇam oṉṟeṉakkuk koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉintanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Ah, this is a wonder, this is a wonder, what shall I say? Those who know the greatness of grace desire the nectar of grace, worrying and waiting, asking why he does not grant grace here. I possess no goodness whatsoever. I walk the path of evil. I am a foolish-hearted base one who knows neither what is ahead nor what is behind. I am utterly cruel. Yet, considering me, he graciously appeared before me and gave me the state of oneness, united with him. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: The absolute union with the divine is given freely to those who have no goodness of their own. Spiritual experts spend their lives waiting for a drop of grace. In total contrast, God directly approaches someone walking the path of evil and instantly merges them into a state of perfect oneness.

translit: aiyō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ pukalvēṉ aruviṉaikaḷ aṇukāmal aṟaneṟiyē naṭantu meyyōtum aṟiñarelām virumpiyiruntiṭavum veyyaviṉaik kaṭalkuḷittu viḻaṟkiṟaittuk kaḷittup poyōtip pulaiperukki nilaicurukki uḻalum puraimaṉattēṉ eṉaikkarutip pukuntaruḷik karuṇaic caiyōka muṟa-eṉakkum valintoṉṟu koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Alas, this is a wonder, this is a wonder. What can I say? The wise ones who speak the truth walk the righteous path so that harsh karmas do not approach them, and they wait in longing. Yet I bathe in the ocean of cruel karma. I rejoice in watering weeds. I speak lies, multiply my baseness, diminish my standing, and wander with a flawed heart. He thought of me, entered me, and bestowed His grace. He forcefully gave me a thing so that I might attain the union of compassion. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Divine grace is completely unpredictable. While wise sages live perfectly and wait for God, the poet sees himself as a flawed person wasting his life on useless things, like watering weeds. Yet God bypassed those patient sages to step directly into his flawed heart and grant him the union of compassion. This grace comes from the cosmic dancer who performs for Sivakama Valli, the goddess representing the divine will and compassion.

translit: eṟṟē-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ icaippēṉ iccaiyelām viṭuttuvaṉat tiṭattummalai yiṭattum uṟṟēmeyt tavampurivār uṉṉiviḻit tiruppa ulakaviṭa yaṅkaḷaiyē vilakaviṭa māṭṭēṉ kaṟṟētum aṟiyakilēṉ kaṭaiyariṉuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ karuṇaiyilāk kalmaṉattuk kaḷvaṉeṉaik karutic caṟṟēyum aṉṟumikap periteṉakkiṅ kaḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: What is this? This is a wonder, this is a wonder. What can I say? Those who perform true penance abandon all desires, reach the forests and mountains, and stay awake meditating on Him. Yet I refuse to let go of worldly matters. I have learned nothing. I am the lowest of the low. I am a thief with a merciless, stony heart. He thought of me and gave me something here that is not small at all, but exceedingly great. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: Severe penance usually involves fleeing to the forests and mountains to meditate night and day. Here the confession is brutally honest: the poet claims he is trapped by worldly desires, completely unlearned, and hardened like a stone. Despite this absolute lack of spiritual effort, God hands him an immeasurably great gift. The divine reaches down to the lowest places, ignoring the conventional rules of ascetic achievement.

translit: eṉṉē-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ icaippēṉ iravupakal aṟiyāmal irunta-iṭat tiruntu muṉṉēmeyt tavampurintār iṉṉēyum iruppa mūṭarkaḷil talainiṉṟa vēṭamaṉak koṭiyēṉ poṉṉēyam mikappurinta pulaikkaṭaiyēṉ iḻinta puḻuviṉumiṅ kiḻintiḻintu pukunta-eṉaik karutit taṉṉēya muṟa-eṉakkum oṉṟaḷittuk kaḷittāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: What is this? This is a wonder, this is a wonder. What can I say? Those who performed true penance in the past sit in one place without knowing night or day, and they still wait here today. Yet I stand foremost among fools. I am a cruel person with a deceitful mind. I am a base one with a deep love for gold. I have sunk lower and lower here, worse than a lowly worm. He thought of me, gave me a thing so that I might attain love for Him, and He rejoiced. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: The contrast here is between the timeless focus of the true ascetic and the base greed of the ordinary mind. Sages sit motionless, forgetting day and night, while the poet calls himself a greedy fool who loves gold and sinks lower than a worm. God's response to this confessed unworthiness is not judgment. Instead, the divine grants him the gift of deep love and actually rejoices in doing so.

translit: ōkō-ī taticayamī taticayameṉ ṉuraippēṉ uḷḷapaṭi uḷḷa-oṉṟai uḷḷamuṟa virumpip pākōmup paḻaracamō eṉarucikkap pāṭip patticeyvār irukkavumōr pattiyumil lātē kōkō-eṉ ṟulakuraippat tirikiṉṟa koṭiyēṉ kuṟṟamaṉṟik kuṇamaṟiyāp pettaṉeṉaik karutit tākōta raṅkuḷirnta taṉmai-oṉṟu koṭuttāṉ taṉittaciva kāmavallik kiṉittanaṭat tavaṉē.
translation: Oho! This is a wonder, this is a wonder. What can I say? There are devoted people who long for the True One with their whole heart, singing and tasting Him like sweet syrup or the juice of the three fruits. Yet I wander without a single trace of devotion. I am a cruel person, wandering while the world cries out in distress at my actions. I am a bound soul who knows only faults and no virtues. He thought of me and gave me a state that completely cools my inner thirst. He dances sweetly for the peerless Sivakama Valli.
commentary: God's grace acts as a cooling relief for a desperate, bound soul. True devotees already taste the sweetness of the divine, singing of God as being as sweet as the traditional three Tamil fruits (mango, jackfruit, and banana). The poet feels completely empty of this devotion, seeing himself as a wandering burden to the world. Even so, God steps in to quench his deep inner thirst, offering profound peace where there were only faults.

sections.title: The Garland Seeking Pardon for Offenses

translit: ceyvakainaṉ kaṟiyātē tiruvaruḷō ṭūṭic cilapukaṉṟēṉ aṟivaṟiyāc ciṟiyariṉuñ ciṟiyēṉ poyvakaiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum puṇṇiyaṉē matiyaṇinta puricaṭaiyāy viṭaiyāy meyvakaiyōr viḻittiruppa virumpi-eṉai aṉṟē mikavalintāṭ koṇṭaruḷi viṉaitavirtta vimalā aivakaiya kaṭavuḷarum antaṉarum parava āṉantat tirunaṭañcey ampalattem aracē.
translation: Not knowing well how to act, I feigned anger with divine grace and spoke a few words. I am the smallest of the small, devoid of wisdom. I am of a false nature. You must forgive the faults I spoke. O meritorious One! O One with twisted matted hair adorned with the moon! O One with the bull! While true devotees stayed awake seeking You, You desired me even then and forcefully claimed me, destroying my karma, O pure One! As the five kinds of gods and the brahmins offer praise, You perform the joyous divine dance in the Hall, O our King!
commentary: The poet asks forgiveness for times he sulked or felt frustrated with divine grace. He marvels at how God's mercy ignores standard expectations of merit. While rigorous seekers stayed awake all night in intense meditation, God bypassed them to forcefully claim this humble, confused soul.

translit: nilaināṭi aṟiyātē niṉṉaruḷō ṭūṭi nīrmaiyala pukaṉṟēṉnaṉ ṉeṟi-oḻukāk kaṭaiyēṉ pulaināyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pūtakaṇañ cūḻanaṭam purikiṉṟa puṉitā kalaināṭu matiyaṇinta kaṉapavaḷac caṭaiyāy karuttaṟiyāk kālaiyilē karuṇai-aḷit tavaṉē talaiñāṉa muṉivarkaḷtan talaimītu viḷaṅkum tāḷuṭaiyāy āḷuṭaiya caṟkuru-eṉ aracē.
translation: Not seeking to know my state, I feigned anger with Your grace and spoke unseemly things. I am the lowest, not treading the good path. I am a lowly dog. You must forgive the faults I spoke. O holy One who dances surrounded by hosts of elements! O One with heavy coral matted hair adorned with the moon sought by the arts! O One who bestowed grace on me in those early days when my mind had no intent! Shining upon the heads of supreme sages of wisdom, You possess holy feet. O Satguru who claims me, my King!
commentary: True grace does not wait for a person to become perfect. God bestowed His compassion on the poet in his earliest days, long before his mind was mature enough to seek it intentionally. God acts here as the Satguru (the true spiritual teacher), claiming the soul purely out of divine love.

translit: kalaikkaṭainaṉ kaṟiyātē kaṉa-aruḷō ṭūṭik karikapukaṉ ṟēṉkavalaik kaṭaṟpuṇai-eṉ ṟuṇarēṉ pulaikkaṭaiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pōṟṟiciva pōṟṟiciva pōṟṟiciva pōṟṟi talaikkaṭaivāy aṉṟiravil tāḷmalaroṉ ṟamarttit taṉipporuḷeṉ kaiyilaḷitta tayavuṭaiya perumāṉ kolaikkaṭaiyārk keytariya kuṇamalaiyē potuvil kūttāṭik koṇṭulakaik kāttāḷuṅ kuruvē.
translation: Not knowing well the end of learning, I feigned anger with Your mighty grace and spoke harsh words. I did not realize You are the raft in the ocean of sorrow. I am a base person. You must forgive the faults I spoke. Praise Siva! Praise Siva! Praise Siva! Praise! At the front doorway on that night, You pressed down one lotus foot and placed the peerless truth in my hand, O compassionate Lord! O mountain of virtue unattainable by those who murder! Dancing in the Hall, You protect and rule the world, O Guru!
commentary: The poet recalls a deeply personal, mystical encounter where God came to his very door at night to hand him the ultimate truth. This supreme grace is described as a mountain of virtue. True to the principle of Jeevakarunyam (compassion for all living beings), this divine presence stays beyond the reach of those who murder any living being.

translit: niṉpukaḻnaṉ kaṟiyātē niṉṉaruḷō ṭūṭi neṟiyalavē pukaṉṟēṉnaṉ ṉilaivirumpi nillēṉ puṉpulaiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pūraṇaciṟ civaṉēmeyp poruḷaruḷum puṉitā eṉpuṭai-an nāḷiravil eḻuntaruḷi aḷitta eṉkuruvē eṉṉirukaṇ ilaṅkiyanaṉ maṇiyē aṉpuṭaiyār iṉpaṭaiyum aḻakiya-am palattē āttāḷum appaṉumāyk kūttāṭum patiyē.
translation: Not knowing Your fame well, I feigned anger with Your grace and spoke things contrary to the path. I do not stand desiring the good state. I am a petty, base person. You must forgive the faults I spoke. O perfect, conscious Siva! O holy One who grants the true reality! On that night at my side, You graced me with Your presence, O my Guru! O good gem shining in my two eyes! In the beautiful Hall where loving devotees attain bliss, You dance as mother and father, O Lord!
commentary: God is experienced not as a distant authority, but as a deeply intimate presence. Returning to the memory of that nighttime visitation, the poet describes the divine as his own eyes and his personal Guru. In the sacred Hall, the Lord dances with the perfectly balanced love of both a mother and a father.

translit: tulaikkoṭinaṉ kaṟiyōtē tuṇai-aruḷō ṭūṭit turicupukaṉ ṟēṉkaruṇaip paricupukaṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ pulaikkoṭiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum poṅkutiraik kaṅkaimati taṅkiyaceñ caṭaiyāy malaikkoṭi-eṉ ammai-aruḷ mātuciva kāma vallimaṟai vallituti colliniṉṟu kāṇak kalaikkoṭinaṉ kuṇarmuṉivar kaṇṭupukaḻn tēttak kaṉakacapai taṉilnaṭikkuṅ kāraṇacaṟ kuruvē.
translation: Not knowing well the scale of justice, I feigned anger with Your supportive grace and spoke flawed words. I do not know how to speak of the gift of grace. I am a base, cruel person. You must forgive the faults I spoke. O One with red matted hair where the surging waves of the Ganga and the moon rest! As the mountain creeper, my Mother, the Lady of grace, Sivakama Valli, the vine of the Vedas, sings Your praises and stands watching, and as sages who well understand the arts see and praise You, You dance in the Golden Hall, O causal Satguru!
commentary: The plea for pardon culminates in a grand vision of the Golden Hall, where the Lord dances as the ultimate cause of all things. He is witnessed by enlightened sages and his consort Sivakama Valli, the goddess who represents divine will and grace. The poet asks this supreme teacher to forgive his petty complaints and flawed words.

translit: paḻuttalainaṉ kuṇarātē patiyaruḷō ṭūṭip paḻutupukaṉ ṟēṉkaruṇaip pāṅkaṟiyāp paṭiṟēṉ puḻuttalaiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum puṇṇiyartam uḷḷakattē naṇṇiyameyp poruḷē kaḻuttalainañ caṇintaruḷuṅ karuṇaineṭuṅ kaṭalē kālmalareṉ talaimītu tāṉmalara aḷittāy viḻuttalaivar pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟilnaṭam puriyum meymmai-aṟi viṉpuruvāy viḷaṅkiyacaṟ kuruvē.
translation: Without proper understanding, I sulked with the Lord's grace. I spoke words of blame, a deceitful one ignorant of the ways of compassion. You must forgive the mistakes uttered by this lowly worm-headed one. O True Reality abiding in the hearts of the virtuous. O vast ocean of compassion wearing poison on your neck. You allowed your flower-like feet to blossom upon my head. O True Guru who shines as the embodiment of true knowledge and bliss, dancing in the ruby hall praised by supreme sages.
commentary: Doubting God's grace leads only to sorrow. Asking for forgiveness, Vallalar calls God an ocean of compassion who wears poison on his neck. This refers to the traditional story of Siva drinking deadly poison to save all living beings, a simple reminder that God's ultimate nature is always to protect.

translit: kaiyaṭainaṉ kaṟiyātē kaṉa-aruḷō ṭūṭik kācupukaṉ ṟēṉkaruṇait tēcaṟiyāk kaṭaiyēṉ poyyaṭiyēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum puttamutē cuttacuka pūraṇaciṟ civamē aiyaṭikaḷ kāṭavarkōṉ akamakiḻntu pōṟṟum ampalattē aruḷnaṭañcey cempavaḷa malaiyē meyyaṭiyar uḷḷakattil viḷaṅkukiṉṟa viḷakkē vētamuṭi mītirunta mētakucaṟ kuruvē.
translation: Without understanding your protection, I sulked with your abundant grace. I spoke words of blame, a lowly one ignorant of the light of compassion. You must forgive the mistakes uttered by this false devotee. O fresh ambrosia. O pure, blissful, and perfect supreme consciousness. O red coral mountain performing the dance of grace in the hall, praised with a joyful heart by the saintly king Aiyadigal Kadavarkon. O lamp shining in the hearts of true devotees. O excellent True Guru seated upon the crown of the Vedas.
commentary: The apology continues for failing to see the light of God's compassion. The divine is the ultimate teacher, seated high above the Vedas (the ancient sacred scriptures), who dances in the hearts of true devotees. Vallalar also remembers Aiyadigal Kadavarkon, a royal saint who gave up his throne to find joy in this same divine dance.

translit: tiṟappaṭanaṉ kuṇarātē tiruvaruḷō ṭūṭit tīmaipukaṉ ṟēṉkaruṇait tiṟañciṟitun teḷiyēṉ puṟappaṭiṟēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pūtamutal nātavaraip puṇaruvitta puṉitā uṟappaṭumey uṇarvuṭaiyār uḷḷakattē viḷaṅkum uṇmaiyaṟi vāṉanta uruvuṭaiya kuruvē ciṟappaṭaimā tavarpōṟṟac cempoṉmaṇip potuvil tiruttoḻilain tiyaṟṟuvikkun tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Without clear understanding, I sulked with the divine grace. I spoke evil words, having no clarity about the nature of your compassion. You must forgive the mistakes uttered by this deceitful outsider. O pure one who linked everything from the five elements to the primal sound. O Guru embodying truth, knowledge, and bliss, shining in the hearts of those with steadfast true awareness. O Lord of the divine dance who directs the five divine actions in the beautiful golden ruby hall, praised by great ascetics.
commentary: Frustration with divine grace comes from a simple lack of clarity. Vallalar addresses God as the master of the five divine actions: creation, protection, destruction, concealment, and the granting of grace. This pure force connects all existence, from the physical elements to the first vibrations of sound, guiding the universe with compassion.

translit: tērntuṇarntu teḷiyātē tiruvaruḷō ṭūṭic cilapukaṉṟēṉ tirukkaruṇait tiṟañciṟitun teriyēṉ pōntakaṉēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pōtānta micaiviḷaṅku nātānta viḷakkē ūrntapaṇak kaṅkaṇamē mutaṟpaṇikaḷ oḷira uyarpotuvil naṭikkiṉṟa ceyaluṭaiya perumāṉ cārntavarai evvakaiyun tāṅki-aḷik kiṉṟa tayavuṭaiya peruntalaimait taṉimutalen tāyē.
translation: Without investigating and realizing the truth, I sulked with your divine grace. I spoke careless words, completely ignorant of the nature of your divine compassion. You must forgive the mistakes uttered by this wanderer who went astray. O lamp of the supreme sound shining above the summit of knowledge. You are the great Lord dancing in the supreme hall, shining with ornaments like the creeping hooded serpent bracelet. You are the compassionate supreme head, the unique source and my parent, who supports and protects in every way those who take refuge in you.
commentary: Even when a person goes astray and speaks out of ignorance, God remains a perfectly compassionate parent. He is the supreme light shining above all human knowledge. Knowing this, Vallalar places his total trust in this unique source, certain that God will always support and protect anyone who seeks shelter.
