translit: ollumvakai aṟiyātē uṉṉaruḷō ṭūṭi ūṟupukaṉ ṟēṉtuyaram āṟumvakai uṇarēṉ pulliyaṉēṉ pukaṉṟapiḻai poṟuttaruḷal vēṇṭum pūtiyaṇin toḷirkiṉṟa poṉmēṉip perumāṉ colliyalum poruḷiyalum kaṭantapara nātat turiyaveḷip poruḷāṉa periyanilaip patiyē melliyalnaṟ civakāma vallikaṇṭu makiḻa viriyumaṟai ēttanaṭam puriyumaruḷ iṟaiyē.
translation: Without knowing the proper way, I sulked with your grace. I spoke harmful words and do not know how to soothe my sorrow. You must forgive the mistakes uttered by this base person. O great Lord whose golden body shines adorned with sacred ash. O Lord of the supreme state, the reality in the transcendent space of the supreme sound beyond words and meanings. O God of grace performing the dance praised by the expansive Vedas, so that the tender goddess Sivakami watches and rejoices.
commentary: Sorrow over his own foolish words leaves the poet looking for comfort. He pictures God as a reality entirely beyond human language and meaning, existing in a space of pure sound. Yet this ungraspable truth is also a personal God of grace who dances joyfully for the goddess Sivakami, bringing the infinite into a warm and intimate form.

sections.title: The Garland of Grace for Sambandar

note: Editor's note: verse 1 is printed with four lines, as in Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar's first edition and later editions. A. Balakrishna Pillai (Ā. Pā.) reports that the author's own manuscript has five lines, with a further line, alakilā uṇarcci aḷittaṉai uṉṟaṉ aruṭkaṭaṟ perumai-eṉ pukalvēṉ (அலகிலா உணர்ச்சி அளித்தனை உன்றன் அருட்கடற் பெருமைஎன் புகல்வேன்), before the last. Verse 11 is a separate song that Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar placed here.
tamil: உலகியல் உணர்வோர் அணுத்துணை மேலும் உற்றிலாச் சிறியஓர் பருவத்
திலகிய எனக்குள் இருந்தருள் நெறியில் ஏற்றவுந் தரமிலா மையினான்
விலகுறங் காலத் தடிக்கடி ஏற விடுத்துப்பின் விலகுறா தளித்தாய்
திலகநன் காழி ஞானசம் பந்தத் தெள்ளமு தாஞ்சிவ குருவே.
translit: ulakiyal uṇarvōr aṇuttuṇai mēlum uṟṟilāc ciṟiya-ōr paruvat tilakiya eṉakkuḷ iruntaruḷ neṟiyil ēṟṟavun taramilā maiyiṉāṉ vilakuṟaṅ kālat taṭikkaṭi ēṟa viṭuttuppiṉ vilakuṟā taḷittāy tilakanaṉ kāḻi ñāṉacam pantat teḷḷamu tāñciva kuruvē.
translation: O Siva Guru, the clear nectar of Gnanasambandar from the excellent and beautiful city of Kazhi! In my tender youth, when I did not possess even an atom of worldly awareness, you remained within me. Since I lacked the capacity to ascend the path of grace, whenever I slipped, you repeatedly helped me climb back. Later, you bestowed your grace so I would never slip away again.
commentary: Divine guidance begins long before a person is even aware of it. In his very early childhood, completely free of worldly concerns, the poet was already being held and guided by his master from within. Whenever his spiritual footing slipped, this inner teacher caught him and set him right, finally making his path secure.

tamil: உயிர்அனு பவம்உற்றிடில் அதவிடத்தே ஓங்கருள் அனுபவம் உறும்அச்
செயிரில்நல் அனுப வத்திலே சுத்த சிவஅனு பவம்உறும் என்றாய்
பயிலுமூ வாண்டில் சிவைதரு ஞானப் பால்மகிழ்ந் துண்டுமெய்ந் நெறியாம்
பயிர்தழைந் துறவைத் தருளிய ஞான பந்தன்என் றோங்குசற் குருவே.
translit: uyiraṉu pavamuṟṟiṭil ataviṭattē ōṅkaruḷ aṉupavam uṟumac ceyirilnal aṉupa vattilē cutta civa-aṉu pavamuṟum eṉṟāy payilumū vāṇṭil civaitaru ñāṉap pālmakiḻn tuṇṭumeyn neṟiyām payirtaḻain tuṟavait taruḷiya ñāṉa pantaṉeṉ ṟōṅkucaṟ kuruvē.
translation: O supreme true Guru known as Gnanasambandar! You joyfully drank the milk of wisdom offered by the Goddess in your third year and established the flourishing crop of the true path. You taught me: "If you attain the experience of the soul, from there the exalted experience of grace will manifest. Within that flawless experience of grace, the pure experience of Siva will manifest."
commentary: The spiritual journey unfolds in three distinct, sequential stages. First comes the direct realization of the soul itself, which naturally opens into the experience of divine grace. Only within that perfect, flawless state of grace can a person finally reach the pure experience of the divine reality.

tamil: தத்துவநிலைகள் தனித்தனி ஏறித் தனிப்பர நாதமாந் தலத்தே
ஒத்தான் மயமாம் நின்னைநீ இன்றி உற்றிடல் உயிரனு பவம்என்
றித்துணை வெளியின் என்னைஎன் னிடத்தே இருந்தவா றளித்தனை அன்றோ
சித்தநற் காழி ஞானசம் பந்தச் செல்வமே எனதுசற் குருவே.
translit: tattuvanilaikaḷ taṉittaṉi ēṟit taṉippara nātamān talattē ottāṉ mayamām niṉṉainī iṉṟi uṟṟiṭal uyiraṉu pavameṉ ṟittuṇai veḷiyiṉ eṉṉai-eṉ ṉiṭattē iruntavā ṟaḷittaṉai aṉṟō cittanaṟ kāḻi ñāṉacam pantac celvamē eṉatucaṟ kuruvē.
translation: O treasure of Gnanasambandar in the good city of Kazhi of the siddhas! O my true Guru! You taught me that climbing the levels of reality one by one to reach the space of the supreme primal sound, and experiencing yourself as of that very nature without the sense of 'you', is the experience of the soul. Dwelling within me in this vast space, you bestowed this upon me, did you not?
commentary: The first great milestone is the true experience of the soul. To reach this, a seeker must rise above all the physical and mental layers of existence to arrive at the subtle space of the primal cosmic sound. Here, the individual ego completely drops away, and the soul finally knows its own unclouded nature.

tamil: தனிப்பர நாத வெளியின்மேல் நினது தன்மயந் ஆக்கிப்
பனிப்பிலா தென்றும் உள்ளதாய் விளங்கிப் பரம்பரத் துட்புற மாகி
இனிப்புற ஒன்றும் இயம்புறா இயல்பாய் இருந்தே அருளனு பவம்என்
றெனக்கருள் புரிந்தாய் ஞானசம் பந்தன் என்னும்என் சற்குரு மணியே.
translit: taṉippara nāta veḷiyiṉmēl niṉatu taṉmayan ākkip paṉippilā teṉṟum uḷḷatāy viḷaṅkip paramparat tuṭpuṟa māki iṉippuṟa oṉṟum iyampuṟā iyalpāy iruntē aruḷaṉu pavameṉ ṟeṉakkaruḷ purintāy ñāṉacam pantaṉ eṉṉumeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O my jewel of a true Guru named Gnanasambandar! You transformed me into your own nature above the space of the supreme primal sound. You shone as the eternal and unwavering reality, becoming the inside and outside of the supreme beyond. Existing in a sweet state that cannot be described in words, you granted me this state and declared it the experience of grace.
commentary: The second milestone is the experience of grace, which takes place even higher than the space of primal sound. In this state, the soul is transformed into the very nature of the divine teacher. It is an eternal, deeply sweet reality that encompasses everything inside and outside the universe, completely beyond the reach of human language.

tamil: உள்ளதாய் விளங்கும் ஒருபெரு வெளிமேல் உள்ளதாய் முற்றும்உள் ளதுவாய்
நள்ளதாய் எனதாய் நானதாய்த் தளதாய் நவிற்றருந் தானதாய் இன்ன
விள்ளொணா அப்பால் அப்படிக் கப்பால் வெறுவெளி சிவஅனு பவம்என்
றுள்ளுற அளித்த ஞானசம் பந்த உத்தம சுத்தசற் குருவே.
translit: uḷḷatāy viḷaṅkum oruperu veḷimēl uḷḷatāy muṟṟumuḷ ḷatuvāy naḷḷatāy eṉatāy nāṉatāyt taḷatāy naviṟṟarun tāṉatāy iṉṉa viḷḷoṇā appāl appaṭik kappāl veṟuveḷi civa-aṉu pavameṉ ṟuḷḷuṟa aḷitta ñāṉacam panta uttama cuttacaṟ kuruvē.
translation: O supreme, pure, and true Guru Gnanasambandar! You inwardly bestowed upon me the pure experience of Siva. You revealed it as existing above the one great space of reality, becoming all that exists. It becomes the center, becomes mine, becomes 'I', becomes the foundation, and becomes 'That' which is hard to express. You declared that this indescribable beyond, and the absolute void beyond even that, is the experience of Siva.
commentary: The final culmination is the pure experience of the supreme divine, resting above all known dimensions of space and reality. Here, the divine becomes absolutely everything: the center, the self, the foundation, and the vast emptiness that exists beyond all concepts. It is the ultimate reality where all boundaries vanish entirely.

tamil: பொத்திய மூல மலப்பிணி தவிர்க்கும் பொருள்அரு ளனுபவம் அதற்குப்
பத்தியம் உயிரின் அனுபவம் இதனைப் பற்றறப் பற்றுதி இதுவே
சத்தியம் எனஎன் தனக்கருள் புரிந்த தனிப்பெருங் கருணைஎன் புகல்வேன்
முத்தியற் சிவிகை இவர்ந்தருள் நெறியின் முதலர சியற்றிய துரையே.
translit: pottiya mūla malappiṇi tavirkkum poruḷaru ḷaṉupavam ataṟkup pattiyam uyiriṉ aṉupavam itaṉaip paṟṟaṟap paṟṟuti ituvē cattiyam eṉa-eṉ taṉakkaruḷ purinta taṉipperuṅ karuṇai-eṉ pukalvēṉ muttiyaṟ civikai ivarntaruḷ neṟiyiṉ mutalara ciyaṟṟiya turaiyē.
translation: O Lord who rode the pearl palanquin of liberation and established the primal kingdom of the path of grace. How can I describe your supreme unique compassion that blessed me with these words: "The substance that cures the ingrained disease of primal impurity is the experience of grace. The regimen for this cure is the experience of the soul. Grasp this without any other attachment. This is the truth."
commentary: Grace is the only medicine capable of curing the deep-rooted impurities of the soul. For this medicine to work, the seeker must follow a strict healing regimen: living fully from the pure experience of the soul without any other attachments.

tamil: அடியெனல் எதுவோ முடியெனல் எதுவோ அருட்சிவ மதற்கெனப் பலகால்
படியுற வருந்தி இருந்தஎன் வருத்தம் பார்த்தரு ளால்எழுந் தருளி
மிடியற எனைத்தான் கடைக்கணித் துனக்குள் விளங்குவ அடிமுடி என்றாய்
வடிவிலாக் கருணை வாரியே மூன்று வயதினில் அருள்பெற்ற மணியே.
translit: aṭiyeṉal etuvō muṭiyeṉal etuvō aruṭciva mataṟkeṉap palakāl paṭiyuṟa varunti irunta-eṉ varuttam pārttaru ḷāleḻun taruḷi miṭiyaṟa eṉaittāṉ kaṭaikkaṇit tuṉakkuḷ viḷaṅkuva aṭimuṭi eṉṟāy vaṭivilāk karuṇai vāriyē mūṉṟu vayatiṉil aruḷpeṟṟa maṇiyē.
translation: O formless ocean of compassion, O gem who received grace at three years of age. I suffered deeply and repeatedly wondered what constitutes the foot and what constitutes the crown of the gracious Supreme. Seeing my sorrow, you arose out of grace and cast your compassionate glance upon me to remove my destitution. You told me, "The foot and the crown shine right within you."
commentary: Traditional stories describe the divine as so vast that the other gods could not find its head or its feet. The guru reveals a simpler and deeper truth: the infinite heights and depths of the divine are actually found shining right inside the seeker.

tamil: செவ்வகை ஒருகால் படுமதி அளவே செறிபொறி மனம்அதன் முடிவில்
எவ்வகை நிலையும் தோற்றும்நீ நினக்குள் எண்ணிய படிஎலாம் எய்தும்
இவ்வகை ஒன்றே வருத்தமில் வகைஎன் றெனக்கருள் புரிந்தசற் குருவே
தெவ்வகை அமண இருளற எழுந்த தீபமே சம்பந்தத் தேவே.
translit: cevvakai orukāl paṭumati aḷavē ceṟipoṟi maṉamataṉ muṭivil evvakai nilaiyum tōṟṟumnī niṉakkuḷ eṇṇiya paṭi-elām eytum ivvakai oṉṟē varuttamil vakai-eṉ ṟeṉakkaruḷ purintacaṟ kuruvē tevvakai amaṇa iruḷaṟa eḻunta tīpamē campantat tēvē.
translation: O Lord Sambandar, O lamp that arose to dispel the hostile darkness of Jainism. You are the true Guru who graced me with these words: "If you properly align your dense senses and mind even once, every state will be revealed at the end of that focus, and you will attain everything you envision within yourself. This alone is the painless way."
commentary: Mastering the mind and senses does not require endless struggle. Aligning and focusing them perfectly even once is a painless path that naturally unlocks all spiritual states from within.

tamil: முன்புறு நிலையும் பின்புறு நிலையும் முன்னிநின் றுளமயக் குறுங்கால்
அன்புறு நிலையால் திருநெறித் தமிழ்கொண் டையநீத் தருளிய அரசே
என்புபெண் ணுருவோ டின்னுயி ரதுகொண் டெழுந்திடப் புரிந்துல கெல்லாம்
இன்புறப் புரிந்த மறைத்தனிக் கொழுந்தே என்னுயிர்க் குயிர்எனுங் குருவே.
translit: muṉpuṟu nilaiyum piṉpuṟu nilaiyum muṉṉiniṉ ṟuḷamayak kuṟuṅkāl aṉpuṟu nilaiyāl tiruneṟit tamiḻkoṇ ṭaiyanīt taruḷiya aracē eṉpupeṇ ṇuruvō ṭiṉṉuyi ratukoṇ ṭeḻuntiṭap purintula kellām iṉpuṟap purinta maṟaittaṉik koḻuntē eṉṉuyirk kuyireṉuṅ kuruvē.
translation: O Guru who is the very life of my life, O unique tender shoot of the Vedas who brought joy to the whole world by resurrecting bones into a living female form. When I stood with a confused mind pondering my past and future states, you, O King, dispelled my doubts using the loving path of divine Tamil.
commentary: The guru dispels all human anxiety about the past and the future through the path of love and sacred Tamil poetry. This divine power of love is compared to the legendary miracle where dry bones were restored into a living person.

tamil: வருபகற் கற்பம் பலமுயன் றாலும் வரலருந் திறனெலாம் எனக்கே
ஒருபகற் பொழுதில் உறஅளித் தனைநின் உறுபெருங் கருணைஎன் உரைப்பேன்
பெருமண நல்லூர்த் திருமணங் காணப் பெற்றவர் தமையெலாம் ஞான
உருவடைந் தோங்கக் கருணைசெய் தளித்த உயர்தனிக் கவுணிய மணியே.
translit: varupakaṟ kaṟpam palamuyaṉ ṟālum varalarun tiṟaṉelām eṉakkē orupakaṟ poḻutil uṟa-aḷit taṉainiṉ uṟuperuṅ karuṇai-eṉ uraippēṉ perumaṇa nallūrt tirumaṇaṅ kāṇap peṟṟavar tamaiyelām ñāṉa uruvaṭain tōṅkak karuṇaicey taḷitta uyartaṉik kavuṇiya maṇiyē.
translation: O exalted and unique gem of the Kaundinya lineage, you compassionately transformed all those who gathered to witness your grand wedding at Perumananallur, allowing them to attain the form of wisdom and ascend. How can I describe your great compassion that granted me in a single day all those rare abilities that remain unattainable even after striving for many eons.
commentary: Attaining spiritual wisdom and divine abilities usually takes lifetimes of intense effort. The boundless compassion of the guru grants these ultimate gifts in a single day, just as a legendary saint once elevated everyone attending his wedding into pure divine light.

tamil: சீரார் சண்பைக் கவுணியர்தம் தெய்வ மரபில் திகழ்விளக்கே
தெவிட்டா துளத்தில் தித்திக்கும் தேனே அழியாச் செல்வமே
காரார் மிடற்றுப் பவளமலைக் கண்ணின் முளைத்த கற்பகமே
கரும்பே கனியே என்இரண்டு கண்ணே கண்ணிற் கருமணியே
ஏரார் பருவம் மூன்றில்உமை இனிய முலைப்பால் எடுத்தூட்டும்
பேரார் ஞான சம்பந்தப் பெருமா னேநின் திருப்புகழைப்
பேசு கின்றோர் மேன்மேலும் பெருஞ்செல் வத்தில் பிறங்குவரே.
translit: cīrār caṇpaik kavuṇiyartam teyva marapil tikaḻviḷakkē teviṭṭā tuḷattil tittikkum tēṉē aḻiyāc celvamē kārār miṭaṟṟup pavaḷamalaik kaṇṇiṉ muḷaitta kaṟpakamē karumpē kaṉiyē eṉiraṇṭu kaṇṇē kaṇṇiṟ karumaṇiyē ērār paruvam mūṉṟilumai iṉiya mulaippāl eṭuttūṭṭum iṉpak kutalaimoḻikkuruntē eṉā ruyiruk korutuṇaiyē pērār ñāṉa campantap perumā ṉēniṉ tiruppukaḻaip pēcu kiṉṟōr mēṉmēlum peruñcel vattil piṟaṅkuvarē.
translation: O radiant lamp shining in the divine lineage of the Kavuniyars of excellent Sanpai! O honey that sweetens the heart without ever cloying! O imperishable wealth! O wish-fulfilling tree sprouted from the eye of the dark-throated coral mountain! O sugarcane! O fruit! O my two eyes! O the dark pupil in my eyes! O tender sprout who spoke joyous babbling words when Mother Umai fed you sweet breast milk at the beautiful age of three! O singular companion to my precious life! O greatly renowned Lord Gnanasambandar! Those who speak your divine praise will shine in immense wealth, prospering more and more.
commentary: The young saint Gnanasambandar is addressed here as a supreme guide and the most intimate companion to the soul. The verse uses terms of intense affection, calling the child saint sweet honey, sugarcane, and the very pupils of the poet's eyes. It recalls the famous story of Sambandar as a three-year-old receiving divine milk from the Goddess Uma, a gift that awakened his ability to sing sacred poetry. The "dark-throated coral mountain" refers to Lord Siva, who drank poison to save the universe, and the saint is described as a wish-fulfilling tree born directly from his grace. Reciting the praises of this great saint brings the blessing of lasting prosperity.

sections.title: The Garland of Grace for Appar

note: Editor's note: verse 5, “you who said: you placed nine gates within” recalls Thirunavukkarasar's Thiruppugalur Thiruthandagam (Thevaram 6.99.1).
translit: tiruttakucīr atikai-aruḷ talattiṉ ōṅkum civakkoḻuntiṉ aruṭperumait tiṟattāl vāymai uruttakumey uṇarccivaṭi vākic caiva oḷiviḷaṅka nāvaraceṉ ṟorupēr peṟṟup poruttamuṟa uḻavārap paṭaikaik koṇṭa puṇṇiyaṉē naṇṇiyacīrp puṉita ṉē-eṉ karuttamarnta kalaimatiyē karuṇai ñāṉak kaṭalēniṉ kaḻalkarutak karutu vāyē.
translation: By the great grace of the tender sprout of Siva rising in the glorious, grace-filled shrine of Thiruvathigai, you became the very embodiment of true awareness. You received the supreme name Sovereign of Speech so the light of the Saiva path would shine. O virtuous one who fittingly held the weeding implement in your hand. O pure one of vast glory. O brilliant moon of arts seated in my mind. O ocean of compassion and wisdom. Please grant that I may meditate upon your holy feet.
commentary: Vallalar celebrates the transformation of the saint Appar by the grace of Lord Siva at the shrine of Thiruvathigai. He was given the title 'Sovereign of Speech' and took up a simple hoe to physically clear weeds from temple grounds. This humble work showed that true spiritual awareness always expresses itself in practical service.

translit: vāymaiyilāc camaṇātar palakāṟ ceyta vañcamelām tiruvaruṭpēr valattāl nīntit tūymaipeṟum civaneṟiyē viḷaṅka ōṅkum cōtimaṇi viḷakkē-eṉ tuṇaiyē emmaic cēmmaiviṭā taṇimaiviṭat tāḷa vanta celvamē ellaiyilāc ciṟappu vāyntuḷ āymaiyuṟu peruntakaiyē amutē caiva aṇiyēcol laraceṉumpēr amainta tēvē.
translation: You swam across all the treacheries repeatedly committed by the truthless Jains using the great power of divine grace. O radiant, jewelled lamp who rises to make the pure Saiva path shine. O my companion. O wealth who came to rule us, keeping us close and bringing us near. O great and noble one endowed with boundless eminence and deep inner inquiry. O nectar. O ornament of the Saiva path. O divine one bearing the name Sovereign of Words.
commentary: Traditional accounts say the saint faced severe persecution and attempts on his life by the Jain rulers of his time. He survived these physical trials solely through the power of divine grace, standing as a guiding light for the Saiva path (the tradition of devotion to Lord Siva).

translit: tēvarelām toḻuntalaimait tēvar pātat tirumalarai muṭikkaṇintu tikaḻntu niṉṟa nāvaracē nāṉmukaṉum virumpum ñāṉa nāyakaṉē nallavarkku naṇpa ṉē-em pāvamelām akaṟṟi-aruṭ pāṉmai nalkum paṇpuṭaiya perumāṉē paṇintu niṉpāl mēvavirup puṟumaṭiyark kaṉpu ceyya vēṇṭiṉēṉ avvakainī vititti ṭāyē.
translation: O Sovereign of Speech, you stand radiant, wearing on your head the holy lotus feet of the Supreme Lord worshipped by all the gods. O Lord of wisdom desired even by the four-faced Brahma. O friend to the good. O Lord whose very nature is to remove all our sins and grant the quality of grace. I long to serve and love the devotees who bow and desire to reach you. Please ordain that I may do so.
commentary: To keep the divine feet resting upon one's own head is a symbol of total surrender. Because the saint achieved this, even a creator god like Brahma (the four-faced deity of Hindu tradition) looks up to him. The only blessing asked of the saint here is the chance to lovingly serve others who walk this same spiritual path.

translit: vitivilakkī teṉṟaṟiyum viḷaivoṉ ṟillā viṉaiyiṉēṉ eṉiṉumeṉṉai virumpi eṉṉuḷ mativiḷakkai ēṟṟi-aruḷ maṉaiyiṉ ñāṉa vāḻvaṭaiyac ceyalvēṇṭum vaḷḷa lēnaṟ patimalarttāḷ niḻalaṭainta tavattōrk kellām patiyēcol laraceṉumpēr paṭaitta tēvē katitarukaṟ pakamēmuk kaṉiyē ñāṉak kaṭalē-eṉ karuttē-eṉ kaṇṇu ḷāṉē.
translation: I am bound by karma, lacking the maturity to discern rules from prohibitions. Yet, O benevolent one, you must love me, light the lamp of understanding within me, and make me attain the life of wisdom in the house of grace. O master of all the ascetics who have reached the shade of the good Lord's lotus feet. O divine one bearing the name Sovereign of Words. O wish-fulfilling tree granting liberation. O essence of the three sweet fruits. O ocean of wisdom. O my very thought. O resident within my eyes.
commentary: A sincere seeker often feels burdened by the consequences of past actions (karma) and confused by complex religious rules. Here, the plea is for the saint to ignore these human flaws, light the lamp of understanding within, and guide the soul to a life of wisdom where divine grace is the only home.

translit: kaṇṇuḷē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa maṇiyē caivak kaṉiyēnā varacēceṅ karumpē vētap paṇṇuḷē viḷainta-aruṭ payaṉē uṇmaip patiyōṅku nitiyēniṉ pātam aṉṟi viṇṇuḷē aṭaikiṉṟa pōkam oṉṟum virumpēṉeṉ ṟaṉaiyāḷa vēṇṭuṅ kaṇṭāy oṇṇuḷē oṉpatuvāy vaittāy eṉṟa uttamaṉēcittamakiḻn tutavu vōṉē.
translation: O jewel shining within my eye. O fruit of the Saiva path. O Sovereign of Speech. O sweet red sugarcane. O fruit of grace grown within the melodies of the Vedas. O exalted treasure of the true Lord. I do not desire any pleasure found in heaven, only your holy feet. You must rule over me. O pure one who sang that the Lord placed nine gates within this single body. O you who help with a joyful heart.
commentary: Heavenly pleasures mean nothing compared to the joy of pure devotion. The verse references one of the saint's own famous songs, which describes the human body as a fragile house with nine physical openings, reminding us that lasting joy is found only in the divine, not in the perishable body.

translit: ōṅkārat taṉimoḻiyiṉ payaṉaic caṟṟum ōrkilēṉ ciṟiyēṉiv vulaka vāḻvil āṅkārap perumatamāl yāṉai pōla akampāva mayaṉāki alaikiṉ ṟēṉuṉ pāṅkāya meyyaṭiyar tammaic caṟṟum parintilēṉ aruḷaṭaiyum paricoṉ ṟuṇṭō tīṅkāya ceyalaṉaittum uṭaiyēṉ eṉṉa ceyvēṉcol laracē-eṉ ceyku vēṉē.
translation: I am a lowly one who does not realize the benefit of the unique mantra Omkara. In this worldly life, I wander full of arrogance, like a large elephant intoxicated by ego. I have shown no love at all for your true devotees. Is there any way for me to attain grace? I possess every kind of evil deed. What will I do, O King of Words? What will I do?
commentary: The speaker admits he is lost in ego, wandering like a wild elephant blind to the meaning of Omkara (the sacred syllable Om). He asks the King of Words (the revered 7th-century saint Appar) if a person who has done nothing but wrong and ignored true devotees can still hope to receive grace.

translit: ceyvakai-oṉ ṟaṟiyāta ciṟiyēṉ intac ciṟṟulaka vāḻkkaiyiṭaic cikki antō poyvakaiyē purikiṉṟēṉ puṇṇi yāniṉ poṉṉaṭiyaip pōṟṟilēṉ puṉita ṉēnāṉ uyvakai-ev vakaiyātu ceyvēṉ nīyē uṟutuṇai-eṉ ṟirukkiṉṟēṉ uṇarvi lēṉai meyvakaiyiṟ celuttaniṉait tiṭuti yōcol vēntē-eṉ uyirttuṇaiyāy viḷaṅkuṅ kōvē.
translation: I am a lowly one who knows no course of action. Caught in this petty worldly life, alas, I commit only falsehood. O virtuous one, I do not praise your golden feet. O holy one, how will I be saved? What will I do? I believe you alone are my firm support. Will you consider guiding me, who lacks understanding, on the true path? O King of Words, O King who shines as my life's companion.
commentary: Caught in a web of worldly lies, the speaker confesses his total inability to save himself. He throws himself entirely on the mercy of the saint, asking to be led out of ignorance and onto the path of truth.

translit: viḷaṅkumaṇi viḷakkeṉanāl vētat tucci mēviyameyp poruḷai uḷḷē virumpi vaittuk kaḷaṅkaṟumey yaṉparellāṅ kaḷippa aṉṟōr kaṟṟuṇaiyāṟ kaṭalkaṭantu karaiyiṟ pōntu tuḷaṅkuperuñ civaneṟiyaic cārnta ñāṉat tuṇaiyēnan turaiyēnaṟ cukamē eṉṟum vaḷaṅkeḻumā kananeṟiyai vaḷarkka vanta vaḷḷalē niṉṉaruḷai vaḻaṅku vāyē.
translation: You lovingly placed within your heart the true reality that rests at the peak of the four Vedas like a shining jeweled lamp, making all flawless true devotees rejoice. On that day, you crossed the ocean using a stone pillar as a float and reached the shore. You embraced the great and radiant path of Siva. O companion of wisdom, our Lord, our pure bliss, O benevolent one who came to foster the ever-prosperous Agamic path, please grant your grace.
commentary: The verse recalls a famous miracle from the life of Appar, who was tied to a heavy stone pillar and thrown into the sea by a hostile king. Because the saint held the supreme truth of the scriptures in his heart, the stone floated like a raft and carried him to safety. The speaker prays to this same saint for the grace to cross the dangerous waters of worldly life.

translit: aruḷvaḻaṅkun tilakavati ammai yārpiṉ avataritta maṇiyecol laracē ñāṉat teruḷvaḻaṅkum civaneṟiyai viḷakka vanta ceḻuñcuṭarmā maṇiviḷakkē ciṟiya ṉēṉai iruḷvaḻaṅkum ulakiyalniṉ ṟeṭuttu ñāṉa iṉṉaruḷtan tāṇṭaruḷvāy iṉṟēl antō maruḷvaḻaṅkum pavaneṟiyiṟ cuḻalvēṉ uyyum vakai-aṟiyēṉ niṉṉaruṭku marapaṉ ṟītē.
translation: O gem born after the grace-bestowing mother Tilakavati, O King of Words, O great jeweled lamp of rich flame who came to illuminate the path of Siva that grants the clarity of wisdom. Lift me, a lowly one, out of this dark worldly existence and rule me by granting your sweet grace of wisdom. If you do not, alas, I will spin in the deluding path of endless births. I know no way to be saved. This does not befit your grace.
commentary: Tilakavati was the devoted older sister whose prayers guided Appar to the path of divine wisdom. The speaker praises the saint as a brilliant lamp and begs to be rescued from the endless cycle of birth and death, reminding the saint that leaving a soul in darkness would contradict his great compassion.

translit: tērnta-uḷat tiṭaimikavum tittit tūṟum ceḻuntēṉē collaracām tēvē meymmai cārntutikaḻ appūti aṭikaṭ kiṉpam tantaperun takaiyē-em tantai yē-uḷ kūrntamati niṟaivē-eṉ kuruvē eṅkaḷ kulateyva mēcaivak koḻuntē tuṉpam tīrntaperu neṟittuṇaiyē oppi lāta celvamē appaṉeṉat tikaḻkiṉ ṟōṉē.
translation: O rich honey that wells up with immense sweetness in a clear heart. O King of Words, O divine one, O great and noble one who gave joy to Appudi Adigal who shone in truth. O our father, O fullness of sharp inner intellect, O my Guru. O our family deity, O tender shoot of the Saiva path. O companion on the great path free from sorrow. O peerless wealth, you shine as a father.
commentary: Appudi Adigal was a deeply devoted follower who named everything he owned, including his children, after Appar. By recalling how the saint brought joy to this devotee, the speaker addresses him as a father, a teacher, and a peerless guide who frees the heart from sorrow.

sections.title: The Garland of Grace for Sundarar

note: Editor's note: verse 5 opens with the words of Sundarar's hymn on Thiruvarur (Thevaram 7.51.10). Verse 7: by old custom Sambandar's hymns are called Thirukkadaikkappu, Thirunavukkarasar's Thevaram, and Sundarar's Thiruppattu.
translit: matiyaṇiceñ caṭaikkaṉiyai maṉṟuḷnaṭam purimaruntait tutiyaṇiceñ cuvaipporuḷil coṉmālai toṭuttaruḷi vitiyaṇimā maṟaineṟiyum meynnilai-ā kamaneṟiyum vatiyaṇintu viḷaṅkavaitta vaṉtoṇṭap peruntakaiyē.
translation: O great Vantondar, you graciously wove a garland of words filled with profound and sweet meaning to praise the divine fruit who wears the moon on His red matted hair, the healing medicine dancing in the hall. You made the great Vedic path of sacred rules and the true Agamic path shine brightly in the world.
commentary: Sundarar composed sweet poetry that brought the divine beautifully to life for ordinary people. Vallalar credits the ancient saint with making both the Vedic path of traditional scriptures and the Agamic path of temple worship shine brightly in the world.

translit: nīṟṟiliṭṭa nilaiyāppuṉ ṉeṟiyuṭaiyār tamaikkūṭic cēṟṟiliṭṭa kampameṉat tiyaṅkuṟṟēṉ taṉai-āḷāy ēṟṟaliṭṭa tiruvaṭiyai eṇṇi-arum poṉṉaiyelām āṟṟiliṭṭuk kuḷatteṭutta aruṭṭalaimaip peruntakaiyē.
translation: I joined people of unsteady and base paths and swayed helplessly like a pole planted in mud. Please rule over me and save me. O great one of supreme grace, you meditated on the exalted holy feet of the Lord, dropped all your rare gold into the river, and retrieved it safely from the temple tank.
commentary: Comparing his own mind to a helpless pole wobbling in wet mud, Vallalar asks the saint for firm guidance. He recalls a famous miracle where Sundarar threw gold into a river and safely retrieved it miles away from a temple tank through his absolute faith.

translit: ilaikkuḷanī raḻaittaṉil iṭaṅkaruṟa aḻaittataṉvāyt talaikkutalai matalai-uyir taḻaippa-aḻait taruḷiyaniṉ kalaikkumvaṭa kalaiyiṉmutaṟ kalaikkumuṟu kaṇakkuyarpoṉ malaikkumaṇu nilaikkumuṟā vaṉtoṇṭap peruntakaiyē.
translation: O great Vantondar, you summoned the crocodile in the pond to release the babbling child from its mouth and graciously brought the boy back to flourishing life. Comparing the primary scriptures of the northern language to your divine Tamil hymns falls utterly short of comparing a tiny atom to the towering golden mountain.
commentary: Vallalar recalls another beloved miracle, when Sundarar commanded a crocodile to release a child it had swallowed alive. Vallalar then says the traditional northern scriptures in Sanskrit cannot begin to compare to the spiritual power of Sundarar's Tamil hymns, calling the difference as stark as a tiny atom beside a towering golden mountain.

translit: vētamutaṟ kalaikaḷelām viraintuvirain taṉantamuṟai ōta-avaik kaṇuttuṇaiyum uṇarvaritām emperumāṉ pātamalar niṉatutirup paṇimuṭimēṟ paṭappurinta mātavamyā turaittaruḷāy vaṉtoṇṭap peruntakaiyē.
translation: All the Vedas and primary scriptures swiftly recite His praise countless times, yet even an atomic fraction of our Lord remains entirely beyond their comprehension. O great Vantondar, please tell me what immense penance you performed to have His sacred lotus feet rest directly upon your devoted head.
commentary: The traditional scriptures cannot grasp even a fraction of the divine truth. God's grace descended so directly upon Sundarar, however, that the divine feet rested right upon his head. Vallalar asks the saint what immense spiritual discipline made such profound intimacy possible.

translit: ēḻicaiyāy icaippayaṉāy iṉṉamutāy eṉṉuṭaiya tōḻaṉumāy eṉṟumuṉnī coṉṉaperuñ coṟporuḷai āḻniṉait tiṭilaṭiyēṉ aruṅkaraṇam karaintukarain tūḻiyaliṉ puṟuvatukāṇ uyarkaruṇaip peruntaṉaiyē.
translation: You once sang of the Lord as the seven musical notes, the fruit of music, sweet nectar, and your very own companion. O great one of supreme compassion, when I deeply contemplate the meaning of your magnificent words, my inner faculties melt completely and I experience eternal bliss.
commentary: Sundarar famously spoke to God not as a distant ruler but as a close personal friend. Just meditating on the profound sweetness of this friendship, Vallalar says, melts his own inner faculties and fills him with endless joy.

translit: vāṉkāṇa intiraṉum mālaiyaṉum mātavarum tāṉkāṇa iṟai-aruḷāl taṉittavaḷa yāṉaiyiṉmēl kōṉkāṇa eḻuntaruḷik kulaviyaniṉ kōlamatai nāṉkāṇap peṟṟilaṉē nāvalūrp peruntakaiyē.
translation: O great lord of Navalur. By the grace of the Lord, you mounted the peerless white elephant. The heavens, Indra, Vishnu, Brahma, and the great ascetics watched you. The king watched you rise in glorious majesty. Yet I was not blessed to witness that celebrated form of yours.
commentary: Vallalar recalls a famous story of the saint Sundarar, who ascended to the divine realm on a white elephant sent by God. Vallalar expresses a deep, personal longing, wishing he could have been there to witness that glorious moment alongside the watching gods and kings.

translit: tēṉpaṭikkum amutāmuṉ tiruppāṭṭaittiṉantōṟum nāṉpaṭikkum pōteṉṉai nāṉaṟiyēṉ nā-oṉṟō ūṉpaṭikkum uḷampaṭikkum uyirpaṭikkum uyirkkuyirum tāṉpaṭikkum aṉupavaṅkāṇ taṉikkaruṇaip peruntaṉaiyē.
translation: O great one of supreme compassion. Every day when I read your sacred songs, which are a nectar sweeter than honey, I lose all awareness of myself. Is it only my tongue that reads? My flesh reads, my heart reads, my life reads, and the very life of my life experiences reading it too.
commentary: Vallalar describes the overwhelming power of the saint's devotional songs. He explains that reading them goes far beyond the physical tongue or the intellect. The poetry completely absorbs his entire being, resonating through his flesh, his life force, and the deepest core of his soul.

translit: iṉpāṭṭut toḻiṟpotuvil iyaṟṟukiṉṟa emperumāṉ uṉpāṭṭuk kuvappuṟalpōl ūrpāṭṭuk kuvantilareṉ ṟeṉpāṭṭuk kicaippiṉumeṉ iṭumpāṭṭuk karaṇamelām aṉpāṭṭuk kicaivatukāṇ aruṭpāṭṭup peruntakaiyē.
translation: O great one of grace-filled songs. Our Lord, who performs the blissful dance in the universal hall, delights in your songs in a way He does not delight in the songs of anyone else. Even as I declare this in my own song, see how all my troublesome inner faculties harmonize in love for your songs.
commentary: Vallalar says that God Himself delights in this saint's songs more than anyone else's. Even as Vallalar writes his own poetry to declare this, he finds that his restless and difficult mind is completely calmed and brought into harmony by the saint's words.

translit: paramparamām turiyameṉum patattirunta paramporuḷai urampeṟattō ḻamaikoṇṭa uṉperumai taṉaimatittu varampeṟanaṟ ṟeyvamelām vantikkum eṉṟāleṉ tarampeṟa-eṉ pukalvēṉnāṉ taṉittalaimaip peruntakaiyē.
translation: O great one of absolute primacy. You firmly established a friendship with the Supreme Reality who abides in the transcendent state of Turiya. Seeing your greatness, all the good gods worship you to receive boons. If this is so, what can I, with my limited capacity, possibly say to praise you?
commentary: The saint Sundarar is celebrated for approaching God directly as a close friend. Vallalar points out that because the saint attained this profound intimacy with the Supreme Reality in the highest state of consciousness (Turiya), even the lesser gods revere him. Seeing this, Vallalar feels he lacks the words to praise the saint enough.

translit: pērūrum paravaimaṉap piṇakkaṟa-em perumāṉai ūrūrum palapukala ōriravil tūtaṉeṉta tērūrum tiruvārūrt teruvutoṟum naṭappittāy ārūra niṉperumai ayaṉmālum aḷapparitē.
translation: O lord of Aroor. To resolve the lover's quarrel in the heart of Paravai in the great town, you made our Lord walk as a messenger through every chariot-running street of Thiruvarur in a single night, while the townsfolk whispered many things. Your greatness is impossible for even Brahma and Vishnu to measure.
commentary: Vallalar recalls a beloved story where God loved this saint so much that He agreed to act as a midnight messenger to resolve a domestic quarrel between the saint and his wife. Vallalar concludes that if the Lord of the universe was willing to walk the village streets on his behalf, the saint's greatness is truly beyond measure.

sections.title: The Garland of Grace for Manikkavasagar

note: Editor's note: verse 4, “the unique Agaval that said: be” is the Thiruvasagam's Thiruvandappaguthi (lines 170–182), where Manikkavasagar sings that the Lord “made even me to be”.
translit: tēcakattil iṉikkiṉṟa teḷḷamutē māṇikka vācakaṉē āṉanta vaṭivāṉa mātavaṉē mācakaṉṟa nītiruvāy malarntatamiḻ māmaṟaiyiṉ ācakaṉṟa aṉupavamnāṉ aṉupavikka aruḷutiyē.
translation: O clear nectar that tastes sweet in this world. O Manikkavasagar. O great ascetic whose very form is bliss. You are completely free of flaws. Please grant me the grace to experience the transcendent state of the great Tamil Veda that blossomed from your divine mouth.
commentary: The poetry of Manikkavasagar is revered here as the Tamil Veda, a sacred scripture of supreme authority. Vallalar asks the saint directly for the grace to experience the transcendent spiritual state these words describe, rather than merely reading them.

translit: karuveḷikkuṭ puṟaṉākik karaṇamelāṅ kaṭantuniṉṟa peruveḷikku neṭuṅkālam pittākit tirikiṉṟōr kuruveḷikkē niṉṟuḻalak kōtaṟanī kalantaṉi uruveḷikkē maṟaipukaḻum uyarvāta vūrmaṇiyē.
translation: Seekers wander madly for a long time after the vast space that transcends all faculties and exists both inside and outside the primal void. While they merely spin around in the space of their own minds, you merged flawlessly into the space of divine form. O exalted gem of Vadavur, you are praised by the Vedas.
commentary: Many spiritual seekers spend their lives chasing abstract concepts of a vast, empty void beyond the mind. Vallalar points out that while these seekers end up spinning in their own mental illusions, Manikkavasagar achieved something real and tangible by merging completely into the divine form.

translit: maṉpuruva naṭumutalā maṉamputaittu neṭuṅkālam eṉpuruvāyt tavañceyvār ellārum ēmākka aṉpuruvam peṟṟataṉpiṉ aruḷuruvam aṭaintupiṉṉar iṉpuruvam āyiṉainī eḻilvāta vūriṟaiyē.
translation: Ascetics perform penance for a long time. They fix their minds intensely on the center of their eyebrows and become mere skeletons. While all of them are left utterly disappointed, you first attained a form of love, then achieved a form of grace, and finally became the very form of bliss. O beautiful Lord of Vadavur.
commentary: Extreme physical austerities, where ascetics focus their minds endlessly and starve themselves to the bone, ultimately end in disappointment. True spiritual transformation follows a completely different path. Vallalar traces Manikkavasagar's success through a clear progression: he first became a body of love, which transformed into a body of grace, and finally became pure bliss.

translit: uru-aṇṭap perumaṟai-eṉ ṟulakamelām pukaḻkiṉṟa tiru-aṇṭap pakuti-eṉum tiru-akaval vāymalarnta kuru-eṉṟep peruntavarum kūṟukiṉṟa kōvēnī iru-eṉṟa taṉi-akavaleṇṇameṉak kiyamputiyē.
translation: The entire world praises the sacred verses of Thiruvandappaguthi, which blossomed from your divine mouth, as the great Veda of the manifest universe. O King, all great ascetics proclaim you as the supreme Guru. Please reveal to me the deep meaning of that unparalleled sacred verse.
commentary: Thiruvandappaguthi is a famous section of Manikkavasagar's poetry that describes the creation and vastness of the universe. Recognizing the saint as the ultimate teacher, Vallalar asks him to reveal the hidden, inner meaning behind these deeply revered verses.

translit: tēṭukiṉṟa āṉantac ciṟcapaiyil ciṉmayamāy āṭukiṉṟa cēvaṭikakkīḻ āṭukiṉṟa āramutē nāṭukiṉṟa vātavūr nāyakaṉē nāyaṭiyēṉ vāṭukiṉṟa vāṭṭamelām vantorukkāl māṟṟutiyē.
translation: You are the rare nectar dancing beneath the red feet of the Lord, who dances as pure consciousness in the highly sought hall of blissful wisdom. O Lord of Vadavur, sought by everyone. I am a lowly devotee. Please come to me just once and banish all my withering sorrow.
commentary: The hall of blissful wisdom is the space of pure consciousness where the divine dance of God takes place. Vallalar visualizes the saint participating in this divine joy right at the feet of God. He begs the saint to visit him just once to wipe away his worldly suffering and sorrow.

translit: cēmamikum tiruvāta vūrttēveṉ ṟulakupukaḻ māmaṇiyē nī-uraitta vācakattai eṇṇutoṟum kāmamiku kātalaṉṟaṉ kalavitaṉaik karutukiṉṟa ēmamuṟu kaṟpuṭaiyāḷ iṉpiṉumiṉ peytuvatē.
translation: O great gem praised by the world as the god of prosperous Thiruvadavur! Whenever I think of the words you spoke, it brings a joy sweeter than the joy of a secure, chaste wife contemplating union with her deeply desiring lover.
commentary: Reading the words of the ancient saint Manikkavasagar brings an intensely intimate and overpowering joy. This spiritual delight surpasses even the deep physical and emotional happiness of a loving wife anticipating union with her husband. Thiruvadavur is the saint's birthplace, where he is revered as a divine figure.

translit: vāṉkalanta māṇikka vācakaniṉ vācakattai nāṉkalantu pāṭuṅkāl naṟkaruppañ cāṟṟiṉilē tēṉkalantu pālkalantu ceḻuṅkaṉittīñ cuvaikalanteṉ ūṉkalantu uyirkalantu uvaṭṭāmal iṉippatuvē.
translation: O Manikkavasagar who merged with the heavens! When I become one with your words and sing them, they mix into my flesh and my life breath like good sugarcane juice mixed with honey, milk, and the sweet taste of rich fruits, sweetening me without ever cloying.
commentary: Singing these holy verses is a complete experience that permeates both the physical body and the soul. The poetry mixes into the flesh and breath like a rich blend of sugarcane juice, honey, milk, and fruit. It is infinitely sweet, yet it never cloys or becomes overwhelming to the senses.

translit: varumoḻicey māṇikka vācakaniṉ vācakattil orumoḻiyē eṉṉaiyumeṉ uṭaiyaṉaiyum oṉṟuvittut tarumoḻiyām eṉṉiliṉic cātakamēṉ cañcalamēṉ kurumoḻiyai virumpi-ayal kūṭuvatēṉ kūṟutiyē.
translation: O Manikkavasagar who utters enduring words! If just a single word among your words unites me with my Master and grants everything, why engage in further practice? Why this agitation? Tell me why one would desire another guru's words and gather elsewhere.
commentary: A single word from this saint is enough to bring about complete union with God. Since just one word grants everything, there is no need to seek out other teachers, struggle with complex spiritual practices, or feel anxious about the path. The poetry itself provides the ultimate guidance.

translit: peṇcumanta pākap perumāṉ orumāmēl eṇcumanta cēvakaṉpōl eytiyatum vaikainati maṇcumantu niṉṟatumōr māṟaṉ pirampaṭiyāl puṇcumantu koṇṭatumniṉ poruṭṭaṉṟō puṇṇiyaṉē .
translation: O virtuous one! Was it not for your sake that the great Lord who bears the Goddess on his side arrived like an esteemed warrior on a horse, stood carrying earth at the Vaigai river, and bore the wound from the Pandyan king's cane?
commentary: God's love for Manikkavasagar was so absolute that the divine directly stepped into the physical world to suffer for him. Traditional stories tell how the Lord took the form of a warrior on horseback, worked as a common laborer carrying earth at the Vaigai river, and even endured being beaten with a cane to protect the saint. The verse celebrates how intimately God responds to true devotion.

translit: vāṭṭamilā māṇikka vācakaniṉ vācattaik kēṭṭapoḻu taṅkirunta kīḻppaṟavaic cātikaḷum vēṭṭamuṟum pollā vilaṅkukaḷum meyññāṉa nāṭṭamuṟum eṉṉiliṅku nāṉaṭaital viyappaṉṟē.
translation: O unfading Manikkavasagar! When they heard your words, even the lowly bird species and fierce hunting animals there fixed their sights on true wisdom. This being so, it is no surprise that I attain it here.
commentary: The spiritual power of this poetry is so immense that it can awaken true wisdom even in fierce beasts and simple birds. If creatures living entirely by instinct are transformed just by hearing these words, it is completely natural that a human being reading them will also be awakened.

glossary.def: Agamas, traditional scripture governing ritual and temple worship. Vallalar states their ultimate truth is known by direct inner experience of the divine, not merely by reading.
Agaval, a Tamil verse form of long, flowing lines. In this book it names a hymn of the Thiruvasagam, the Thiruvandappaguthi.
Ambalam, the hall or open space. Vallalar uses this term to refer to the supreme spiritual realm where the divine performs the cosmic dance of boundless joy.
Ananda, supreme bliss. Vallalar describes this as the very space and form of the divine, experienced perfectly when the soul unites with God.
Abhirami, a name for the Divine Mother meaning the supremely beautiful one. Vallalar invokes her as his own mother and a source of sweet, life-giving spiritual nourishment.
Appar, the seventh-century Saiva saint also known as Thirunavukkarasar. Vallalar reveres him as the ultimate example of steadfast devotion and pure reliance on divine grace.
Brahma, the traditional creator god. Vallalar frequently points out that even this mighty deity cannot comprehend the supreme grace freely given to an ordinary seeker.
Saivism. The religious tradition dedicated to Siva. Vallalar honors its profound wisdom but teaches that the ultimate divine reality transcends all formal sectarian systems.
Jain rulers or practitioners. Vallalar references the historical persecution of Saint Appar by these rulers to show how divine grace protects true devotees from worldly harm.
Sanmarkkam, the true path. Vallalar's name for his universal spiritual framework based entirely on boundless compassion and direct experience of the divine.
Satguru, the true spiritual teacher. Vallalar applies this title to the divine itself, emphasizing that God actively steps into human confusion to offer direct guidance.
Sadasiva, an exalted deity associated with supreme grace. Vallalar states that even this high cosmic being cannot grasp the ultimate reality that willingly comforts a humble devotee.
Chitrambalam, also known as Chit Sabhai, the hall of divine consciousness. Vallalar identifies this sacred inner space as the arena where God performs the cosmic dance.
Chidambaram, a sacred temple town in South India. Vallalar uses this physical location as a metaphor for the vast inner space of human awareness where the Divine continually acts.
Siddha, an accomplished spiritual master. Vallalar states he achieved this perfected state in the world entirely through divine grace rather than through his own personal effort.
Siddhanta, the established philosophical tradition of Saivism. Vallalar pairs this with Vedanta to demonstrate that the ultimate Reality transcends all formal religious systems.
Sivakama Valli, also known as Sivakami, the feminine divine energy of love and grace. In Vallalar's poetry she represents the inseparable companion to the dancing Lord.
Jeevakarunyam, the active practice of compassion for all living beings. Vallalar insists that receiving God's grace requires a person to engage daily in this selfless service.
Sivam, the state of being entirely permeated by the supreme divine reality. Vallalar describes the ultimate spiritual experience as shedding mortal limitations to become one with this essence.
Siva. The supreme Lord. Vallalar experiences God not as a distant deity, but as an intimate, actively guiding presence who descends to grant grace.
Sivayanama, the sacred mantra of Siva. Vallalar explains that God directly taught him this chant to pull him out of worldly illusions and grant him eternal life.
Jothi, the divine light. Vallalar uses Jothi as the primary form and name for the ultimate reality, an active presence that willingly descends to grant grace to the seeker.
Kalpaka, a mythical heavenly tree that grants all desires. Vallalar uses this as a metaphor for pure saints who freely bestow spiritual blessings upon devoted seekers.
Murder of any living being. Vallalar condemns this action as the absolute barrier to spiritual realization, warning that divine grace remains hidden from those who harm other creatures.
Malai, a garland; here a garland of songs. Each of the twelve works in this book is a mālai.
Vishnu, also referred to as Thirumal or Narayana, the preserver god. Vallalar says that even these supreme gods watch in envy at the direct love the ultimate divine reality shows to a simple devotee.
Manikkavasagar, a highly revered ancient Tamil poet and saint from Vadavur. Vallalar views him as the ultimate spiritual master who successfully transformed his physical body into pure divine bliss.
Maya, illusion or deceptive worldly attachment. Vallalar teaches that divine grace allows the soul to live inside a physical body without being corrupted by its deceptive nature.
Gnanasambandar, also known as Sambandar, a revered seventh-century child saint. Vallalar addresses him with deep affection as a supreme spiritual guide and intimate companion to the soul.
Nandi, the sacred bull mount of Lord Siva. Vallalar contrasts this majestic divine posture in mythology with the extreme humility God shows by walking on tired feet to reach a suffering person.
Nada, primal sound or fundamental spiritual vibration that shapes reality. Vallalar teaches that the inner divine light reveals the secrets of this sacred sound.
Nataraja, the Lord of the cosmic dance. Vallalar uses this traditional image of a dancing God to represent the active, joyous movement of divine grace.
Omkara, the primal cosmic sound Om. Vallalar describes the ultimate divine light as resting deep inside this foundational vibration of the universe.
Pasupati, the Lord and protector of all living souls. Vallalar uses this name to emphasize God's role as a deeply personal guardian who seeks out the lowliest devotee.
Poorani, the complete or all-encompassing Goddess. In Vallalar's verse, she embodies the supreme consciousness and forms the very fabric of the universe.
Tattvas, the fundamental principles of existence. Vallalar refers to thirty-six such principles governing material and mental reality, which the divine helps the soul transcend.
Thevaram, the hymns of Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar to Siva, sung in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
Thillai, the sacred town of Chidambaram where the cosmic dance takes place. It symbolizes the ultimate spiritual space where God dances to grant eternal bliss to all living beings.
Thiruvasagam, Manikkavasagar's book of hymns to Siva, much loved by Vallalar.
Turiya, the transcendent fourth state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. Vallalar locates the divine presence in the very center of this state.
Uma or Umai, representing the divine mother and the active grace of Siva. Vallalar praises her as the bestower of the sacred milk of wisdom that awakens a soul to divine poetry.
Unmani, the highest state of spiritual stillness beyond the mind. Vallalar describes divine grace as existing both within this ultimate inner silence and completely beyond it.
Upanishads, the ancient philosophical texts of India. Vallalar emphasizes that God is the deepest hidden essence of these scriptures, remaining out of reach to all except the spiritually awakened.
Rudrani, the consort of Rudra. Vallalar groups her with other major traditional goddesses who revere the ultimate power of divine grace.
Rudra, the deity responsible for cosmic dissolution. Vallalar uses him to illustrate a hierarchy of traditional gods who remain unable to perceive the ultimate Divine feet.
Vallalar, the nineteenth-century Tamil saint, sage, and author of the Thiru Arutpa, who taught the universal path of boundless compassion and direct experience of the Grace-Light.
Sundarar, traditionally titled Vantondar, an ancient Saiva saint. Vallalar praises him for achieving an incredibly close, personal relationship with the divine.
Vedas, the ancient spiritual scriptures. Vallalar notes that grace bypasses their unreachable, grand status to hand a physical gift directly to the simplest seeker.
Vedanta, the philosophical conclusion of the Vedas. Vallalar views this school of thought as a stepping stone rather than the ultimate destination, describing the Divine as resting far above it.
Karma, the accumulated consequences of past actions. Vallalar emphasizes that direct divine grace has the power to completely erase this burden and instantly purify the soul.
Bindu, the cosmic principle of light or the original seed of creation. Vallalar describes God as the sovereign ruler over this elemental force.
